`README.md`:

```md
# PlasmaTrack

Job tracker for Euro Truck Simulator 2 and American Truck Simulator. A game plugin
records telemetry, a background client uploads it, and the server rebuilds each job
and scores it, with anti-cheat checks done server-side. ETS2 and ATS jobs are kept
fully separate.

Status: beta (client 0.2.6).

## How it fits together

1. The plugin (a DLL loaded by the game) streams telemetry to the client over TCP on loopback.
2. The client keeps a local SQLite log and uploads raw chunks to the server.
3. The server, on Cloudflare Workers, replays each player's chunks through the shared
   timeline and rules, stores the scored jobs, and serves them to the Discord bot through
   the public and admin APIs.

The client and the server use the same Rust core (`pt-core`), so a job is scored the
same way wherever it is replayed.

## Layout

| Path | What |
|------|------|
| `plugin/` | C++ telemetry plugin (Windows x64 DLL, also a native Linux `.so`) |
| `crates/pt-core/` | Shared core: units, config, timeline reconstruction, scoring rules |
| `crates/pt-client/` | Background client: receives telemetry, keeps the local log, uploads, self-updates |
| `crates/pt-server/` | Server logic: ingest, scoring, public and admin APIs, webhooks (tested natively) |
| `crates/pt-worker/` | Cloudflare Workers binding for `pt-server` (D1, R2, Queues, Durable Object, Cron) |
| `crates/pt-replay/` | Replays captures and fixtures through the timeline and rules |
| `installer/` | Electron setup program that installs the plugin and client |
| `config/plasmatrack.sample.toml` | Every threshold, with units in the key names |
| `scripts/` | Build, release and server-seeding helpers |
| `third_party/` | SCS Telemetry SDK 1.14 and TruckersMP client SDK headers, unmodified, plus toolchain notices |
| `docs/` | Design plan, API references, build, install and server guides |

## Build

Rust workspace (needs a stable toolchain from https://rustup.rs and a C compiler for SQLite):

    cargo test --workspace

The plugin, the Windows toolchain and the installer have their own steps in
[`docs/BUILD.md`](docs/BUILD.md). Deploying the server is covered in
[`docs/SERVER.md`](docs/SERVER.md), and publishing a client release in
[`docs/UPDATES.md`](docs/UPDATES.md).

## Docs

- [`docs/INSTALL.md`](docs/INSTALL.md): installing the plugin and client
- [`docs/CLIENT.md`](docs/CLIENT.md): what the client does on a player's machine
- [`docs/PUBLIC_API.md`](docs/PUBLIC_API.md) and [`docs/ADMIN_API.md`](docs/ADMIN_API.md): the API the Discord bot uses
- [`docs/WEBHOOKS.md`](docs/WEBHOOKS.md): events the server sends to the bot
- [`docs/PLAN.md`](docs/PLAN.md): the original design plan

## License

PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0: reuse and modification allowed, no commercial use. See
`LICENSE.md` and `NOTICE`. Third-party components keep their own licenses (see
`THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`).

```

`config/plasmatrack.sample.toml`:

```toml
# PlasmaTrack sample configuration.
#
# Every threshold carries its unit in the key name:
#   _mph, _mi, _km, _l (litres), _l_per_s, _s (seconds of paused simulation
#   time unless noted), _wall_s (wall-clock seconds), _min_game (in-game minutes),
#   _hz, _frames.
# Distances are qualified: _world_ = physical 1:1 distance (odometer / local.scale,
# what points use); _game_ = the game's own scale (odometer, job list, map);
# _world_m = metres of the 3D world (positions).
#
# Unit conversions are fixed by the spec and are NOT configurable:
#   1 km = 0.621371 mi, mph = m/s x 2.23694 (see crates/pt-core/src/units.rs).
#
# Copy to config/plasmatrack.toml (git-ignored). Only [local] may differ per
# driver; everything else must match a server-published config version.
# Values marked PROVISIONAL must be calibrated from real game captures.

config_version = 1

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Scoring rules (server is authoritative; client uses the same values for its
# provisional result). Rule numbers match the spec's precedence table.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[rules]
# Rule 3: loaded WORLD distance (physical 1:1, PLAN §6) strictly
# greater than this is held for review.
manual_review_over_world_km = 150.0
# A whole job averaging more than this many 1:1 km per real minute is held for
# review: 5 = 300 km/h (2026-10-14). Time is unpaused simulation time, so
# pausing cannot lower the average; distance is odometer / local.scale, so
# ferries, trains and teleports add nothing. Jobs with less driving than
# average_pace_min_driving_s are not averaged.
review_over_average_world_km_per_min = 5.0
average_pace_min_driving_s = 60.0
# In tandem: the same check timed by the game's own clock. In-game minutes are
# turned back into real minutes at the game's time rate (local.scale in
# singleplayer; on TruckersMP one in-game minute is 10 real seconds, you,
# 2026-10-14), then 1:1 km per minute is compared (5 = 300 km/h). Sleeping,
# ferries and cargo loading skip game time, which only lowers this average.
review_over_average_world_km_per_game_clock_min = 5.0
truckersmp_game_min_per_real_min = 6.0
average_pace_min_game_min = 20.0
# A delivery paying more than this per mile of the game's delivery distance
# (the game's currency: USD in ATS, EUR in ETS2) is held for review (you,
# 2026-10-16). Real jobs pay about 70-140 a mile; a road trip about 290.
review_over_income_per_game_mi = 400.0
# The same for the whole delivery's income. A very long job or a future game
# version can pass it honestly, so it only sends the job to review.
review_over_income = 500000.0
# Rule 5: accepted distance = driven distance x this factor when penalized.
speed_penalty_factor = 0.85
# Rule 6: points per accepted WORLD mile (physical 1:1 distance = odometer /
# local.scale, PLAN §6).
points_per_world_mi = 1.0
# The job total is floored once, at the end, to this many decimals
# (3.79 -> 3.7 with 1). Never rounds up.
points_decimals = 1

[rules.speed]
# "Over X" means strictly over X for longer than this window (single-sample
# spikes never count). Measured in paused simulation time, so pausing the game
# neither adds time to nor splits an episode.
sustained_window_s = 3.0
# Speeds are compared after rounding to this precision, so a sample of exactly
# 105.0 mph is not "over 105".
compare_precision_mph = 0.001

[rules.speed.ats]
penalty_over_mph = 105.0   # rule 5
invalid_over_mph = 125.0   # rule 2

# Road trips (car_job: a car or pickup) drive faster than trucks (you, 2026-10-16).
[rules.speed.ats.road_trip]
penalty_over_mph = 155.0
invalid_over_mph = 200.0

[rules.speed.ets2]
penalty_over_mph = 100.0   # rule 5
invalid_over_mph = 150.0   # rule 2

[rules.distance]
# Distances are compared after rounding to this precision (150.0 km is not
# "over 150"; 150.1 km is). Distance thresholds are in km, so this is in km too.
compare_precision_km = 0.001
# Odometer comparisons use max(4 x ulp(odometer), this value), because the SDK
# odometer channel is a 32-bit float in km (scssdk_telemetry_truck_common_channels.h:640-645).
odometer_epsilon_km = 0.005
# The game's job.delivered distance.km is in GAME scale (measured on two clean
# deliveries: 71 vs 71.47 km and 1233 vs 1232.14 km) and includes the empty drive
# to the pickup. It is compared with the tracker's whole-job odometer distance
# (accept -> delivery, kept timeline); if they differ by more than the
# GREATER of these two (pct is relative to the larger figure), the job goes to
# manual review. The scored 1:1 distance is (distance.km - uncounted legs) x the
# job's driven world/game ratio (PLAN §6). PROVISIONAL: two clean deliveries.
delivered_vs_trace_tolerance_pct = 1.0
delivered_vs_trace_tolerance_min_mi = 30.0
# All measured on the SDK-reported delivery distance (job.delivered distance.km,
# game scale, in miles): the job length for the short-job test, the floor and
# the percentage.
# Jobs shorter than short_job_under_mi are hard-capped at short_job_max_pct.
delivered_vs_trace_short_job_under_mi = 100.0
delivered_vs_trace_short_job_max_pct = 5.0
# distance.km is reported in whole km, so the comparison always allows 1 km on
# top of the tolerance (a 1 km quick job tracked 1.8 km, 2026-10-13).
delivered_distance_resolution_km = 1.0

[rules.fuel]
# Rule 4: job fuel used below -tolerance is flagged (float noise stays silent).
negative_fuel_tolerance_l = 0.5
# A fuel increase within one tracked run larger than this, outside a detected
# refuel episode, is stored as a "mid-job fuel jump" with its timestamp.
mid_job_jump_tolerance_l = 0.5

[rules.refuel]
# The SDK has no refuel event (scssdk_telemetry_common_gameplay_events.h), so a
# refuel is inferred from the fuel channel. PROVISIONAL.
stationary_below_mph = 1.0
min_duration_s = 1.0
min_rate_l_per_s = 0.5
max_rate_l_per_s = 200.0

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Review policy. Every flag in PlasmaTrack means MANUAL REVIEW: the job is
# pending and its points are held until an admin approves or rejects it
# (via the Discord bot). This includes rule 4 (negative fuel).
#   "review" = send to manual review
#   "off"    = not raised
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[review_policy]
gap = "review"          # forward load / untracked stretch inside a job
late_start = "review"   # job first seen mid-job; distance comes from job.delivered distance.km
trace_checks = "review" # trace-measured mismatches: sample timing, seq gaps, hello vs data (§6a)
# Gaps smaller than BOTH of these are ignored (e.g. a brief socket hiccup).
min_gap_distance_mi = 0.1
min_gap_duration_s = 5.0

# Extra heuristics: manual review only (never invalidation), OFF by default.
[review_flags]
odometer_jump = false
impossible_delivery_time = false

[review_flags.params]
# Average speeds are world distance over simulated time (what the speedometer
# shows); odometer over real time would read up to 20x too fast.
odometer_jump_min_km = 1.0
min_plausible_avg_speed_mph = 0.0
max_plausible_avg_speed_mph = 150.0

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Save-load / timeline detection. ALL PROVISIONAL until capture-calibrated.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[timeline]
# A load is a world reload (job and truck configs emptied in one bracket), or a
# session change plus a discontinuity against the last kept state (PLAN §5).
# A pause bracket alone is never evidence. game.time is used in singleplayer
# only (TruckersMP runs a server-side clock).
game_time_decrease_min_game = 1
bracket_min_live_frames_after_started_frames = 30
bracket_wall_cap_wall_s = 600.0
gameplay_event_explain_window_wall_s = 2.0
ferry_train_explain_window_wall_s = 10.0
# A position jump of at least this many world metres (truck.world.placement;
# game distance = world metres x local.scale) with no load is a teleport (F7,
# ferry, train, quick travel). A teleport only adds no distance: it never
# invalidates, penalises or sends a job to review (decided 2026-09-28).
teleport_min_distance_world_m = 500.0
# Loaded state must match a previously observed point within these tolerances
# to count as "the same point" (for truncation or for restoring a reverted run).
# Position is in world metres (x local.scale for game distance).
match_position_tolerance_world_m = 50.0
match_fuel_tolerance_l = 1.0
match_game_time_tolerance_min_game = 2
# Jobs that finished (or were abandoned) longer ago than this leave the live
# timeline when a new session starts; they are already stored. A save from such
# a job loaded later starts a new late-start job (manual review). Bounds memory
# on the server and in the client (PLAN §7a). Measured on frame wall-clock time.
reopen_window_wall_h = 48.0

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Route map scale classes (PLAN §8). Each stretch of a route is coloured by the
# local.scale it was driven at: 1 = one_to_one (1:1 mod), these vanilla values =
# city / road, anything else = nonstandard (modded). Display only: scale never
# sends a job to review by itself. A game can have several road scales; the
# first is the main one. Measured: ATS 3 / 20 (2026-09-28); ETS2 3 / 19, and 15
# on UK roads (2026-10-13; the UK is "currently" 1:15 per the maintainer, so
# re-check after UK map updates).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[map.scale.ats]
city_local_scale = 3.0
road_local_scales = [20.0]

[map.scale.ets2]
city_local_scale = 3.0
road_local_scales = [19.0, 15.0]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Player notifications (desktop notification from the client).
# Sent for: a delivery marked Invalid (rule 2) and the moment the speed
# penalty (rule 5) activates. Each is delayed by a uniformly random time in
# [delay_min_wall_s, delay_max_wall_s] with microsecond resolution.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[notifications]
enabled = true
delay_min_wall_s = 5.0
delay_max_wall_s = 30.0

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Multiplayer. All multiplayer is tracked (TruckersMP, other MP mods, Convoy).
# Convoy is detected from multiplayer.time.offset != 0 while no TruckersMP module
# is loaded (TruckersMP reports an offset too, observed 2026-09-28)
# (common/scssdk_telemetry_common_channels.h:287-300). The SDK cannot identify
# TruckersMP, so the plugin reports whether any of these module file names is
# loaded in the game process. PROVISIONAL: empty until confirmed by capture.
# Users with the "Singleplayer Division" flag have TruckersMP jobs discarded.
# Other multiplayer mods are listed under [[multiplayer.mods]], each with the
# module names that identify it; a job on one has multiplayer.kind = its kind,
# and singleplayer_division_discard decides whether the Singleplayer Division
# discards it too.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[multiplayer]
# Confirmed: core_atsmp.dll (ATS, 2026-09-28) and core_ets2mp.dll (ETS2,
# 2026-10-13). Only a fallback: the TruckersMP SDK messages decide (PLAN §6b).
truckersmp_module_names = ["core_atsmp.dll", "core_ets2mp.dll"]

# HaulMP (ETS2), captured 2026-10-22: its launcher injects haulmp_stub.dll and
# arms its own telemetry plugin haulmp-telemetry.dll. Its game clock runs at
# local.scale and multiplayer.time.offset stays 0, so without these names a
# HaulMP job looks like singleplayer.
[[multiplayer.mods]]
kind = "haulmp"
name = "HaulMP"
module_names = ["haulmp_stub.dll", "haulmp-telemetry.dll"]
singleplayer_division_discard = true

# TrucklineMP (ETS2 and ATS), seen 2026-10-23: its launcher injects
# trucklineets.dll into ETS2 and trucklineats.dll into ATS (both names are in
# its injector, gamehelper.exe). multiplayer.time.offset stays 0, but the
# server keeps the game clock at one game minute per 9.00 real seconds
# whatever local.scale (it pulls the game's own steps back by a minute).
# PROVISIONAL: measured on one ETS2 session.
[[multiplayer.mods]]
kind = "trucklinemp"
name = "TrucklineMP"
module_names = ["trucklineets.dll", "trucklineats.dll"]
game_min_per_real_min = 6.667
singleplayer_division_discard = true

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Plugin <-> client transport (localhost only).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[plugin]
sample_rate_hz = 20.0
# Frames kept in memory for a reconnecting client (samples only; gameplay and
# config events are journaled to disk until the client acknowledges them).
replay_buffer_wall_s = 120.0

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Client -> server sync.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[sync]
# Failed uploads are retried at this fixed interval, forever, until they succeed.
retry_interval_wall_s = 20.0

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Per-driver settings. This is the ONLY section excluded from the integrity
# check: every other key must match a config version published by the server,
# or the job is discarded (rule 0).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[local]
listen_address = "127.0.0.1"
port = 30455
server_url = "https://plasmatrack.example.invalid"
# Local status page of the client: http://127.0.0.1:<status_port>/
status_port = 30456
# Player token issued by the server (via the Discord bot). Keep this file private.
token = ""

```

`crates/pt-client/src/bin/clientw.rs`:

```rs
//! `plasmatrack-clientw`: the same commands as `plasmatrack-client`, without a
//! console window on Windows. The installer starts `plasmatrack-clientw run` at
//! login; log lines go to `client.log` in the data directory.

#![windows_subsystem = "windows"]

fn main() -> std::process::ExitCode {
    pt_client::cli::main(true)
}

```

`crates/pt-client/src/bin/uninstall.rs`:

```rs
//! `plasmatrack-uninstall` (published as `PlasmaTrack-Uninstall.exe`): removes
//! PlasmaTrack from this PC; see [`pt_client::uninstall`]. Anyone may download
//! it, and Windows starts it from "Installed apps".

#![windows_subsystem = "windows"]

fn main() -> std::process::ExitCode {
    pt_client::uninstall::gui_main()
}

```

`crates/pt-client/src/cli.rs`:

```rs
//! Command line shared by `plasmatrack-client` (console) and
//! `plasmatrack-clientw` (Windows, no console window; started at login by the
//! installer, logging to `client.log` in the data directory, with a tray icon).
//!
//!   run              [--config PATH] [--data-dir PATH]   a second `run` finds the first
//!                                      and (windowless) opens its status page
//!   stop             [--config PATH]   ask a running client to quit
//!   init-config      [--config PATH]
//!   status           [--config PATH] [--data-dir PATH]
//!   find-games       [--json]
//!   write-ini        [--config PATH]
//!   install-plugin   --plugin PATH [--config PATH]   copy the plugin into every game found
//!   uninstall-plugin                                 remove it (and plasmatrack.ini) again
//!   set-local        [--config PATH]   reads {"server_url": .., "token": ..} (both optional)
//!                                      as JSON on stdin, so the token never shows up
//!                                      in a process list; writes the config this build
//!                                      ships, keeping the existing [local] values
//!   show-local       [--config PATH]   [local] as JSON, with the token only as set/unset
//!   check-update     [--config PATH] [--data-dir PATH]   ask the server, download and
//!                                      verify a newer release without installing it
//!   uninstall        [--delete-data] [--json] [--config PATH] [--data-dir PATH]
//!                                      remove PlasmaTrack (what PlasmaTrack-Uninstall.exe does)
//!   register         [--bin PATH]      add PlasmaTrack to Windows' "Installed apps"
//!   apply-update     --bin PATH [--from VERSION] [--config PATH] [--data-dir PATH]
//!                                      run by the updater from the staged release
//!                                      (docs/UPDATES.md); installs it into PATH

use std::io::Read;
use std::net::{IpAddr, SocketAddr};
use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::process::ExitCode;
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex, OnceLock};
use std::time::Duration;

use pt_core::Config;
use tokio::sync::Notify;

use crate::db::Db;
use crate::status::{SharedStatus, Status};
use crate::uploader::UploaderConfig;
use crate::live::{self, Alert, LiveJobs};
use crate::{gamelog, listener, log, manifest, paths, setup, status, steam, updater, uploader};

/// Log file of the windowless client, in the data directory.
pub const LOG_FILE: &str = "client.log";
const LOG_ROTATE_BYTES: u64 = 8 << 20;

struct Args {
    command: String,
    config: PathBuf,
    data_dir: PathBuf,
    json: bool,
    plugin: Option<PathBuf>,
    bin: Option<PathBuf>,
    from: Option<String>,
    delete_data: bool,
}

fn parse_args() -> Result<Args, String> {
    let mut it = std::env::args().skip(1);
    let command = it.next().unwrap_or_else(|| "run".into());
    let mut args = Args {
        command,
        config: paths::default_config_path(),
        data_dir: paths::default_data_dir(),
        json: false,
        plugin: None,
        bin: None,
        from: None,
        delete_data: false,
    };
    while let Some(a) = it.next() {
        match a.as_str() {
            "--config" => args.config = it.next().ok_or("--config needs a path")?.into(),
            "--data-dir" => args.data_dir = it.next().ok_or("--data-dir needs a path")?.into(),
            "--plugin" => args.plugin = Some(it.next().ok_or("--plugin needs a path")?.into()),
            "--bin" => args.bin = Some(it.next().ok_or("--bin needs a path")?.into()),
            "--from" => args.from = Some(it.next().ok_or("--from needs a version")?),
            "--json" => args.json = true,
            "--delete-data" => args.delete_data = true,
            other => return Err(format!("unknown argument {other:?}")),
        }
    }
    Ok(args)
}

fn load_config(path: &PathBuf) -> Result<Config, String> {
    let text = std::fs::read_to_string(path)
        .map_err(|e| format!("cannot read {}: {e} (run `plasmatrack-client init-config`)", path.display()))?;
    Config::from_toml_str(&text).map_err(|e| format!("{}: {e}", path.display()))
}

pub fn managed_ini(cfg: &Config) -> Vec<(&'static str, String)> {
    vec![
        ("port", cfg.local.port.to_string()),
        ("sample_rate_hz", cfg.plugin.sample_rate_hz.to_string()),
        ("replay_buffer_s", cfg.plugin.replay_buffer_wall_s.to_string()),
    ]
}

fn write_inis(cfg: &Config, installs: &[steam::GameInstall]) {
    for i in installs {
        if !i.plugin_path().is_file() {
            continue; // only where the plugin is installed
        }
        match steam::write_ini(&i.plugins_dir, &managed_ini(cfg)) {
            Ok(true) => log!("updated {}", i.plugins_dir.join(steam::INI_FILE).display()),
            Ok(false) => {}
            Err(e) => log!("cannot write ini in {}: {e}", i.plugins_dir.display()),
        }
    }
}

/// Links `run` with whoever started it (the tray): a shutdown request, and the
/// live state once the client is up.
#[derive(Clone, Default)]
pub struct Hooks {
    pub shutdown: Arc<Notify>,
    pub live: Arc<OnceLock<Live>>,
    /// Shows a desktop notification (title, text); the tray sets it.
    pub notify: Arc<OnceLock<NotifyFn>>,
    /// Keep this client up to date (the windowless client run from the
    /// installed `bin` folder; docs/UPDATES.md).
    pub auto_update: bool,
}

pub type NotifyFn = Box<dyn Fn(&str, &str) + Send + Sync>;

pub struct Live {
    pub status: SharedStatus,
    pub db: Arc<Mutex<Db>>,
    pub status_url: String,
}

enum RunError {
    /// Another client already listens; its status page.
    AlreadyRunning(String),
    Failed(String),
}

impl From<String> for RunError {
    fn from(e: String) -> Self {
        RunError::Failed(e)
    }
}

fn status_url(cfg: &Config) -> String {
    format!("http://{}:{}/", cfg.local.listen_address, cfg.local.status_port)
}

fn local_http() -> Option<reqwest::Client> {
    reqwest::Client::builder().no_proxy().timeout(Duration::from_secs(2)).build().ok()
}

/// True when a PlasmaTrack client answers on the status page.
async fn client_answers(status_url: &str) -> bool {
    let Some(http) = local_http() else { return false };
    let Ok(res) = http.get(format!("{status_url}status.json")).send().await else { return false };
    if !res.status().is_success() {
        return false;
    }
    let body = res.text().await.unwrap_or_default();
    serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(&body).is_ok_and(|v| v.get("client_version").is_some())
}

async fn run(args: Args, hooks: Hooks) -> Result<(), RunError> {
    let cfg = load_config(&args.config)?;
    let url = status_url(&cfg);
    let ip: IpAddr = cfg.local.listen_address.parse().map_err(|e| format!("listen_address: {e}"))?;
    let plugin_listener = match tokio::net::TcpListener::bind(SocketAddr::new(ip, cfg.local.port)).await {
        Ok(l) => l,
        Err(_) if client_answers(&url).await => return Err(RunError::AlreadyRunning(url)),
        Err(e) => return Err(format!("cannot listen on {ip}:{} (port in use?): {e}", cfg.local.port).into()),
    };
    std::fs::create_dir_all(&args.data_dir).map_err(|e| format!("{}: {e}", args.data_dir.display()))?;
    let db = Db::open(&args.data_dir.join(paths::DB_FILE)).map_err(|e| format!("database: {e}"))?;
    let db = Arc::new(Mutex::new(db));

    let installs = steam::discover();
    for i in &installs {
        log!("found {:?} plugins folder {} (plugin installed: {})", i.game, i.plugins_dir.display(), i.plugin_path().is_file());
    }
    write_inis(&cfg, &installs);
    let exe = std::env::current_exe().ok();
    let manifest = manifest::compute(exe.as_deref(), Some(&args.config), &installs);

    let status = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Status {
        client_version: crate::CLIENT_VERSION.into(),
        config_hash: cfg.integrity_hash(),
        manifest_files: manifest.len(),
        ..Default::default()
    }));
    let manifest = Arc::new(Mutex::new(manifest));

    // Provisional results and alerts (PLAN §6b), rebuilt from what is stored.
    let live_jobs = Arc::new(Mutex::new(LiveJobs::new(cfg.clone())));
    let (alert_tx, alert_rx) = tokio::sync::mpsc::unbounded_channel();
    let since = crate::now_ms() - (cfg.timeline.reopen_window_wall_h * 3_600_000.0) as i64;
    let feed = live::spawn_worker(live_jobs.clone(), db.clone(), since, alert_tx);
    tokio::spawn(show_alerts(alert_rx, cfg.clone(), hooks.notify.clone()));
    let libraries = steam::library_folders(&steam::steam_roots());
    tokio::spawn(gamelog::watch(db.clone(), Some(feed.clone()), libraries));

    log!("waiting for the plugin on {ip}:{}", cfg.local.port);
    tokio::spawn(listener::serve(plugin_listener, db.clone(), status.clone(), Some(feed)));

    let status_addr = SocketAddr::new(ip, cfg.local.status_port);
    {
        let (status, db, shutdown, jobs) = (status.clone(), db.clone(), hooks.shutdown.clone(), live_jobs.clone());
        tokio::spawn(async move {
            if let Err(e) = status::serve(status_addr, status, db, shutdown, Some(jobs)).await {
                log!("status page unavailable: {e}");
            }
        });
    }
    log!("status page: http://{status_addr}/");

    let ucfg = UploaderConfig {
        server_url: cfg.local.server_url.clone(),
        token: cfg.local.token.clone(),
        retry_interval: Duration::from_secs_f64(cfg.sync.retry_interval_wall_s),
        idle_poll: Duration::from_secs(2),
        batch_interval: Duration::from_secs(10),
        max_frames: 5000,
        max_bytes: 4 << 20,
        multiplayer: cfg.multiplayer.clone(),
        config_hash: cfg.integrity_hash(),
        config_canonical_json: cfg.integrity_canonical_json(),
    };
    if !ucfg.is_configured() {
        log!("uploads paused until [local] server_url and token are set; everything is kept locally");
    }
    let can_update = ucfg.is_configured();
    tokio::spawn(uploader::run(ucfg, db.clone(), status.clone(), manifest.clone()));
    // The live view reads back the reopen window; a day more stays on the PC.
    let keep_ms = ((cfg.timeline.reopen_window_wall_h + 24.0) * 3_600_000.0) as i64;
    tokio::spawn(maintenance_loop(db.clone(), status.clone(), keep_ms));
    if let (true, Some(bin)) = (hooks.auto_update, updater::installed_bin(&args.data_dir)) {
        if !can_update {
            log!("updates paused until [local] server_url and token are set");
        } else {
            let u = UpdateLoop { cfg: cfg.clone(), args: args.clone_paths(), bin, exe: exe.clone() };
            tokio::spawn(update_loop(u, status.clone(), manifest.clone(), hooks.shutdown.clone(), hooks.notify.clone()));
        }
    }
    let _ = hooks.live.set(Live { status, db, status_url: url });

    // Ctrl+C (console), POST /quit (`stop`, installer) or the tray's Quit.
    // Without a console, ctrl_c() may fail; then only the other two apply.
    let ctrl_c = async {
        if tokio::signal::ctrl_c().await.is_err() {
            std::future::pending::<()>().await;
        }
    };
    tokio::select! {
        _ = ctrl_c => {}
        _ = hooks.shutdown.notified() => {}
    }
    log!("shutting down");
    Ok(())
}

struct UpdateLoop {
    cfg: Config,
    args: Args,
    bin: PathBuf,
    exe: Option<PathBuf>,
}

impl Args {
    fn clone_paths(&self) -> Args {
Args {
            command: String::new(),
            config: self.config.clone(),
            data_dir: self.data_dir.clone(),
            json: false,
            plugin: None,
            bin: None,
            from: None,
            delete_data: false,
        }
    }
}

const FIRST_CHECK: Duration = Duration::from_secs(60);
const CHECK_EVERY: Duration = Duration::from_secs(6 * 3600);
const CHECK_AFTER_ERROR: Duration = Duration::from_secs(3600);
const UPDATE_TICK: Duration = Duration::from_secs(60);

fn http_for_updates() -> Result<reqwest::Client, String> {
    reqwest::Client::builder()
        .timeout(Duration::from_secs(600))
        .user_agent(format!("plasmatrack-client/{}", crate::CLIENT_VERSION))
        .build()
        .map_err(|e| e.to_string())
}

/// Starts a program of the client without a window, detached from this one.
fn launch(exe: &std::path::Path, args: &[&std::ffi::OsStr]) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    let mut c = std::process::Command::new(exe);
    c.args(args).stdin(std::process::Stdio::null()).stdout(std::process::Stdio::null()).stderr(std::process::Stdio::null());
    #[cfg(windows)]
    {
        use std::os::windows::process::CommandExt;
        const DETACHED_PROCESS: u32 = 0x0000_0008;
        const CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP: u32 = 0x0000_0200;
        c.creation_flags(DETACHED_PROCESS | CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP);
    }
    c.spawn().map(|_| ())
}

fn path_args(args: &Args) -> [&std::ffi::OsStr; 4] {
    ["--config".as_ref(), args.config.as_os_str(), "--data-dir".as_ref(), args.data_dir.as_os_str()]
}

/// Every hour while no game runs (from two minutes after start): deletes the
/// uploaded sessions older than `keep_ms` (the server keeps them) and gives
/// the space back; the first, full vacuum of an older file can take a while.
async fn maintenance_loop(db: Arc<Mutex<Db>>, status: SharedStatus, keep_ms: i64) {
    tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_secs(120)).await;
    loop {
        let connected = status.lock().map(|s| s.plugin_connections > 0).unwrap_or(true);
        let quiet = !connected && !tokio::task::spawn_blocking(updater::games_running).await.unwrap_or(true);
        // A first cleanup can take a while with the database locked: never
        // while a game is recording.
        if !quiet {
            tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_secs(600)).await;
            continue;
        }
        let db2 = db.clone();
        let done = tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || -> rusqlite::Result<(usize, usize, i64, bool)> {
            let mut db = db2.lock().expect("db");
            let (sessions, frames) = db.prune(crate::now_ms() - keep_ms)?;
            let free = db.free_bytes()?;
            let reclaimed = free >= 64 << 20 && db.reclaim(true)?;
            Ok((sessions, frames, free, reclaimed))
        })
        .await;
        match done {
            Ok(Ok((sessions, frames, free, reclaimed))) if sessions > 0 || reclaimed => log!(
                "removed {sessions} uploaded session(s) ({frames} frames) older than {} h; {} MB {}",
                keep_ms / 3_600_000,
                free >> 20,
                if reclaimed { "given back to the disk" } else { "free inside the file" }
            ),
            Ok(Err(e)) => log!("cleaning the local data failed: {e}"),
            _ => {}
        }
        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_secs(3600)).await;
    }
}

/// Checks for updates, downloads them and, once no game runs, hands over to
/// `apply-update` and quits. Also keeps the games' plugin in step with `bin`.
async fn update_loop(u: UpdateLoop, status: SharedStatus, manifest: Arc<Mutex<Vec<pt_core::upload::ManifestEntry>>>, shutdown: Arc<Notify>, notify: Arc<OnceLock<NotifyFn>>) {
    let keys = pt_core::update::UPDATE_KEYS;
    let data_dir = u.args.data_dir.clone();
    let updates_dir = data_dir.join(updater::UPDATES_DIR);
    let Ok(http) = http_for_updates() else { return };
    let ini = managed_ini(&u.cfg);
    tokio::time::sleep(FIRST_CHECK).await;
    if let Some(o) = updater::read_outcome(&data_dir.join(updater::UPDATED_FILE)) {
        let _ = std::fs::remove_file(data_dir.join(updater::UPDATED_FILE));
        let text = format!("Updated from {} to {}.", o.from, o.version);
        log!("{text}");
        if let Some(show) = notify.get() {
            show("PlasmaTrack updated", &text);
        }
    }
    updater::clean(&updates_dir, crate::CLIENT_VERSION);
    let mut next_check = tokio::time::Instant::now();
    loop {
        let (bin, ini2) = (u.bin.clone(), ini.clone());
        let synced = tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || updater::sync_plugins(&bin, &ini2)).await.unwrap_or_default();
        if synced.iter().any(|r| r.changed) {
            let installs = steam::discover();
            *manifest.lock().expect("manifest") = manifest::compute(u.exe.as_deref(), Some(&u.args.config), &installs);
        }
        let (dir, current) = (updates_dir.clone(), crate::CLIENT_VERSION);
        let ready = tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || updater::staged(&dir, current, keys)).await.ok().flatten();
        if let Some((dir, m)) = ready {
            let failed = updater::failed_recently(&data_dir, &m.version, crate::now_ms());
            let connected = status.lock().map(|s| s.plugin_connections > 0).unwrap_or(true);
            let note = match &failed {
                Some(e) => format!("PlasmaTrack {} could not be installed ({e}); trying again later", m.version),
                None => format!("PlasmaTrack {} is ready and installs once ETS2 and ATS are closed", m.version),
            };
            if let Ok(mut s) = status.lock() {
                s.update = Some(note);
            }
            if failed.is_none() && !connected && !tokio::task::spawn_blocking(updater::games_running).await.unwrap_or(true) {
                let exe = dir.join("plasmatrack-clientw.exe");
                let mut a: Vec<&std::ffi::OsStr> = vec!["apply-update".as_ref(), "--bin".as_ref(), u.bin.as_os_str(), "--from".as_ref(), current.as_ref()];
                a.extend(path_args(&u.args));
                match launch(&exe, &a) {
                    Ok(()) => {
                        log!("installing PlasmaTrack {}; this client quits", m.version);
                        shutdown.notify_one();
                        return;
                    }
                    Err(e) => log!("cannot start {}: {e}", exe.display()),
                }
            }
        } else if tokio::time::Instant::now() >= next_check {
            next_check = tokio::time::Instant::now() + CHECK_EVERY;
            match updater::fetch_offer(&http, &u.cfg.local.server_url, &u.cfg.local.token, crate::CLIENT_VERSION, keys).await {
                Ok(None) => {}
                Ok(Some(offer)) => {
                    log!("downloading PlasmaTrack {}", offer.manifest.version);
                    if let Ok(mut s) = status.lock() {
                        s.update = Some(format!("Downloading PlasmaTrack {}", offer.manifest.version));
                    }
                    if let Err(e) = updater::stage(&http, &u.cfg.local.server_url, &u.cfg.local.token, &offer, &updates_dir).await {
                        log!("update download failed: {e}");
                        next_check = tokio::time::Instant::now() + CHECK_AFTER_ERROR;
                    }
                }
                Err(e) => {
                    log!("{e}");
                    next_check = tokio::time::Instant::now() + CHECK_AFTER_ERROR;
                }
            }
        }
        tokio::time::sleep(UPDATE_TICK).await;
    }
}

/// `apply-update`, run from the staged release (docs/UPDATES.md): waits for
/// the old client to quit, swaps `bin`, rebases the config, updates the
/// plugin and starts the new client. Anything that fails puts the old version
/// back and starts it again.
fn apply_update(args: &Args) -> Result<(), String> {
    let staged = std::env::current_exe().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?.parent().ok_or("no folder")?.to_path_buf();
    let bin = args.bin.clone().ok_or("apply-update needs --bin PATH")?;
    let from = args.from.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| "an older version".into());
    let m = updater::verify_staged(&staged, pt_core::update::UPDATE_KEYS)?;
    log!("apply-update: installing {} from {} into {}", m.version, staged.display(), bin.display());
    let rt = tokio::runtime::Runtime::new().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    let url = load_config(&args.config).map(|c| status_url(&c)).unwrap_or_else(|_| "http://127.0.0.1:30456/".into());
    let start = |dir: &std::path::Path| {
        let mut a: Vec<&std::ffi::OsStr> = vec!["run".as_ref()];
        a.extend(path_args(args));
        launch(&dir.join("plasmatrack-clientw.exe"), &a)
    };
    let fail = |e: String| -> Result<(), String> {
        log!("apply-update: {e}");
        updater::write_outcome(&args.data_dir.join(updater::FAILED_FILE), &updater::Outcome {
            version: m.version.clone(), from: from.clone(), at_ms: crate::now_ms(), error: Some(e.clone()),
        });
        let _ = start(&bin);
        Err(e)
    };
    let gone = rt.block_on(async {
        for _ in 0..300 {
            if !client_answers(&url).await {
                return true;
            }
            tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(100)).await;
        }
        false
    });
    if !gone {
        return fail("the running client did not quit".into());
    }
    if updater::games_running() {
        return fail("a game was started".into());
    }
    let old = match updater::swap_bin(&staged, &m, &bin) {
        Ok(old) => old,
        Err(e) => return fail(e),
    };
    // The config this release ships, with the player's [local] values.
    let old_config = std::fs::read_to_string(&args.config).ok();
    let rebased = setup::rebase_config(old_config.as_deref(), paths::SAMPLE_CONFIG).and_then(|text| {
        setup::write_atomically(&args.config, &text).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        Config::from_toml_str(&text).map_err(|e| e.to_string())
    });
    let ini = rebased.as_ref().map(managed_ini).unwrap_or_default();
    updater::sync_plugins(&bin, &ini);
    if let Err(e) = crate::uninstall::register(&bin, &m.version) {
        log!("apply-update: Installed apps entry: {e}");
    }
    let done = updater::Outcome { version: m.version.clone(), from: from.clone(), at_ms: crate::now_ms(), error: None };
    updater::write_outcome(&args.data_dir.join(updater::UPDATED_FILE), &done);
    let started = start(&bin).is_ok()
        && rt.block_on(async {
            for _ in 0..60 {
                tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(500)).await;
                if client_answers(&url).await {
                    return true;
                }
            }
            false
        });
    if started && rebased.is_ok() {
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&old);
        let _ = std::fs::remove_file(args.data_dir.join(updater::FAILED_FILE));
        log!("apply-update: PlasmaTrack {} is running", m.version);
        return Ok(());
    }
    // Back to the old version: its bin, its config, its plugin.
    let why = match rebased {
        Err(e) => format!("config: {e}"),
        Ok(_) => "the new client did not start".into(),
    };
    let _ = std::fs::remove_file(args.data_dir.join(updater::UPDATED_FILE));
    let _ = rt.block_on(async {
        let http = local_http()?;
        http.post(format!("{url}quit")).header(status::QUIT_HEADER.0, status::QUIT_HEADER.1).send().await.ok()
    });
    std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_secs(2));
    if let Err(e) = updater::restore_bin(&bin, &old) {
        log!("apply-update: {e}");
    }
    if let Some(text) = old_config {
        let _ = setup::write_atomically(&args.config, &text);
    }
    let old_ini = load_config(&args.config).map(|c| managed_ini(&c)).unwrap_or(ini);
    updater::sync_plugins(&bin, &old_ini);
    fail(why)
}

/// `uninstall`: removes PlasmaTrack, printing each step (as JSON with
/// `--json`, for Setup). Fails when any step failed.
fn uninstall(args: &Args) -> Result<(), String> {
    let p = crate::uninstall::Paths { config: args.config.clone(), data_dir: args.data_dir.clone() };
    let steps = crate::uninstall::uninstall(&p, args.delete_data);
    if args.json {
        print_json(&serde_json::json!({ "steps": steps }));
    } else {
        for s in &steps {
            println!("{} {}{}", if s.ok { "ok  " } else { "FAIL" }, s.text, s.detail.as_ref().map(|d| format!(" ({d})")).unwrap_or_default());
        }
    }
    match steps.iter().filter(|s| !s.ok).count() {
        0 => Ok(()),
        n => Err(format!("{n} step(s) failed")),
    }
}

/// `check-update`: what the updater would download, verified, without
/// installing it. Prints the result as JSON.
fn check_update(args: &Args) -> Result<(), String> {
    let cfg = load_config(&args.config)?;
    let rt = tokio::runtime::Runtime::new().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    let http = http_for_updates()?;
    let keys = pt_core::update::UPDATE_KEYS;
    let offer = rt.block_on(updater::fetch_offer(&http, &cfg.local.server_url, &cfg.local.token, crate::CLIENT_VERSION, keys))?;
    let Some(offer) = offer else {
        print_json(&serde_json::json!({"current": crate::CLIENT_VERSION, "update": null}));
        return Ok(());
    };
    let dir = rt.block_on(updater::stage(&http, &cfg.local.server_url, &cfg.local.token, &offer, &args.data_dir.join(updater::UPDATES_DIR)))?;
    let m = updater::verify_staged(&dir, keys)?;
    print_json(&serde_json::json!({"current": crate::CLIENT_VERSION, "update": m.version, "staged": dir, "files": m.files.len()}));
    Ok(())
}

/// Shows each alert after its random delay (PLAN decision 10), as a desktop
/// notification where there is a tray, and always in the log.
async fn show_alerts(mut rx: tokio::sync::mpsc::UnboundedReceiver<Alert>, cfg: Config, notify: Arc<OnceLock<NotifyFn>>) {
    while let Some(alert) = rx.recv().await {
        if !cfg.notifications.enabled {
            continue;
        }
        let delay = live::alert_delay(&cfg);
        let (cfg, notify) = (cfg.clone(), notify.clone());
        tokio::spawn(async move {
            tokio::time::sleep(delay).await;
            let (title, text) = alert.message(&cfg);
            log!("{title}: {text}");
            if let Some(show) = notify.get() {
                show(&title, &text);
            }
        });
    }
}

/// Tooltip and tray menu lines: game connection, then uploads.
pub fn status_lines(s: &Status, pending: Option<u64>) -> Vec<String> {
    let game = match s.last_game.as_deref() {
        Some("eut2") => "ETS2",
        Some("ats") => "ATS",
        _ => "the game",
    };
    let connection =
        if s.plugin_connections > 0 { format!("Connected to {game}") } else { "Waiting for ETS2 or ATS".to_string() };
    let failing = s.last_upload_error.is_some() && s.last_upload_ok_ms < s.last_upload_attempt_ms;
    let upload = match pending {
        _ if !s.upload_configured => Some("Uploads paused: no token".to_string()),
        _ if failing => Some("Upload failing, retrying".to_string()),
        Some(0) => Some("Everything uploaded".to_string()),
        Some(n) => Some(format!("{n} frames waiting to upload")),
        None => None,
    };
    std::iter::once(connection).chain(upload).collect()
}

/// `run` for plasmatrack-clientw on Windows: a tray icon while the client runs
/// on a worker thread; errors as a dialog, since there is no console.
#[cfg(windows)]
fn run_windowless(args: Args) -> Result<(), String> {
    use crate::tray;

    let cfg = match load_config(&args.config) {
        Ok(c) => c,
        Err(e) => {
            tray::error_box(&format!("PlasmaTrack could not start.\n\n{e}\n\nRun PlasmaTrack Setup to set it up."));
            return Err(e);
        }
    };
    let rt = tokio::runtime::Runtime::new().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    let url = status_url(&cfg);
    if rt.block_on(client_answers(&url)) {
        log!("already running; opening {url}");
        tray::open(&url);
        return Ok(());
    }

    let hooks = Hooks { auto_update: true, ..Hooks::default() };
    let (live, live2, shutdown) = (hooks.live.clone(), hooks.live.clone(), hooks.shutdown.clone());
    let data_dir = args.data_dir.clone();
    let cb = tray::Callbacks {
        title: format!("PlasmaTrack {}", crate::CLIENT_VERSION),
        lines: Box::new(move || match live.get() {
            Some(l) => {
                let status = l.status.lock().map(|s| s.clone()).unwrap_or_default();
                let pending = l.db.try_lock().ok().and_then(|db| db.stats().ok()).map(|s| s.frames_pending_upload);
                status_lines(&status, pending)
            }
            None => vec!["Starting…".to_string()],
        }),
        open_status: Box::new(move || {
            if let Some(l) = live2.get() {
                tray::open(&l.status_url);
            }
        }),
        open_data: Box::new(move || tray::open(&data_dir.to_string_lossy())),
        quit: Box::new(move || shutdown.notify_one()),
    };
    tray::run(cb, move |exit| {
        let notifier = exit.notifier();
        let _ = hooks.notify.set(Box::new(move |title: &str, text: &str| notifier.show(title, text)));
        std::thread::spawn(move || {
            match rt.block_on(run(args, hooks)) {
                Ok(()) => {}
                Err(RunError::AlreadyRunning(url)) => tray::open(&url),
                Err(RunError::Failed(e)) => {
                    log!("error: {e}");
                    tray::error_box(&format!("PlasmaTrack stopped.\n\n{e}"));
                }
            }
            exit.post();
        });
    })
}

#[cfg(not(windows))]
fn run_windowless(args: Args) -> Result<(), String> {
    run_console(args)
}

fn run_console(args: Args) -> Result<(), String> {
    let rt = tokio::runtime::Runtime::new().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    match rt.block_on(run(args, Hooks::default())) {
        Ok(()) => Ok(()),
        Err(RunError::AlreadyRunning(url)) => {
            println!("PlasmaTrack is already running; status page: {url}");
            Ok(())
        }
        Err(RunError::Failed(e)) => Err(e),
    }
}

/// Asks a running client to quit and waits until it has.
fn stop(args: &Args) -> Result<(), String> {
    let cfg = load_config(&args.config)?;
    let url = status_url(&cfg);
    let rt = tokio::runtime::Runtime::new().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    rt.block_on(async {
        let http = local_http().ok_or("http client")?;
        let sent = http.post(format!("{url}quit")).header(status::QUIT_HEADER.0, status::QUIT_HEADER.1).send().await;
        match sent {
            Err(_) => {
                println!("not running");
                return Ok(());
            }
            Ok(r) if !r.status().is_success() => return Err(format!("quit refused: {}", r.status())),
            Ok(_) => {}
        }
        for _ in 0..50 {
            if !client_answers(&url).await {
                println!("stopped");
                return Ok(());
            }
            tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(100)).await;
        }
        Err("the client did not stop within 5 s".to_string())
    })
}

fn print_json<T: serde::Serialize>(v: &T) {
    println!("{}", serde_json::to_string_pretty(v).unwrap_or_default());
}

/// Fails when any folder failed, after printing every result.
fn report(results: Vec<setup::FolderResult>) -> Result<(), String> {
    let failed = results.iter().filter(|r| r.error.is_some()).count();
    print_json(&results);
    match failed {
        0 => Ok(()),
        n => Err(format!("{n} game folder(s) failed")),
    }
}

#[derive(serde::Deserialize)]
struct LocalInput {
    server_url: Option<String>,
    token: Option<String>,
}

fn set_local(args: &Args) -> Result<(), String> {
    let mut input = String::new();
    std::io::stdin().read_to_string(&mut input).map_err(|e| format!("stdin: {e}"))?;
    let input: LocalInput = serde_json::from_str(&input).map_err(|e| format!("stdin JSON: {e}"))?;
    let existing = match std::fs::read_to_string(&args.config) {
        Ok(t) => Some(t),
        Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => None,
        Err(e) => return Err(format!("{}: {e}", args.config.display())),
    };
    // Always the config this build ships, with the player's [local] kept.
    let rebased = setup::rebase_config(existing.as_deref(), paths::SAMPLE_CONFIG)?;
    let text = setup::set_local(&rebased, input.server_url.as_deref(), input.token.as_deref())?;
    setup::write_atomically(&args.config, &text).map_err(|e| format!("{}: {e}", args.config.display()))?;
    println!("wrote {}", args.config.display());
    Ok(())
}

fn show_local(args: &Args) -> Result<(), String> {
    let exists = args.config.is_file();
    let cfg = if exists { load_config(&args.config)? } else { Config::from_toml_str(paths::SAMPLE_CONFIG).map_err(|e| e.to_string())? };
    print_json(&serde_json::json!({
        "config_path": args.config,
        "config_exists": exists,
        "server_url": cfg.local.server_url,
        "token_set": !cfg.local.token.trim().is_empty(),
        "status_url": format!("http://{}:{}/", cfg.local.listen_address, cfg.local.status_port),
    }));
    Ok(())
}

fn install_plugin(args: &Args) -> Result<(), String> {
    let plugin = args.plugin.as_ref().ok_or("install-plugin needs --plugin PATH")?;
    if !plugin.is_file() {
        return Err(format!("{} not found", plugin.display()));
    }
    let cfg = load_config(&args.config)?;
    let installs = steam::discover();
    if installs.is_empty() {
        return Err("no ETS2 or ATS install found in any Steam library".into());
    }
    report(setup::install_plugin(&installs, plugin, &managed_ini(&cfg)))
}

/// Sends `log!` lines to `client.log` in the data directory, keeping one older
/// file once it grows past a few MiB.
fn log_to_file(data_dir: &std::path::Path) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    std::fs::create_dir_all(data_dir)?;
    let path = data_dir.join(LOG_FILE);
    if std::fs::metadata(&path).is_ok_and(|m| m.len() > LOG_ROTATE_BYTES) {
        let _ = std::fs::rename(&path, data_dir.join(format!("{LOG_FILE}.old")));
    }
    crate::set_log_file(std::fs::OpenOptions::new().create(true).append(true).open(path)?);
    Ok(())
}

/// Entry point of both binaries. `windowless`: log to the data directory's
/// `client.log`, since there is no console to write to.
pub fn main(windowless: bool) -> ExitCode {
    let args = match parse_args() {
        Ok(a) => a,
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("{e}");
            return ExitCode::from(2);
        }
    };
    if windowless {
        if let Err(e) = log_to_file(&args.data_dir) {
            eprintln!("cannot open {}: {e}", args.data_dir.join(LOG_FILE).display());
        }
    }
    let result = match args.command.as_str() {
        "run" if windowless => run_windowless(args),
        "run" => run_console(args),
        "stop" => stop(&args),
        "init-config" => {
            if args.config.exists() {
                Err(format!("{} already exists", args.config.display()))
            } else {
                std::fs::create_dir_all(args.config.parent().unwrap_or(&PathBuf::from(".")))
                    .and_then(|_| std::fs::write(&args.config, paths::SAMPLE_CONFIG))
                    .map(|_| println!("wrote {}", args.config.display()))
                    .map_err(|e| e.to_string())
            }
        }
        "status" => Db::open(&args.data_dir.join(paths::DB_FILE))
            .and_then(|db| db.stats())
            .map(|s| print_json(&s))
            .map_err(|e| e.to_string()),
        "find-games" => {
            let installs = steam::discover();
            if args.json {
                let rows: Vec<_> = installs
                    .iter()
                    .map(|i| {
                        serde_json::json!({
                            "game": i.game,
                            "plugins_dir": i.plugins_dir,
                            "windows_build": i.windows_build,
                            "plugin_installed": i.plugin_path().is_file(),
                        })
                    })
                    .collect();
                print_json(&rows);
            } else {
                for i in installs {
                    println!("{:?}\t{}\tplugin installed: {}", i.game, i.plugins_dir.display(), i.plugin_path().is_file());
                }
            }
            Ok(())
        }
        "write-ini" => load_config(&args.config).map(|cfg| write_inis(&cfg, &steam::discover())),
        "install-plugin" => install_plugin(&args),
        "uninstall-plugin" => report(setup::uninstall_plugin(&steam::discover())),
        "set-local" => set_local(&args),
        "show-local" => show_local(&args),
        "check-update" => check_update(&args),
        "uninstall" => uninstall(&args),
        "register" => {
            let bin = args.bin.clone().or_else(|| std::env::current_exe().ok().and_then(|e| e.parent().map(PathBuf::from)));
            bin.ok_or_else(|| "register needs --bin PATH".to_string()).and_then(|b| crate::uninstall::register(&b, crate::CLIENT_VERSION))
        }
        "apply-update" => apply_update(&args),
        other => Err(format!("unknown command {other:?}")),
    };
    match result {
        Ok(()) => ExitCode::SUCCESS,
        Err(e) => {
            if windowless {
                log!("error: {e}");
            }
            eprintln!("error: {e}");
            ExitCode::FAILURE
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn status_lines_describe_game_and_uploads() {
        let mut s = Status::default();
        assert_eq!(status_lines(&s, Some(3)), ["Waiting for ETS2 or ATS", "Uploads paused: no token"]);
        s.upload_configured = true;
        s.plugin_connections = 1;
        s.last_game = Some("eut2".into());
        assert_eq!(status_lines(&s, Some(0)), ["Connected to ETS2", "Everything uploaded"]);
        assert_eq!(status_lines(&s, Some(12)), ["Connected to ETS2", "12 frames waiting to upload"]);
        assert_eq!(status_lines(&s, None), ["Connected to ETS2"]);
        s.last_upload_attempt_ms = Some(20);
        s.last_upload_ok_ms = Some(10);
        s.last_upload_error = Some("503".into());
        assert_eq!(status_lines(&s, Some(12))[1], "Upload failing, retrying");
        s.last_upload_ok_ms = Some(20);
        assert_eq!(status_lines(&s, Some(0))[1], "Everything uploaded");
    }
}

```

`crates/pt-client/src/db.rs`:

```rs
//! The client's local SQLite log. Frames are stored verbatim, keyed by
//! (session, seq), so replays from the plugin are idempotent. A frame is only
//! acknowledged to the plugin after the transaction holding it has committed
//! (`synchronous=FULL`), so an acknowledged frame survives a crash of the client.

use std::collections::BTreeMap;
use std::path::Path;

use pt_core::wire::Envelope;
use rusqlite::{params, Connection, OptionalExtension};

pub type Result<T> = rusqlite::Result<T>;

/// A frame received from the plugin, already parsed for its envelope.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Incoming {
    pub env: Envelope,
    pub raw: String,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct PendingChunk {
    pub sess: String,
    pub seq_from: u64,
    pub seq_to: u64,
    pub frames: Vec<String>,
    pub hello: Option<String>,
    /// Client notes placed among `frames`; marked uploaded with the chunk.
    pub note_ids: Vec<i64>,
    /// When the oldest of these frames arrived (the client's clock).
    pub oldest_ms: i64,
    /// It reached `max_frames` or `max_bytes`: more is waiting.
    pub full: bool,
    /// It carries a game event (a delivery, a cancellation), which is sent at once.
    pub urgent: bool,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize)]
pub struct DbStats {
    pub sessions: u64,
    pub frames: u64,
    pub frames_pending_upload: u64,
    pub snapshots: u64,
}

pub struct Db {
    conn: Connection,
}

const SCHEMA: &str = "
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sessions (
    sess          TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    first_seen_ms INTEGER NOT NULL,
    last_seen_ms  INTEGER NOT NULL,
    game_id       TEXT,
    hello         TEXT
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS frames (
    sess        TEXT    NOT NULL,
    seq         INTEGER NOT NULL,
    kind        TEXT    NOT NULL,
    json        TEXT    NOT NULL,
    received_ms INTEGER NOT NULL,
    uploaded    INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    PRIMARY KEY (sess, seq)
) WITHOUT ROWID;
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS frames_pending ON frames (uploaded, sess, seq);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS snapshots (
    id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    sess        TEXT    NOT NULL,
    received_ms INTEGER NOT NULL,
    json        TEXT    NOT NULL
);
-- Client-inserted frames (profile changes, PLAN §6b). They carry no plugin seq;
-- each belongs right after plugin frame `after_seq` of its session.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS notes (
    id        INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    sess      TEXT    NOT NULL,
    after_seq INTEGER NOT NULL,
    json      TEXT    NOT NULL,
    uploaded  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    added_ms  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS notes_pending ON notes (uploaded, sess, after_seq);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS uploads (
    id       INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    at_ms    INTEGER NOT NULL,
    sess     TEXT    NOT NULL,
    seq_from INTEGER NOT NULL,
    seq_to   INTEGER NOT NULL,
    ok       INTEGER NOT NULL,
    detail   TEXT    NOT NULL
);
";

impl Db {
    pub fn open(path: &Path) -> Result<Db> {
        let conn = Connection::open(path)?;
        conn.pragma_update(None, "journal_mode", "WAL")?;
        conn.pragma_update(None, "synchronous", "FULL")?;
        Self::init(conn)
    }

    pub fn open_in_memory() -> Result<Db> {
        Self::init(Connection::open_in_memory()?)
    }

    fn init(conn: Connection) -> Result<Db> {
        // Takes effect on a new file only; an older one switches in `reclaim`.
        conn.pragma_update(None, "auto_vacuum", "INCREMENTAL")?;
        conn.execute_batch(SCHEMA)?;
        Ok(Db { conn })
    }

    /// Deletes the sessions last seen before `cutoff_ms` whose frames and
    /// notes are all uploaded: the server has them (owner, 2026-10-16: the
    /// file had grown to 2.4 GB). Returns (sessions, frames) deleted.
    pub fn prune(&mut self, cutoff_ms: i64) -> Result<(usize, usize)> {
        let tx = self.conn.transaction()?;
        let sessions: Vec<String> = {
            let mut st = tx.prepare(
                "SELECT s.sess FROM sessions s WHERE s.last_seen_ms < ?1
                   AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM frames f WHERE f.uploaded = 0 AND f.sess = s.sess)
                   AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM notes n WHERE n.uploaded = 0 AND n.sess = s.sess)",
            )?;
            let rows = st.query_map(params![cutoff_ms], |r| r.get(0))?;
            rows.collect::<Result<_>>()?
        };
        let mut frames = 0;
        for s in &sessions {
            frames += tx.execute("DELETE FROM frames WHERE sess = ?1", params![s])?;
            tx.execute("DELETE FROM notes WHERE sess = ?1", params![s])?;
            tx.execute("DELETE FROM snapshots WHERE sess = ?1", params![s])?;
            tx.execute("DELETE FROM sessions WHERE sess = ?1", params![s])?;
        }
        tx.execute("DELETE FROM uploads WHERE at_ms < ?1", params![cutoff_ms])?;
        tx.commit()?;
        Ok((sessions.len(), frames))
    }

    /// Bytes of free pages inside the file.
    pub fn free_bytes(&self) -> Result<i64> {
        let pages: i64 = self.conn.query_row("PRAGMA freelist_count", [], |r| r.get(0))?;
        let size: i64 = self.conn.query_row("PRAGMA page_size", [], |r| r.get(0))?;
        Ok(pages * size)
    }

    /// Gives free pages back to the disk. A file made before 0.2.3 first needs a
    /// full VACUUM, which locks it for a while: only when `allow_full` (no game
    /// running). After that the file vacuums incrementally, which is quick.
    /// Returns whether space was given back.
    pub fn reclaim(&mut self, allow_full: bool) -> Result<bool> {
        let mode: i64 = self.conn.query_row("PRAGMA auto_vacuum", [], |r| r.get(0))?;
        if mode == 2 {
            self.conn.execute_batch("PRAGMA incremental_vacuum;")?;
        } else if allow_full {
            self.conn.execute_batch("PRAGMA auto_vacuum = INCREMENTAL; VACUUM;")?;
        } else {
            return Ok(false);
        }
        self.conn.query_row("PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)", [], |_| Ok(()))?;
        Ok(true)
    }

    /// Persists a batch in one transaction and returns, per session, the highest
    /// seq now stored. The caller acknowledges exactly those to the plugin.
    pub fn store(&mut self, batch: &[Incoming], now_ms: i64) -> Result<BTreeMap<String, u64>> {
        self.store_fresh(batch, now_ms).map(|(acks, _)| acks)
    }

    /// [`Db::store`], plus the indices of the frames that were new (a plugin
    /// replays unacknowledged frames after a reconnect).
    pub fn store_fresh(&mut self, batch: &[Incoming], now_ms: i64) -> Result<(BTreeMap<String, u64>, Vec<usize>)> {
        let mut acks: BTreeMap<String, u64> = BTreeMap::new();
        let mut fresh = Vec::new();
        let tx = self.conn.transaction()?;
        {
            let mut touch = tx.prepare_cached(
                "INSERT INTO sessions (sess, first_seen_ms, last_seen_ms) VALUES (?1, ?2, ?2)
                 ON CONFLICT(sess) DO UPDATE SET last_seen_ms = excluded.last_seen_ms",
            )?;
            let mut frame = tx.prepare_cached(
                "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO frames (sess, seq, kind, json, received_ms) VALUES (?1, ?2, ?3, ?4, ?5)",
            )?;
            for (i, m) in batch.iter().enumerate() {
                let env = &m.env;
                touch.execute(params![env.sess, now_ms])?;
                match (env.kind.as_str(), env.seq) {
                    ("hello", _) => {
                        tx.execute("UPDATE sessions SET hello = ?2 WHERE sess = ?1", params![env.sess, m.raw])?;
                    }
                    ("snapshot", _) => {
                        tx.execute(
                            "INSERT INTO snapshots (sess, received_ms, json) VALUES (?1, ?2, ?3)",
                            params![env.sess, now_ms, m.raw],
                        )?;
                    }
                    (kind, Some(seq)) => {
                        if frame.execute(params![env.sess, seq as i64, kind, m.raw, now_ms])? == 1 {
                            fresh.push(i);
                        }
                        if kind == "init" {
                            if let Some(game) = serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(&m.raw)
                                .ok()
                                .and_then(|v| v.get("game_id").and_then(|g| g.as_str()).map(str::to_owned))
                            {
                                tx.execute("UPDATE sessions SET game_id = ?2 WHERE sess = ?1", params![env.sess, game])?;
                            }
                        }
                        let e = acks.entry(env.sess.clone()).or_insert(0);
                        *e = (*e).max(seq);
                    }
                    (_, None) => {} // unknown seq-less kind: nothing to persist
                }
            }
        }
        tx.commit()?;
        Ok((acks, fresh))
    }

    /// Sessions that still have frames to upload, oldest first.
    pub fn pending_sessions(&self) -> Result<Vec<String>> {
        let mut st = self.conn.prepare(
            "SELECT s.sess FROM sessions s
             WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM frames f WHERE f.uploaded = 0 AND f.sess = s.sess)
             ORDER BY s.first_seen_ms, s.sess",
        )?;
        let rows = st.query_map([], |r| r.get(0))?;
        rows.collect()
    }

    /// The next run of unuploaded frames of `sess`, in seq order, bounded by
    /// `max_frames` and (approximately) `max_bytes`.
    pub fn next_chunk(&self, sess: &str, max_frames: usize, max_bytes: usize) -> Result<Option<PendingChunk>> {
        let mut st = self.conn.prepare_cached(
            "SELECT seq, json, kind, received_ms FROM frames WHERE sess = ?1 AND uploaded = 0 ORDER BY seq LIMIT ?2",
        )?;
        let mut rows = st.query(params![sess, max_frames as i64])?;
        let mut plugin: Vec<(u64, String)> = Vec::new();
        let mut bytes = 0usize;
        let (mut oldest_ms, mut urgent, mut full) = (i64::MAX, false, false);
        while let Some(r) = rows.next()? {
            let seq: i64 = r.get(0)?;
            let json: String = r.get(1)?;
            if !plugin.is_empty() && bytes + json.len() > max_bytes {
                full = true;
                break;
            }
            bytes += json.len();
            urgent |= r.get::<_, String>(2)? == "gameplay";
            oldest_ms = oldest_ms.min(r.get(3)?);
            plugin.push((seq as u64, json));
        }
        full |= plugin.len() >= max_frames;
        let (Some(&(from, _)), Some(&(to, _))) = (plugin.first(), plugin.last()) else {
            return Ok(None);
        };
        // Notes go right after the frame they followed (or, when that frame was
        // dropped by the plugin or already uploaded, before the next one).
        let mut st = self.conn.prepare_cached(
            "SELECT id, after_seq, json FROM notes WHERE sess = ?1 AND uploaded = 0 AND after_seq <= ?2 ORDER BY after_seq, id",
        )?;
        let notes: Vec<(i64, u64, String)> = st
            .query_map(params![sess, to as i64], |r| Ok((r.get(0)?, r.get::<_, i64>(1)? as u64, r.get(2)?)))?
            .collect::<Result<_>>()?;
        let mut frames = Vec::with_capacity(plugin.len() + notes.len());
        let mut note_ids = Vec::with_capacity(notes.len());
        let mut pending_notes = notes.into_iter().peekable();
        for (seq, json) in plugin {
            while let Some((id, _, note)) = pending_notes.next_if(|n| n.1 < seq) {
                note_ids.push(id);
                frames.push(note);
            }
            frames.push(json);
            while let Some((id, _, note)) = pending_notes.next_if(|n| n.1 == seq) {
                note_ids.push(id);
                frames.push(note);
            }
        }
        let hello: Option<String> = self
            .conn
            .query_row("SELECT hello FROM sessions WHERE sess = ?1", params![sess], |r| r.get(0))
            .optional()?
            .flatten();
        Ok(Some(PendingChunk { sess: sess.to_owned(), seq_from: from, seq_to: to, frames, hello, note_ids, oldest_ms, full, urgent }))
    }

    /// Records a client note (e.g. a profile change) at the current end of
    /// `sess`: it follows the newest plugin frame stored so far. Returns its JSON.
    pub fn add_note(&mut self, sess: &str, mut note: serde_json::Value, now_ms: i64) -> Result<String> {
        let after: i64 =
            self.conn.query_row("SELECT COALESCE(MAX(seq), 0) FROM frames WHERE sess = ?1", params![sess], |r| r.get(0))?;
        note["sess"] = sess.into();
        note["after_seq"] = after.into();
        let json = note.to_string();
        self.conn.execute("INSERT INTO notes (sess, after_seq, json, added_ms) VALUES (?1, ?2, ?3, ?4)", params![sess, after, json, now_ms])?;
        Ok(json)
    }

    pub fn mark_notes_uploaded(&mut self, ids: &[i64]) -> Result<()> {
        let tx = self.conn.transaction()?;
        for id in ids {
            tx.execute("UPDATE notes SET uploaded = 1 WHERE id = ?1", params![id])?;
        }
        tx.commit()
    }

    /// The newest session of a game (`game_id` as the plugin reports it) and when
    /// a frame of it last arrived.
    pub fn latest_session(&self, game_id: &str) -> Result<Option<(String, i64)>> {
        self.conn
            .query_row(
                "SELECT sess, last_seen_ms FROM sessions WHERE game_id = ?1 ORDER BY first_seen_ms DESC, sess DESC LIMIT 1",
                params![game_id],
                |r| Ok((r.get(0)?, r.get(1)?)),
            )
            .optional()
    }

    /// Sessions last seen at or after `since_ms`, oldest first, with their game.
    pub fn sessions_since(&self, since_ms: i64) -> Result<Vec<(String, Option<String>)>> {
        let mut st = self
            .conn
            .prepare("SELECT sess, game_id FROM sessions WHERE last_seen_ms >= ?1 ORDER BY first_seen_ms, sess")?;
        let rows = st.query_map(params![since_ms], |r| Ok((r.get(0)?, r.get(1)?)))?;
        rows.collect()
    }

    /// Every frame and note of `sess` stored before `before_ms`, in stream order
    /// (for rebuilding the live timeline after a restart).
    pub fn session_stream(&self, sess: &str, before_ms: i64) -> Result<Vec<String>> {
        let mut st = self.conn.prepare(
            "SELECT json FROM (
                 SELECT seq AS k, 0 AS n, json FROM frames WHERE sess = ?1 AND received_ms < ?2
                 UNION ALL
                 SELECT after_seq AS k, id AS n, json FROM notes WHERE sess = ?1 AND added_ms < ?2
             ) ORDER BY k, n",
        )?;
        let rows = st.query_map(params![sess, before_ms], |r| r.get(0))?;
        rows.collect()
    }

    /// Marks every frame of `sess` up to `through_seq` as accepted by the server.
    pub fn mark_uploaded(&mut self, sess: &str, through_seq: u64) -> Result<usize> {
        self.conn.execute(
            "UPDATE frames SET uploaded = 1 WHERE sess = ?1 AND seq <= ?2 AND uploaded = 0",
            params![sess, through_seq as i64],
        )
    }

    pub fn record_upload(&mut self, sess: &str, from: u64, to: u64, ok: bool, detail: &str, now_ms: i64) -> Result<()> {
        self.conn.execute(
            "INSERT INTO uploads (at_ms, sess, seq_from, seq_to, ok, detail) VALUES (?1, ?2, ?3, ?4, ?5, ?6)",
            params![now_ms, sess, from as i64, to as i64, ok, detail],
        )?;
        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn stats(&self) -> Result<DbStats> {
        let count = |sql: &str| -> Result<u64> { self.conn.query_row(sql, [], |r| r.get::<_, i64>(0)).map(|v| v as u64) };
        Ok(DbStats {
            sessions: count("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sessions")?,
            frames: count("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM frames")?,
            frames_pending_upload: count("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM frames WHERE uploaded = 0")?,
            snapshots: count("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM snapshots")?,
        })
    }

    pub fn frame_seqs(&self, sess: &str) -> Result<Vec<u64>> {
        let mut st = self.conn.prepare("SELECT seq FROM frames WHERE sess = ?1 ORDER BY seq")?;
        let rows = st.query_map(params![sess], |r| r.get::<_, i64>(0).map(|v| v as u64))?;
        rows.collect()
    }

    pub fn session_game(&self, sess: &str) -> Result<Option<String>> {
        Ok(self
            .conn
            .query_row("SELECT game_id FROM sessions WHERE sess = ?1", params![sess], |r| r.get(0))
            .optional()?
            .flatten())
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    const S1: &str = "11111111111111111111111111111111";
    const S2: &str = "22222222222222222222222222222222";

    fn msg(sess: &str, kind: &str, seq: Option<u64>, extra: &str) -> Incoming {
        let raw = match seq {
            Some(s) => format!("{{\"v\":1,\"kind\":\"{kind}\",\"sess\":\"{sess}\",\"seq\":{s}{extra}}}"),
            None => format!("{{\"v\":1,\"kind\":\"{kind}\",\"sess\":\"{sess}\"{extra}}}"),
        };
        Incoming { env: Envelope::parse(&raw).unwrap(), raw }
    }

    #[test]
    fn prune_deletes_old_uploaded_sessions_only_and_gives_the_space_back() {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let path = dir.path().join("client.sqlite");
        let mut db = Db::open(&path).unwrap();
        // Switch to the pre-0.2.3 layout, as on players' PCs.
        db.conn.execute_batch("PRAGMA auto_vacuum = NONE; VACUUM;").unwrap();
        let pad = format!(",\"pad\":\"{}\"", "x".repeat(2000));
        let old: Vec<Incoming> = (1..=2000).map(|i| msg(S1, "sample", Some(i), &pad)).collect();
        db.store(&old, 1_000).unwrap();
        db.mark_uploaded(S1, 2000).unwrap();
        // An old session not fully uploaded, and a recent one.
        db.store(&[msg(S2, "sample", Some(1), ""), msg(S2, "sample", Some(2), "")], 1_000).unwrap();
        db.mark_uploaded(S2, 1).unwrap();
        db.store(&[msg("33333333333333333333333333333333", "sample", Some(1), "")], 900_000).unwrap();
        db.mark_uploaded("33333333333333333333333333333333", 1).unwrap();

        assert_eq!(db.prune(500_000).unwrap(), (1, 2000));
        assert!(db.frame_seqs(S1).unwrap().is_empty());
        assert_eq!(db.frame_seqs(S2).unwrap(), vec![1, 2], "a frame still to upload keeps its session");
        assert_eq!(db.frame_seqs("33333333333333333333333333333333").unwrap(), vec![1]);

        let before = std::fs::metadata(&path).unwrap().len();
        assert!(db.free_bytes().unwrap() > 3_000_000);
        assert!(!db.reclaim(false).unwrap(), "the first full vacuum waits for a quiet moment");
        assert!(db.reclaim(true).unwrap());
        let after = std::fs::metadata(&path).unwrap().len();
        assert!(after * 4 < before, "{before} -> {after}");
        // From now on it is incremental.
        let mode: i64 = db.conn.query_row("PRAGMA auto_vacuum", [], |r| r.get(0)).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(mode, 2);
        assert!(db.reclaim(false).unwrap());
    }

    #[test]
    fn store_is_idempotent_and_acks_max_seq() {
        let mut db = Db::open_in_memory().unwrap();
        let batch = vec![
            msg(S1, "hello", None, ""),
            msg(S1, "snapshot", None, ",\"paused\":true"),
            msg(S1, "init", Some(1), ",\"game_id\":\"ats\""),
            msg(S1, "sample", Some(2), ""),
            msg(S1, "sample", Some(4), ""), // 3 was dropped by the plugin
        ];
        let acks = db.store(&batch, 10).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(acks.get(S1), Some(&4));
        // Replay after a reconnect: duplicates are ignored, new frames added.
        let acks = db.store(&[msg(S1, "sample", Some(2), ""), msg(S1, "sample", Some(5), "")], 20).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(acks.get(S1), Some(&5));
        assert_eq!(db.frame_seqs(S1).unwrap(), vec![1, 2, 4, 5]);
        assert_eq!(db.session_game(S1).unwrap().as_deref(), Some("ats"));
        let st = db.stats().unwrap();
        assert_eq!((st.sessions, st.frames, st.frames_pending_upload, st.snapshots), (1, 4, 4, 1));
    }

    #[test]
    fn chunks_respect_limits_and_upload_marks() {
        let mut db = Db::open_in_memory().unwrap();
        let mut batch = vec![msg(S1, "hello", None, "")];
        batch.extend((1..=10).map(|i| msg(S1, "sample", Some(i), "")));
        batch.extend((1..=3).map(|i| msg(S2, "config", Some(i), "")));
        db.store(&batch, 1).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(db.pending_sessions().unwrap().len(), 2);

        let c = db.next_chunk(S1, 4, usize::MAX).unwrap().unwrap();
        assert_eq!((c.seq_from, c.seq_to, c.frames.len()), (1, 4, 4));
        assert!(c.hello.is_some());
        let one_frame = c.frames[0].len();
        let c = db.next_chunk(S1, 100, one_frame * 2).unwrap().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(c.frames.len(), 2);

        assert_eq!(db.mark_uploaded(S1, 4).unwrap(), 4);
        let c = db.next_chunk(S1, 100, usize::MAX).unwrap().unwrap();
        assert_eq!((c.seq_from, c.seq_to), (5, 10));
        db.mark_uploaded(S1, 10).unwrap();
        assert!(db.next_chunk(S1, 100, usize::MAX).unwrap().is_none());
        assert_eq!(db.pending_sessions().unwrap(), vec![S2.to_string()]);
        assert!(db.next_chunk(S2, 100, usize::MAX).unwrap().unwrap().hello.is_none());
    }

    #[test]
    fn notes_ride_in_stream_order() {
        let mut db = Db::open_in_memory().unwrap();
        let note = |db: &mut Db, k: &str| db.add_note(S1, serde_json::json!({"v": 1, "kind": "profile", "profile_key": k}), 1).unwrap();
        let first = note(&mut db, "a"); // before any frame
        db.store(&[msg(S1, "init", Some(1), ",\"game_id\":\"ats\""), msg(S1, "sample", Some(2), "")], 1).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(db.latest_session("ats").unwrap(), Some((S1.to_string(), 1)));
        let second = note(&mut db, "b"); // after seq 2
        db.store(&[msg(S1, "sample", Some(4), ""), msg(S1, "sample", Some(5), "")], 2).unwrap();
        assert!(first.contains("\"after_seq\":0") && second.contains("\"after_seq\":2"));

        let c = db.next_chunk(S1, 100, usize::MAX).unwrap().unwrap();
        let kinds: Vec<String> = c
            .frames
            .iter()
            .map(|f| {
                let v: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(f).unwrap();
                format!("{}{}", v["kind"].as_str().unwrap(), v["profile_key"].as_str().unwrap_or(""))
            })
            .collect();
        assert_eq!(kinds, ["profilea", "init", "sample", "profileb", "sample", "sample"]);
        assert_eq!(db.session_stream(S1, i64::MAX).unwrap(), c.frames, "a rebuild sees the same order");
        assert_eq!(db.session_stream(S1, 2).unwrap().len(), 4, "only what was stored before");
        assert_eq!(c.note_ids.len(), 2);

        db.mark_uploaded(S1, c.seq_to).unwrap();
        db.mark_notes_uploaded(&c.note_ids).unwrap();
        let third = note(&mut db, "c"); // after seq 5, already uploaded
        assert!(third.contains("\"after_seq\":5"));
        db.store(&[msg(S1, "sample", Some(6), "")], 3).unwrap();
        let c = db.next_chunk(S1, 100, usize::MAX).unwrap().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(c.frames.len(), 2, "the late note leads the next chunk");
        assert!(c.frames[0].contains("profile_key"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn survives_reopen_from_disk() {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let path = dir.path().join("client.sqlite");
        {
            let mut db = Db::open(&path).unwrap();
            db.store(&[msg(S1, "config", Some(7), "")], 1).unwrap();
        }
        let db = Db::open(&path).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(db.frame_seqs(S1).unwrap(), vec![7]);
    }
}
```
