`crates/pt-client/src/gamelog.rs`:

```rs
//! Profile detection from the game's own log (PLAN §6b). The SDK has no profile
//! identifier, but every world load writes
//!
//! ```text
//! 00:00:36.178 : Loading save. Type: 0, slot: 0, path: <MEMFILE><UFS>/home/profiles/<HEX>/save/autosave/game.sii
//! ```
//!
//! to `Documents/<game>/game.log.txt` (captured in ATS and ETS2, 2026-09-28 and
//! 2026-10-13). `<HEX>` is the profile name in hexadecimal and `home` / `steam`
//! says whether it is a local or a Steam Cloud profile. Only a hash of both
//! leaves this PC; the profile name never does.

use std::fs::File;
use std::io::{Read, Seek, SeekFrom};
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use pt_core::Game;
use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};

pub const LOG_FILE: &str = "game.log.txt";

/// The profile key a `Loading save` line names, if it is one.
pub fn profile_key_from_line(line: &str) -> Option<String> {
    let rest = &line[line.find("Loading save.")?..];
    let path = &rest[rest.find("path:")? + 5..];
    let at = path.find("/profiles/")?;
    let location = path[..at].rsplit('/').next().unwrap_or_default();
    let tail = &path[at + "/profiles/".len()..];
    let hex = &tail[..tail.find('/')?];
    if hex.is_empty() || !hex.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_hexdigit()) {
        return None;
    }
    Some(profile_key(location, hex))
}

/// 16 hex digits of SHA-256 over `"{location}/{HEX}"`: stable per profile,
/// says nothing about its name.
pub fn profile_key(location: &str, hex: &str) -> String {
    let digest = Sha256::digest(format!("{}/{}", location.to_ascii_lowercase(), hex.to_ascii_uppercase()));
    digest.iter().take(8).map(|b| format!("{b:02x}")).collect()
}

/// The game's documents folder name.
pub fn documents_folder(game: Game) -> &'static str {
    match game {
        Game::Ets2 => "Euro Truck Simulator 2",
        Game::Ats => "American Truck Simulator",
    }
}

/// Where each game writes its log: the Windows documents folder, and under
/// Proton the prefix of every Steam library that has the game.
pub fn log_paths(game: Game, steam_libraries: &[PathBuf]) -> Vec<PathBuf> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    if cfg!(windows) {
        if let Some(docs) = dirs::document_dir() {
            out.push(docs.join(documents_folder(game)).join(LOG_FILE));
        }
    } else {
        let app_id = match game {
            Game::Ets2 => "227300",
            Game::Ats => "270880",
        };
        for lib in steam_libraries {
            out.push(
                lib.join("steamapps/compatdata")
                    .join(app_id)
                    .join("pfx/drive_c/users/steamuser/Documents")
                    .join(documents_folder(game))
                    .join(LOG_FILE),
            );
        }
        if let Some(config) = dirs::config_dir() {
            out.extend(tlm_homedirs(game, &config.join("TruckersMP")).into_iter().map(|d| d.join(LOG_FILE)));
        }
    }
    out
}

/// TruckersMP's native Linux launcher (run by TLM, the Steam compatibility tool)
/// starts the game with `-homedir`, which the game mounts as its home: the log,
/// `config.cfg` and `profiles/` sit directly in it, not in a `<game>` subfolder.
/// It is the game's `-homedir` from `launcher-options.json` when the player set
/// one, and the launcher's default `homedir` (shared by both games) either way.
pub fn tlm_homedirs(game: Game, tmp_dir: &Path) -> Vec<PathBuf> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    if let Ok(json) = std::fs::read_to_string(tmp_dir.join("launcher-options.json")) {
        out.extend(homedir_from_launcher_options(&json, game, &tmp_dir.join("protonprefix")));
    }
    out.push(tmp_dir.join("homedir"));
    out
}

/// The `-homedir` argument in the launcher's per-game console options, as a
/// Linux path. Options before a `%command%` entry are environment variables.
pub fn homedir_from_launcher_options(json: &str, game: Game, prefix: &Path) -> Option<PathBuf> {
    let v: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(json).ok()?;
    let key = match game {
        Game::Ets2 => "ets2",
        Game::Ats => "ats",
    };
    let opts = v["games"][key]["consoleOpts"].as_array()?;
    let at = opts.iter().position(|o| o.as_str() == Some("-homedir"))?;
    let raw = opts.get(at + 1)?.as_str()?.trim_matches('"');
    wine_to_unix(raw, prefix)
}

/// A Windows path inside a Wine prefix (`Z:\home\me\x`, `C:\users\steamuser\x`)
/// as a Linux path, through the prefix's own drive table: `dosdevices/z:` links
/// to `/`, `dosdevices/c:` to `../drive_c`, and any other drive to wherever the
/// player mapped it. `None` for paths that are not drive-absolute.
pub fn wine_to_unix(path: &str, prefix: &Path) -> Option<PathBuf> {
    let mut chars = path.chars();
    let drive = chars.next().filter(char::is_ascii_alphabetic)?.to_ascii_lowercase();
    let rest = chars.as_str().strip_prefix(':')?;
    let mut out = prefix.join("dosdevices").join(format!("{drive}:"));
    if drive == 'z' && !out.exists() {
        // Every Wine prefix maps Z: to the filesystem root; this holds before
        // the prefix exists, too.
        out = PathBuf::from("/");
    }
    out.extend(rest.split(['\\', '/']).filter(|p| !p.is_empty()));
    Some(out)
}

/// Follows a log file that the game rewrites at every start. The first line
/// ("log created on : <date>") tells a new log from the old one even when the
/// new one is already longer.
pub struct LogTail {
    path: PathBuf,
    pos: u64,
    partial: Vec<u8>,
    head: Vec<u8>,
    rewrites: u64,
}

const HEAD_BYTES: u64 = 80;

impl LogTail {
    /// Starts at the beginning, so the profile loaded before the client started
    /// is found too.
    pub fn new(path: PathBuf) -> LogTail {
        LogTail { path, pos: 0, partial: Vec::new(), head: Vec::new(), rewrites: 0 }
    }

    /// How often the game has rewritten the log (a new game start) so far.
    pub fn rewrites(&self) -> u64 {
        self.rewrites
    }

    pub fn path(&self) -> &Path {
        &self.path
    }

    /// Complete lines written since the last call.
    pub fn poll(&mut self) -> Vec<String> {
        let Ok(mut f) = File::open(&self.path) else { return Vec::new() };
        let len = f.metadata().map(|m| m.len()).unwrap_or(0);
        let mut head = Vec::new();
        if (&mut f).take(HEAD_BYTES).read_to_end(&mut head).is_err() {
            return Vec::new();
        }
        let same_head = head.starts_with(&self.head[..self.head.len().min(head.len())]);
        if len < self.pos || !same_head {
            // A new game start rewrote the file.
            self.pos = 0;
            self.partial.clear();
            self.rewrites += 1;
        }
        self.head = head;
        if len == self.pos || f.seek(SeekFrom::Start(self.pos)).is_err() {
            return Vec::new();
        }
        let mut buf = Vec::new();
        if f.take(len - self.pos).read_to_end(&mut buf).is_err() {
            return Vec::new();
        }
        self.pos += buf.len() as u64;
        self.partial.extend_from_slice(&buf);
        let mut lines = Vec::new();
        while let Some(i) = self.partial.iter().position(|&b| b == b'\n') {
            let line: Vec<u8> = self.partial.drain(..=i).collect();
            lines.push(String::from_utf8_lossy(&line).trim_end().to_string());
        }
        lines
    }
}

/// How recently a session must have sent a frame to count as running.
const ACTIVE_WALL_MS: i64 = 30_000;

/// Per game: which profile the log names, and the profile note last written.
struct Watched {
    game: Game,
    tails: Vec<LogTail>,
    /// Rewrites already seen, per tail.
    rewrites: Vec<u64>,
    wanted: Option<String>,
    sent: Option<(String, String)>,
}

/// Follows both games' logs and records a `profile` note in the running session
/// of that game whenever a save of a (possibly other) profile is loaded. A note
/// waits until the game's session is running; a fresh log (new game start)
/// forgets the previous profile.
pub async fn watch(
    db: std::sync::Arc<std::sync::Mutex<crate::db::Db>>,
    feed: Option<crate::live::Feed>,
    steam_libraries: Vec<PathBuf>,
) {
    let mut games: Vec<Watched> = [Game::Ets2, Game::Ats]
        .into_iter()
        .map(|game| Watched {
            game,
            tails: log_paths(game, &steam_libraries).into_iter().map(LogTail::new).collect(),
            rewrites: Vec::new(),
            wanted: None,
            sent: None,
        })
        .collect();
    let mut tick = tokio::time::interval(std::time::Duration::from_millis(250));
    tick.set_missed_tick_behavior(tokio::time::MissedTickBehavior::Delay);
    loop {
        tick.tick().await;
        for w in games.iter_mut() {
            w.rewrites.resize(w.tails.len(), 0);
            for (t, seen) in w.tails.iter_mut().zip(w.rewrites.iter_mut()) {
                let lines = t.poll();
                if t.rewrites() != *seen {
                    *seen = t.rewrites();
                    w.wanted = None;
                }
                if let Some(key) = lines.iter().rev().find_map(|l| profile_key_from_line(l)) {
                    w.wanted = Some(key);
                }
            }
            let Some(key) = w.wanted.clone() else { continue };
            let now = crate::now_ms();
            let db2 = db.clone();
            let game_id = w.game.sdk_game_id();
            let sent = w.sent.clone();
            let note = tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || -> rusqlite::Result<Option<(String, String)>> {
                let mut db = db2.lock().expect("db");
                let Some((sess, last_seen)) = db.latest_session(game_id)? else { return Ok(None) };
                if now - last_seen > ACTIVE_WALL_MS || sent.as_ref() == Some(&(sess.clone(), key.clone())) {
                    return Ok(None);
                }
                let json = db.add_note(&sess, serde_json::json!({"v": 1, "kind": "profile", "wall_ms": now, "profile_key": key}), now)?;
                Ok(Some((sess, json)))
            })
            .await;
            match note {
                Ok(Ok(Some((sess, json)))) => {
                    crate::log!("{:?} profile {} in session {sess}", w.game, w.wanted.as_deref().unwrap_or_default());
                    w.sent = Some((sess, w.wanted.clone().unwrap_or_default()));
                    if let Some(f) = &feed {
                        f.send(now, vec![json]);
                    }
                }
                Ok(Ok(None)) => {}
                Ok(Err(e)) => crate::log!("cannot record the profile: {e}"),
                Err(e) => crate::log!("profile task failed: {e}"),
            }
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    const HOME: &str = "00:00:36.178 : Loading save. Type: 0, slot: 0, path: <MEMFILE><UFS>/home/profiles/4E616D65/save/autosave/game.sii";
    const STEAM: &str = "01:07:20.930 : Loading save. Type: 0, slot: 0, path: <MEMFILE><UFS>/steam/profiles/4E616D65/save/autosave/game.sii";

    #[test]
    fn keys_come_from_loading_save_lines_only() {
        let home = profile_key_from_line(HOME).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(home.len(), 16);
        assert_eq!(profile_key_from_line(&HOME.replace("/save/autosave", "/save/461")), Some(home.clone()));
        assert_ne!(profile_key_from_line(STEAM).unwrap(), home, "local and Steam Cloud profiles differ");
        assert_eq!(profile_key_from_line(&HOME.replace("4E616D65", "4e616d65")), Some(home), "hex case does not matter");
        assert_eq!(profile_key_from_line("00:00:15.928 : New profile selected: 'Name'"), None);
        assert_eq!(profile_key_from_line("Loading save. path: /home/profiles/not-hex/save/x"), None);
    }

    #[cfg(unix)]
    #[test]
    fn tlm_homedir_comes_from_console_opts() {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let prefix = dir.path().join("protonprefix");
        std::fs::create_dir_all(prefix.join("dosdevices")).unwrap();
        std::fs::create_dir_all(prefix.join("drive_c")).unwrap();
        std::os::unix::fs::symlink("/", prefix.join("dosdevices/z:")).unwrap();
        std::os::unix::fs::symlink("../drive_c", prefix.join("dosdevices/c:")).unwrap();
        let json = r#"{"games":{
            "ets2":{"game":"ets2","path":"x","consoleOpts":["WINEDLLOVERRIDES=dxgi=n,b","%command%","-homedir","Z:\\home\\me\\.config\\TruckersMP\\homedir\\ets2"]},
            "ats":{"game":"ats","path":"x","consoleOpts":["-homedir","\"C:\\users\\steamuser\\Documents\\ATS\""]}}}"#;
        assert_eq!(
            homedir_from_launcher_options(json, Game::Ets2, &prefix).unwrap(),
            prefix.join("dosdevices/z:").join("home/me/.config/TruckersMP/homedir/ets2"),
        );
        assert_eq!(
            homedir_from_launcher_options(json, Game::Ats, &prefix).unwrap(),
            prefix.join("dosdevices/c:").join("users/steamuser/Documents/ATS"),
            "quotes are stripped and C: goes through the prefix",
        );
        assert_eq!(homedir_from_launcher_options(r#"{"games":{"ets2":{"consoleOpts":[]}}}"#, Game::Ets2, &prefix), None);
        assert_eq!(wine_to_unix(r"Z:\a\b", Path::new("/nonexistent")), Some(PathBuf::from("/a/b")), "Z: is / before the prefix exists");
        assert_eq!(wine_to_unix(r"relative\path", &prefix), None);

        let tmp = dir.path();
        std::fs::write(tmp.join("launcher-options.json"), json).unwrap();
        let dirs = tlm_homedirs(Game::Ats, tmp);
        assert_eq!(dirs.last(), Some(&tmp.join("homedir")), "the launcher default is always a candidate");
        assert_eq!(dirs.len(), 2);
    }

    #[test]
    fn tail_follows_appends_and_rewrites() {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let path = dir.path().join(LOG_FILE);
        std::fs::write(&path, "a\nb").unwrap();
        let mut t = LogTail::new(path.clone());
        assert_eq!(t.poll(), vec!["a"]);
        std::fs::write(&path, "a\nbc\r\nd\n").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(t.poll(), vec!["bc", "d"]);
        assert!(t.poll().is_empty());
        std::fs::write(&path, "new\n").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(t.poll(), vec!["new"], "the game rewrote the log");
        std::fs::write(&path, "NEW\nmuch longer than before\n").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(t.poll(), vec!["NEW", "much longer than before"], "a longer rewrite is noticed too");
    }
}

`crates/pt-client/src/lib.rs`:

```rs
//! PlasmaTrack client library. The `plasmatrack-client` binary wires these parts
//! together; integration tests drive them directly.
//!
//! - [`listener`]: accepts the plugin's connection on 127.0.0.1, persists every
//!   frame to SQLite, then acknowledges it (docs/WIRE.md).
//! - [`db`]: the local SQLite log. The client works fully offline.
//! - [`uploader`]: sends unuploaded raw frames to the server as chunks, retrying
//!   at a fixed interval until the server accepts them.
//! - [`steam`], [`manifest`]: finds game installs, writes `plasmatrack.ini`,
//!   hashes installed files for the integrity check (rule 0).
//! - [`setup`]: installs the plugin and sets `[local]` for the installer.
//! - [`status`]: local status page.
//! - [`cli`]: the command line of both binaries.
//! - `tray` (Windows): the notification-area icon of the windowless client.
//! - [`updater`]: downloads signed releases and installs them (docs/UPDATES.md).
//! - [`uninstall`]: removes PlasmaTrack (`PlasmaTrack-Uninstall.exe`, Setup) and
//!   registers it in Windows' "Installed apps".

pub mod cli;
pub mod db;
pub mod gamelog;
pub mod listener;
pub mod live;
pub mod manifest;
pub mod paths;
pub mod setup;
pub mod status;
pub mod steam;
#[cfg(windows)]
pub mod tray;
pub mod uninstall;
pub mod updater;
pub mod uploader;

use std::sync::{Mutex, OnceLock};

pub const CLIENT_VERSION: &str = env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION");

pub fn now_ms() -> i64 {
    use std::time::{SystemTime, UNIX_EPOCH};
    SystemTime::now().duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH).map(|d| d.as_millis() as i64).unwrap_or(0)
}

static LOG_FILE: OnceLock<Mutex<std::fs::File>> = OnceLock::new();

/// Sends [`log!`] lines to `file` instead of stderr (windowless client).
pub fn set_log_file(file: std::fs::File) {
    let _ = LOG_FILE.set(Mutex::new(file));
}

#[doc(hidden)]
pub fn write_log(line: String) {
    use std::io::Write;
    match LOG_FILE.get() {
        Some(f) => {
            if let Ok(mut f) = f.lock() {
                let _ = writeln!(f, "{line}");
            }
        }
        None => eprintln!("{line}"),
    }
}

/// Timestamped log line on stderr, or in the log file once one is set.
#[macro_export]
macro_rules! log {
    ($($arg:tt)*) => {
        $crate::write_log(format!("[{}] {}", $crate::now_ms(), format!($($arg)*)))
    };
}

`crates/pt-client/src/listener.rs`:

```rs
//! Accepts plugin connections on loopback (the plugin connects out to us) and
//! persists every frame before acknowledging it (docs/WIRE.md).
//!
//! Several connections may be open at once (e.g. ETS2 and ATS running together);
//! each carries its own plugin session.

use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
use std::time::Duration;

use pt_core::wire::{ack_json, encode_frame, Envelope, FrameDecoder};
use tokio::io::{AsyncReadExt, AsyncWriteExt};
use tokio::net::{TcpListener, TcpStream};

use crate::db::{Db, Incoming};
use crate::live::Feed;
use crate::log;
use crate::status::SharedStatus;

/// Frames are committed and acknowledged at least this often, or sooner when a
/// batch reaches [`MAX_BATCH`].
pub const FLUSH_INTERVAL: Duration = Duration::from_millis(200);
pub const MAX_BATCH: usize = 1000;

/// `feed` gets every newly stored frame for the live results.
pub async fn serve(listener: TcpListener, db: Arc<Mutex<Db>>, status: SharedStatus, feed: Option<Feed>) {
    loop {
        match listener.accept().await {
            Ok((stream, peer)) => {
                if !peer.ip().is_loopback() {
                    continue; // bound to loopback anyway; defence in depth
                }
                let db = db.clone();
                let status = status.clone();
                let feed = feed.clone();
                tokio::spawn(async move {
                    status.lock().expect("status").plugin_connections += 1;
                    log!("plugin connected from {peer}");
                    if let Err(e) = handle(stream, db, status.clone(), feed).await {
                        log!("plugin connection error: {e}");
                    }
                    status.lock().expect("status").plugin_connections -= 1;
                    log!("plugin disconnected");
                });
            }
            Err(e) => {
                log!("accept failed: {e}");
                tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(200)).await;
            }
        }
    }
}

async fn flush(
    pending: &mut Vec<Incoming>,
    db: &Arc<Mutex<Db>>,
    status: &SharedStatus,
    feed: &Option<Feed>,
    writer: &mut tokio::net::tcp::OwnedWriteHalf,
) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    if pending.is_empty() {
        return Ok(());
    }
    let batch = std::mem::take(pending);
    let count = batch.len() as u64;
    let last = batch.last().map(|m| (m.env.sess.clone(), m.env.kind.clone()));
    let db = db.clone();
    let now = crate::now_ms();
    let (acks, batch) = tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || {
        let stored = db.lock().expect("db").store_fresh(&batch, now);
        stored.map(|(acks, fresh)| (acks, fresh.into_iter().map(|i| batch[i].raw.clone()).collect::<Vec<_>>()))
    })
    .await
    .map_err(std::io::Error::other)?
    .map_err(std::io::Error::other)?;
    if let Some(feed) = feed {
        feed.send(now, batch);
    }
    // Only after the commit: acknowledge what is now durable.
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for (sess, seq) in &acks {
        out.extend(encode_frame(&ack_json(sess, *seq)));
    }
    writer.write_all(&out).await?;
    let mut st = status.lock().expect("status");
    st.frames_received += count;
    st.acks_sent += acks.len() as u64;
    st.last_frame_ms = Some(crate::now_ms());
    if let Some((sess, _)) = last {
        st.last_session = Some(sess);
    }
    Ok(())
}

async fn handle(stream: TcpStream, db: Arc<Mutex<Db>>, status: SharedStatus, feed: Option<Feed>) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    stream.set_nodelay(true)?;
    let (mut reader, mut writer) = stream.into_split();
    let mut decoder = FrameDecoder::new();
    let mut pending: Vec<Incoming> = Vec::new();
    let mut buf = vec![0u8; 64 * 1024];
    let mut tick = tokio::time::interval(FLUSH_INTERVAL);
    tick.set_missed_tick_behavior(tokio::time::MissedTickBehavior::Delay);

    loop {
        tokio::select! {
            n = reader.read(&mut buf) => {
                let n = n?;
                if n == 0 {
                    break;
                }
                decoder.push(&buf[..n]);
                loop {
                    match decoder.next_frame() {
                        Ok(Some(raw)) => match Envelope::parse(&raw) {
                            Ok(env) => {
                                if env.kind == "init" {
                                    if let Some(g) = serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(&raw).ok()
                                        .and_then(|v| v.get("game_id").and_then(|g| g.as_str()).map(str::to_owned)) {
                                        status.lock().expect("status").last_game = Some(g);
                                    }
                                }
                                pending.push(Incoming { env, raw });
                            }
                            Err(e) => log!("dropping malformed frame: {e}"),
                        },
                        Ok(None) => break,
                        Err(e) => {
                            flush(&mut pending, &db, &status, &feed, &mut writer).await?;
                            return Err(std::io::Error::new(std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidData, e));
                        }
                    }
                }
                if pending.len() >= MAX_BATCH {
                    flush(&mut pending, &db, &status, &feed, &mut writer).await?;
                }
            }
            _ = tick.tick() => {
                flush(&mut pending, &db, &status, &feed, &mut writer).await?;
            }
        }
    }
    // Connection closed: persist what arrived (it will be re-sent by the plugin
    // anyway, because it was never acknowledged).
    let _ = flush(&mut pending, &db, &status, &feed, &mut writer).await;
    Ok(())
}

`crates/pt-client/src/live.rs`:

```rs
//! Provisional results while you drive (PLAN §6b). The client runs the same
//! `pt-core` timeline and rules as the server on the frames it stores, one
//! [`Profiles`] per game, and raises the two player alerts: an Invalid delivery
//! and the moment the speed penalty activates. The server's result is
//! authoritative; nothing computed here is uploaded.

use std::collections::{HashMap, VecDeque};

use pt_core::rules::{evaluate, Context, JobResult, Outcome};
use pt_core::timeline::{Job, JobState, Notice, Profiles, StartKind};
use pt_core::trace::{parse_frame, Body};
use pt_core::{Config, Game};
use serde::Serialize;

/// Finished jobs kept for the status page after they left the live timeline.
const FINISHED_KEPT: usize = 50;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize)]
#[serde(tag = "kind", rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum Alert {
    InvalidDelivery { game: Game, cargo: String, peak_mph: f64 },
    PenaltyActivated { game: Game, cargo: String },
}

impl Alert {
    /// Title and text of the desktop notification.
    pub fn message(&self, cfg: &Config) -> (String, String) {
        match self {
            Alert::InvalidDelivery { game, cargo, peak_mph } => (
                "Invalid delivery".into(),
                format!(
                    "{cargo}: you drove over {} mph (peak {peak_mph:.0} mph), so this delivery scores no points. \
                     Moderators can still approve it.",
                    cfg.rules.speed.limits(*game).invalid_over_mph
                ),
            ),
            Alert::PenaltyActivated { game, cargo } => (
                "Speed penalty".into(),
                format!(
                    "{cargo}: you drove over {} mph for too long. This job's distance now counts at {}×.",
                    cfg.rules.speed.limits(*game).penalty_over_mph,
                    cfg.rules.speed_penalty_factor
                ),
            ),
        }
    }
}

/// One job as the status page shows it.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize)]
pub struct JobView {
    pub game: Game,
    pub profile: String,
    pub cargo: String,
    pub source_city: String,
    pub destination_city: String,
    pub state: JobState,
    pub start: StartKind,
    pub outcome: Outcome,
    pub points: f64,
    pub world_km: f64,
    pub game_km: f64,
    pub peak_mph: f64,
    pub reasons: Vec<String>,
    pub started_ms: i64,
    pub updated_ms: i64,
}

impl JobView {
    fn new<P>(job: &Job<P>, r: &JobResult) -> JobView {
        let route = &job.info.fingerprint.route;
        let wall = |e: Option<&pt_core::timeline::JobEvent>| e.map(event_wall).unwrap_or(0);
        let mut reasons: Vec<String> = r.review.iter().map(|x| x.code().to_string()).collect();
        if r.speed.invalid {
            reasons.push("overspeed_invalid".into());
        } else if r.speed.penalty {
            reasons.push("speed_penalty".into());
        }
        JobView {
            game: job.game,
            profile: job.profile.clone(),
            cargo: job.info.cargo_name.clone(),
            source_city: route.source_city.clone(),
            destination_city: route.destination_city.clone(),
            state: job.state,
            start: job.start,
            outcome: r.outcome,
            points: r.points,
            world_km: r.distances.world_km,
            game_km: r.distances.counted_game_km,
            peak_mph: r.speed.peak_mph,
            reasons,
            started_ms: wall(job.events.first()),
            updated_ms: wall(job.events.last()),
        }
    }
}

fn event_wall(e: &pt_core::timeline::JobEvent) -> i64 {
    serde_json::to_value(e).ok().and_then(|v| v["wall_ms"].as_i64()).unwrap_or(0)
}

pub struct LiveJobs {
    cfg: Config,
    games: Vec<(Game, Profiles)>,
    sess_game: HashMap<String, Game>,
    finished: VecDeque<JobView>,
}

impl LiveJobs {
    pub fn new(cfg: Config) -> LiveJobs {
        LiveJobs { cfg, games: Vec::new(), sess_game: HashMap::new(), finished: VecDeque::new() }
    }

    pub fn config(&self) -> &Config {
        &self.cfg
    }

    /// Tells which game a session belongs to before its `init` is seen again
    /// (client restarted mid-session).
    pub fn set_session_game(&mut self, sess: &str, game: Game) {
        self.sess_game.insert(sess.to_string(), game);
    }

    fn game_index(&mut self, game: Game) -> usize {
        if let Some(i) = self.games.iter().position(|(g, _)| *g == game) {
            return i;
        }
        self.games.push((game, Profiles::new(self.cfg.clone())));
        self.games.len() - 1
    }

    /// Pushes one stored frame or client note, in stream order. Returns the
    /// alerts it raised.
    pub fn push(&mut self, raw: &str) -> Vec<Alert> {
        let Ok(f) = parse_frame(raw, &self.cfg.multiplayer) else { return Vec::new() };
        if let Body::Init { game: Some(g), .. } = &f.body {
            self.sess_game.insert(f.sess.clone(), *g);
        }
        let Some(&game) = self.sess_game.get(&f.sess) else { return Vec::new() };
        let gi = self.game_index(game);
        self.games[gi].1.push(&f);
        let notices = self.games[gi].1.take_notices();
        let evicted = self.games[gi].1.take_evicted();
        let mut alerts = Vec::new();
        for (profile, n) in notices {
            let (Notice::JobDelivered { job } | Notice::PenaltyActivated { job, .. }) = &n else { continue };
            let profiles = &self.games[gi].1;
            let Some(j) = profiles.jobs().find(|j| j.profile == profile && j.id == *job) else { continue };
            let cargo = j.info.cargo_name.clone();
            match n {
                Notice::JobDelivered { .. } => {
                    let r = profiles.evaluate(j, &self.cfg, &Context::default());
                    if r.speed.invalid {
                        alerts.push(Alert::InvalidDelivery { game, cargo, peak_mph: r.speed.peak_mph });
                    }
                }
                _ => alerts.push(Alert::PenaltyActivated { game, cargo }),
            }
        }
        for j in evicted {
            let r = evaluate(&j, &self.cfg, &Context::default());
            self.finished.push_front(JobView::new(&j, &r));
            self.finished.truncate(FINISHED_KEPT);
        }
        alerts
    }

    /// Every job, newest first: the live timelines, then recently evicted ones.
    pub fn jobs(&self) -> Vec<JobView> {
        let mut out: Vec<JobView> = self
            .games
            .iter()
            .flat_map(|(_, p)| p.jobs().map(move |j| JobView::new(j, &p.evaluate(j, &self.cfg, &Context::default()))))
            .collect();
        out.sort_by_key(|v| std::cmp::Reverse(v.started_ms));
        out.extend(self.finished.iter().cloned());
        out
    }
}

/// A uniformly random delay in `[min, max]` seconds at microsecond resolution,
/// from the OS random source (PLAN decision 10).
pub fn alert_delay(cfg: &Config) -> std::time::Duration {
    let (lo, hi) = cfg.notifications.delay_range_us();
    let mut b = [0u8; 8];
    let r = if getrandom::fill(&mut b).is_ok() { u64::from_le_bytes(b) } else { 0 };
    let span = hi.saturating_sub(lo) + 1;
    std::time::Duration::from_micros(lo + r % span)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn cfg() -> Config {
        Config::from_toml_str(crate::paths::SAMPLE_CONFIG).unwrap()
    }

    fn line(kind: &str, seq: u64, wall: i64, extra: serde_json::Value) -> String {
        let mut v = serde_json::json!({"v": 1, "kind": kind, "sess": "s1", "seq": seq, "wall_ms": wall, "sim_us": seq * 50_000});
        for (k, x) in extra.as_object().unwrap() {
            v[k] = x.clone();
        }
        v.to_string()
    }

    #[test]
    fn frames_of_unknown_sessions_are_ignored_until_the_game_is_known() {
        let mut live = LiveJobs::new(cfg());
        assert!(live.push(&line("sample", 5, 1, serde_json::json!({"ch": {}}))).is_empty());
        assert!(live.games.is_empty());
        live.set_session_game("s1", Game::Ats);
        live.push(&line("sample", 6, 2, serde_json::json!({"ch": {}})));
        assert_eq!(live.games.len(), 1);
        assert!(live.jobs().is_empty());
    }

    /// A minimal ATS session: accept with the cargo loaded, drive `secs` at
    /// `mph`, deliver. Shaped like the replay simulator (pt-replay tests/sim).
    fn job_at(mph: f64, secs: f64) -> Vec<String> {
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        let (mut seq, mut sim, mut x, mut odo) = (0u64, 0u64, 0.0f64, 1000.0f64);
        let mut emit = |kind: &str, extra: serde_json::Value, sim: u64| {
            seq += 1;
            let mut v = serde_json::json!({"v": 1, "kind": kind, "sess": "s1", "seq": seq, "wall_ms": 1_790_000_000_000i64 + (sim / 1000) as i64, "sim_us": sim});
            for (k, x) in extra.as_object().unwrap() {
                v[k] = x.clone();
            }
            out.push(v.to_string());
        };
        let a = |n: &str, v: serde_json::Value| serde_json::json!({"name": n, "index": null, "value": v});
        let job = serde_json::json!([
            a("cargo.id", "tyres".into()), a("cargo", "Tyres".into()), a("source.city.id", "chicago".into()),
            a("destination.city.id", "joliet".into()), a("source.company.id", "a".into()),
            a("destination.company.id", "b".into()), a("cargo.loaded", true.into()), a("job.market", "cargo_market".into()),
        ]);
        emit("init", serde_json::json!({"game_id": "ats", "game_version": {"major": 1, "minor": 7}}), 0);
        emit("config", serde_json::json!({"id": "truck", "attrs": [a("id", "volvo".into())]}), 0);
        let sample = |x: f64, odo: f64, v: f64| {
            serde_json::json!({"ch": {"truck.speed": v, "truck.odometer": odo, "truck.fuel.amount": 500.0,
                "truck.world.placement": {"position": {"x": x, "y": 0.0, "z": 0.0}}, "game.time": 1000,
                "local.scale": 20.0, "trailer.0.connected": true}})
        };
        emit("sample", sample(x, odo, 0.0), sim);
        emit("config", serde_json::json!({"id": "job", "attrs": job}), sim);
        let v = mph * 0.44704;
        for _ in 0..(secs * 20.0) as u64 {
            sim += 50_000;
            x += v * 0.05;
            odo += v * 0.05 * 20.0 / 1000.0;
            emit("sample", sample(x, odo, v), sim);
        }
        let km = serde_json::json!([a("distance.km", ((odo - 1000.0) as u64).into())]);
        emit("gameplay", serde_json::json!({"id": "job.delivered", "attrs": km}), sim);
        emit("config", serde_json::json!({"id": "job", "attrs": []}), sim);
        sim += 50_000;
        emit("sample", sample(x, odo, 0.0), sim);
        out
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_clean_job_shows_up_without_alerts() {
        let mut live = LiveJobs::new(cfg());
        let alerts: Vec<Alert> = job_at(60.0, 120.0).iter().flat_map(|l| live.push(l)).collect();
        assert!(alerts.is_empty(), "{alerts:?}");
        let jobs = live.jobs();
        assert_eq!(jobs.len(), 1);
        assert_eq!((jobs[0].state, jobs[0].cargo.as_str()), (JobState::Delivered, "Tyres"));
        assert!(jobs[0].world_km > 3.0, "{:?}", jobs[0]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn overspeed_raises_the_penalty_then_the_invalid_delivery() {
        let mut live = LiveJobs::new(cfg());
        let alerts: Vec<Alert> = job_at(160.0, 120.0).iter().flat_map(|l| live.push(l)).collect();
        assert_eq!(alerts.len(), 2, "{alerts:?}");
        assert!(matches!(alerts[0], Alert::PenaltyActivated { game: Game::Ats, .. }));
        assert!(matches!(&alerts[1], Alert::InvalidDelivery { peak_mph, .. } if (*peak_mph - 160.0).abs() < 0.1));
        let (title, text) = alerts[1].message(live.config());
        assert_eq!(title, "Invalid delivery");
        assert!(text.starts_with("Tyres: you drove over 125 mph"), "{text}");
        assert_eq!(live.jobs()[0].outcome, Outcome::Invalid);
    }

    #[test]
    fn delay_stays_inside_the_configured_range() {
        let c = cfg();
        for _ in 0..200 {
            let d = alert_delay(&c).as_secs_f64();
            assert!((c.notifications.delay_min_wall_s..=c.notifications.delay_max_wall_s).contains(&d), "{d}");
        }
    }
}

/// Frames on their way to the live timelines: everything stored at `stored_ms`,
/// in stream order. Cheap to clone; sending never blocks.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct Feed(std::sync::mpsc::Sender<(i64, Vec<String>)>);

impl Feed {
    pub fn send(&self, stored_ms: i64, raws: Vec<String>) {
        if !raws.is_empty() {
            let _ = self.0.send((stored_ms, raws));
        }
    }
}

/// Starts the live worker thread. It first rebuilds the timelines from the
/// sessions seen since `since_ms` (no alerts for those), then follows the feed.
/// Frames stored before the rebuild began are in the rebuild, so the feed
/// skips them.
pub fn spawn_worker(
    jobs: std::sync::Arc<std::sync::Mutex<LiveJobs>>,
    db: std::sync::Arc<std::sync::Mutex<crate::db::Db>>,
    since_ms: i64,
    alerts: tokio::sync::mpsc::UnboundedSender<Alert>,
) -> Feed {
    let (tx, rx) = std::sync::mpsc::channel::<(i64, Vec<String>)>();
    std::thread::spawn(move || {
        let t0 = crate::now_ms();
        let sessions = db.lock().expect("db").sessions_since(since_ms).unwrap_or_default();
        let mut frames = 0usize;
        for (sess, game_id) in sessions {
            let Ok(stream) = db.lock().expect("db").session_stream(&sess, t0) else { continue };
            let mut live = jobs.lock().expect("live");
            if let Some(g) = game_id.as_deref().and_then(Game::from_sdk_game_id) {
                live.set_session_game(&sess, g);
            }
            frames += stream.len();
            for raw in &stream {
                live.push(raw);
            }
        }
        crate::log!("live results rebuilt from {frames} stored frames in {} ms", crate::now_ms() - t0);
        while let Ok((stored_ms, raws)) = rx.recv() {
            if stored_ms < t0 {
                continue;
            }
            let mut live = jobs.lock().expect("live");
            for raw in &raws {
                for a in live.push(raw) {
                    let _ = alerts.send(a);
                }
            }
        }
    });
    Feed(tx)
}

```rs
//! Install manifest for the integrity check (rule 0, PLAN §6a): SHA-256 of the
//! client binary, the config file and every installed PlasmaTrack plugin.

use std::io::Read;
use std::path::Path;

use pt_core::upload::ManifestEntry;
use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};

use crate::steam::GameInstall;

pub fn sha256_file(path: &Path) -> std::io::Result<String> {
    let mut f = std::fs::File::open(path)?;
    let mut h = Sha256::new();
    let mut buf = vec![0u8; 64 * 1024];
    loop {
        let n = f.read(&mut buf)?;
        if n == 0 {
            break;
        }
        h.update(&buf[..n]);
    }
    Ok(h.finalize().iter().map(|b| format!("{b:02x}")).collect())
}

pub fn compute(client_binary: Option<&Path>, config_file: Option<&Path>, installs: &[GameInstall]) -> Vec<ManifestEntry> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let mut add = |role: &str, path: &Path| {
        if let Ok(sha256) = sha256_file(path) {
            out.push(ManifestEntry { role: role.to_string(), path: path.display().to_string(), sha256 });
        }
    };
    if let Some(p) = client_binary {
        add("client_binary", p);
    }
    if let Some(p) = config_file {
        add("config_file", p);
    }
    for i in installs {
        let p = i.plugin_path();
        if p.is_file() {
            add("plugin", &p);
        }
    }
    out
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn hashes_files_and_skips_missing_plugins() {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let cfg = dir.path().join("plasmatrack.toml");
        std::fs::write(&cfg, "abc").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            sha256_file(&cfg).unwrap(),
            "ba7816bf8f01cfea414140de5dae2223b00361a396177a9cb410ff61f20015ad"
        );
        let plugins = dir.path().join("plugins");
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&plugins).unwrap();
        let install = GameInstall { game: pt_core::Game::Ats, plugins_dir: plugins.clone(), windows_build: true };
        let m = compute(None, Some(&cfg), std::slice::from_ref(&install));
        assert_eq!(m.len(), 1);
        std::fs::write(plugins.join("plasmatrack.dll"), "dll").unwrap();
        let m = compute(None, Some(&cfg), &[install]);
        assert_eq!(m.iter().map(|e| e.role.as_str()).collect::<Vec<_>>(), vec!["config_file", "plugin"]);
    }
}

`crates/pt-client/src/setup.rs`:

```rs
//! Install steps behind the `install-plugin`, `uninstall-plugin` and `set-local`
//! commands. The installer (installer/, Electron) only calls these commands, so
//! everything that touches game folders or the config is here and tested.

use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use pt_core::{Config, Game};
use serde::Serialize;

use crate::steam::{self, GameInstall};

/// What happened in one plugins folder.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
pub struct FolderResult {
    pub game: Game,
    pub plugins_dir: PathBuf,
    /// The folder's contents changed.
    pub changed: bool,
    /// Why this folder failed; the other folders are still handled.
    pub error: Option<String>,
}

fn same_file_contents(a: &Path, b: &Path) -> bool {
    match (std::fs::read(a), std::fs::read(b)) {
        (Ok(x), Ok(y)) => x == y,
        _ => false,
    }
}

fn io_hint(e: &std::io::Error) -> String {
    match e.kind() {
        // A loaded DLL cannot be overwritten while the game runs.
        std::io::ErrorKind::PermissionDenied => format!("{e} (close the game; if it persists, run as administrator)"),
        _ => e.to_string(),
    }
}

/// Copies `plugin` (plasmatrack.dll or plasmatrack.so) into every install built
/// for it, then writes `plasmatrack.ini` there. Returns one result per folder.
pub fn install_plugin(installs: &[GameInstall], plugin: &Path, ini: &[(&str, String)]) -> Vec<FolderResult> {
    let is_dll = plugin.extension().is_some_and(|e| e.eq_ignore_ascii_case("dll"));
    installs
        .iter()
        .filter(|i| i.windows_build == is_dll)
        .map(|i| {
            let dest = i.plugin_path();
            let copied = if same_file_contents(plugin, &dest) {
                Ok(false)
            } else {
                std::fs::create_dir_all(&i.plugins_dir).and_then(|_| std::fs::copy(plugin, &dest)).map(|_| true)
            };
            let result = copied.and_then(|c| steam::write_ini(&i.plugins_dir, ini).map(|w| c || w));
            FolderResult {
                game: i.game,
                plugins_dir: i.plugins_dir.clone(),
                changed: *result.as_ref().unwrap_or(&false),
                error: result.err().map(|e| io_hint(&e)),
            }
        })
        .collect()
}

/// Removes the plugin and `plasmatrack.ini` from every install. The plugin's
/// `plasmatrack/` folder (journal, captures) is left for the player to delete.
pub fn uninstall_plugin(installs: &[GameInstall]) -> Vec<FolderResult> {
    installs
        .iter()
        .map(|i| {
            let mut changed = false;
            let mut error = None;
            for p in [i.plugin_path(), i.plugins_dir.join(steam::INI_FILE)] {
                match std::fs::remove_file(&p) {
                    Ok(()) => changed = true,
                    Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {}
                    Err(e) => error = Some(io_hint(&e)),
                }
            }
            FolderResult { game: i.game, plugins_dir: i.plugins_dir.clone(), changed, error }
        })
        .collect()
}

/// Replaces a value in place, so the comment above its key stays.
fn set(table: &mut dyn toml_edit::TableLike, key: &str, v: &str) {
    match table.get_mut(key) {
        Some(item) => *item = toml_edit::value(v),
        None => {
            table.insert(key, toml_edit::value(v));
        }
    }
}

/// Sets `[local] server_url` and/or `token` in a config file's text. Comments
/// and every other key are kept as they are, so the config still matches the
/// published version (rule 0 ignores `[local]`).
pub fn set_local(config_text: &str, server_url: Option<&str>, token: Option<&str>) -> Result<String, String> {
    let mut doc: toml_edit::DocumentMut = config_text.parse().map_err(|e| format!("config: {e}"))?;
    let local = doc
        .get_mut("local")
        .and_then(|t| t.as_table_like_mut())
        .ok_or("config has no [local] table")?;
    if let Some(url) = server_url {
        let url = url.trim().trim_end_matches('/');
        if !(url.starts_with("https://") || url.starts_with("http://")) {
            return Err("server URL must start with https://".into());
        }
        set(local, "server_url", url);
    }
    if let Some(token) = token {
        let token = token.trim();
        if token.chars().any(|c| c.is_control()) {
            return Err("token contains control characters".into());
        }
        set(local, "token", token);
    }
    let text = doc.to_string();
    Config::from_toml_str(&text).map_err(|e| format!("config: {e}"))?;
    Ok(text)
}

/// The shipped config with the `[local]` values of an existing config carried
/// over. Everything else must match a published config version (rule 0), so an
/// install or update always starts from the config it ships; an old file that
/// lacks newer keys, or no longer parses, cannot stop the client. Values of
/// `[local]` keys the shipped config does not have are dropped.
pub fn rebase_config(existing: Option<&str>, shipped: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
    let mut doc: toml_edit::DocumentMut = shipped.parse().map_err(|e| format!("shipped config: {e}"))?;
    let old: Option<toml_edit::DocumentMut> = existing.and_then(|t| t.parse().ok());
    if let (Some(old_local), Some(new_local)) = (
        old.as_ref().and_then(|d| d.get("local")).and_then(|t| t.as_table_like()),
        doc.get_mut("local").and_then(|t| t.as_table_like_mut()),
    ) {
        let keys: Vec<String> = new_local.iter().map(|(k, _)| k.to_string()).collect();
        for k in keys {
            if let Some(v) = old_local.get(&k).and_then(|i| i.as_value()) {
                // Keep the shipped line's decoration (comments stay where they are).
                let mut v = v.clone();
                v.decor_mut().clear();
                if let Some(item) = new_local.get_mut(&k) {
                    *item = toml_edit::Item::Value(v);
                }
            }
        }
    }
    let text = doc.to_string();
    Config::from_toml_str(&text).map_err(|e| format!("config: {e}"))?;
    Ok(text)
}

/// Writes `text` to `path` through a temporary file, so a crash never leaves a
/// half-written config. The config holds the player token: on Unix the file is
/// owner-only (0600), since `~/.config` is not private the way `%APPDATA%` is.
pub fn write_atomically(path: &Path, text: &str) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    use std::io::Write;
    if let Some(dir) = path.parent() {
        std::fs::create_dir_all(dir)?;
    }
    let tmp = path.with_extension("toml.tmp");
    let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&tmp); // `mode` below only applies to a new file
    let mut open = std::fs::OpenOptions::new();
    open.write(true).create_new(true);
    #[cfg(unix)]
    std::os::unix::fs::OpenOptionsExt::mode(&mut open, 0o600);
    open.open(&tmp)?.write_all(text.as_bytes())?;
    std::fs::rename(&tmp, path)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[cfg(unix)]
    #[test]
    fn config_is_written_owner_only() {
        use std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt;
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let path = dir.path().join("plasmatrack.toml");
        std::fs::write(&path, "old").unwrap();
        std::fs::set_permissions(&path, std::fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o644)).unwrap();
        write_atomically(&path, "token = \"x\"\n").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(std::fs::read_to_string(&path).unwrap(), "token = \"x\"\n");
        assert_eq!(std::fs::metadata(&path).unwrap().permissions().mode() & 0o777, 0o600);
    }
    use crate::paths::SAMPLE_CONFIG;

    fn fake_installs(root: &Path) -> Vec<GameInstall> {
        vec![
            GameInstall { game: Game::Ats, plugins_dir: root.join("ats/bin/win_x64/plugins"), windows_build: true },
            GameInstall { game: Game::Ets2, plugins_dir: root.join("ets2/bin/win_x64/plugins"), windows_build: true },
            GameInstall { game: Game::Ets2, plugins_dir: root.join("ets2/bin/linux_x64/plugins"), windows_build: false },
        ]
    }

    #[test]
    fn installs_into_matching_builds_and_is_idempotent() {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let dll = dir.path().join("plasmatrack.dll");
        std::fs::write(&dll, "dll v1").unwrap();
        let installs = fake_installs(dir.path());
        let ini = [("port", "30455".to_string())];

        let r = install_plugin(&installs, &dll, &ini);
        assert_eq!(r.len(), 2, "the .so folder is skipped");
        assert!(r.iter().all(|f| f.changed && f.error.is_none()));
        assert_eq!(std::fs::read_to_string(installs[0].plugin_path()).unwrap(), "dll v1");
        assert_eq!(std::fs::read_to_string(installs[1].plugins_dir.join("plasmatrack.ini")).unwrap(), "port = 30455\n");
        assert!(!installs[2].plugins_dir.exists());

        assert!(install_plugin(&installs, &dll, &ini).iter().all(|f| !f.changed));
        std::fs::write(&dll, "dll v2").unwrap();
        assert!(install_plugin(&installs, &dll, &ini).iter().all(|f| f.changed));
        assert_eq!(std::fs::read_to_string(installs[1].plugin_path()).unwrap(), "dll v2");
    }

    #[test]
    fn install_keeps_unmanaged_ini_lines() {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let dll = dir.path().join("plasmatrack.dll");
        std::fs::write(&dll, "dll").unwrap();
        let installs = fake_installs(dir.path());
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&installs[0].plugins_dir).unwrap();
        std::fs::write(installs[0].plugins_dir.join("plasmatrack.ini"), "capture = 1\nport = 1\n").unwrap();
        install_plugin(&installs[..1], &dll, &[("port", "30455".into())]);
        assert_eq!(
            std::fs::read_to_string(installs[0].plugins_dir.join("plasmatrack.ini")).unwrap(),
            "capture = 1\nport = 30455\n"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn uninstall_removes_plugin_and_ini_only() {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let dll = dir.path().join("plasmatrack.dll");
        std::fs::write(&dll, "dll").unwrap();
        let installs = fake_installs(dir.path());
        install_plugin(&installs, &dll, &[("port", "30455".into())]);
        let journal = installs[0].plugins_dir.join("plasmatrack");
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&journal).unwrap();

        let r = uninstall_plugin(&installs);
        assert_eq!(r.iter().map(|f| f.changed).collect::<Vec<_>>(), [true, true, false]);
        assert!(r.iter().all(|f| f.error.is_none()));
        assert!(!installs[0].plugin_path().exists());
        assert!(!installs[0].plugins_dir.join("plasmatrack.ini").exists());
        assert!(journal.is_dir());
    }

    #[test]
    fn set_local_keeps_comments_and_integrity_hash() {
        let text = set_local(SAMPLE_CONFIG, Some("https://pt.example.org/ "), Some(" abc123 ")).unwrap();
        let before = Config::from_toml_str(SAMPLE_CONFIG).unwrap();
        let after = Config::from_toml_str(&text).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(after.local.server_url, "https://pt.example.org");
        assert_eq!(after.local.token, "abc123");
        assert_eq!(after.integrity_hash(), before.integrity_hash());
        assert!(text.contains("# Player token issued by the server"));
        assert_eq!(text.lines().count(), SAMPLE_CONFIG.lines().count());

        // Token only: the URL stays.
        let again = set_local(&text, None, Some("xyz")).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(Config::from_toml_str(&again).unwrap().local.server_url, "https://pt.example.org");
    }

    #[test]
    fn rebase_keeps_local_and_takes_everything_else_from_the_shipped_config() {
        let mine = set_local(SAMPLE_CONFIG, Some("https://pt.example.org"), Some("tok")).unwrap();
        // An old config: a rule changed, a newer key missing, a custom port.
        let old = mine
            .replace("speed_penalty_factor = 0.85", "speed_penalty_factor = 0.5")
            .replace("port = 30455", "port = 31111")
            .lines()
            .filter(|l| !l.starts_with("delivered_distance_resolution_km"))
            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
            .join("\n");
        assert!(Config::from_toml_str(&old).is_err(), "the old file no longer loads");
        let text = rebase_config(Some(&old), SAMPLE_CONFIG).unwrap();
        let cfg = Config::from_toml_str(&text).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(cfg.integrity_hash(), Config::from_toml_str(SAMPLE_CONFIG).unwrap().integrity_hash());
        assert_eq!((cfg.local.server_url.as_str(), cfg.local.token.as_str(), cfg.local.port), ("https://pt.example.org", "tok", 31111));
        assert!(text.contains("# Player token issued by the server"));
        // Nothing to carry over: the shipped config as is.
        assert_eq!(rebase_config(None, SAMPLE_CONFIG).unwrap(), SAMPLE_CONFIG);
        assert_eq!(rebase_config(Some("not toml ["), SAMPLE_CONFIG).unwrap(), SAMPLE_CONFIG);
    }

    #[test]
    fn set_local_rejects_bad_input() {
        assert!(set_local(SAMPLE_CONFIG, Some("pt.example.org"), None).is_err());
        assert!(set_local(SAMPLE_CONFIG, None, Some("a\nb")).is_err());
        assert!(set_local("[sync]\n", None, Some("a")).is_err());
    }
}

`crates/pt-client/src/status.rs`:

```rs
//! Live client status, shared by all tasks, and the local status page
//! (`http://127.0.0.1:<status_port>/`, loopback only).

use std::net::SocketAddr;
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};

use axum::extract::State;
use axum::http::{HeaderMap, StatusCode};
use axum::response::{Html, IntoResponse};
use axum::routing::{get, post};
use axum::{Json, Router};
use serde::Serialize;
use tokio::sync::Notify;

use crate::db::{Db, DbStats};
use crate::live::{JobView, LiveJobs};

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, Serialize)]
pub struct Status {
    pub client_version: String,
    pub plugin_connections: u32,
    pub last_frame_ms: Option<i64>,
    pub frames_received: u64,
    pub acks_sent: u64,
    pub last_session: Option<String>,
    pub last_game: Option<String>,
    pub upload_configured: bool,
    pub last_upload_attempt_ms: Option<i64>,
    pub last_upload_ok_ms: Option<i64>,
    pub last_upload_error: Option<String>,
    pub config_hash: String,
    pub manifest_files: usize,
    /// A newer release being downloaded or waiting to install (docs/UPDATES.md).
    pub update: Option<String>,
}

pub type SharedStatus = Arc<Mutex<Status>>;

#[derive(Clone)]
struct AppState {
    status: SharedStatus,
    db: Arc<Mutex<Db>>,
    shutdown: Arc<Notify>,
    jobs: Option<Arc<Mutex<LiveJobs>>>,
}

#[derive(Serialize)]
struct Report {
    #[serde(flatten)]
    status: Status,
    db: DbStats,
}

fn report(state: &AppState) -> Report {
    let status = state.status.lock().expect("status lock").clone();
    let db = state.db.lock().expect("db lock").stats().unwrap_or_default();
    Report { status, db }
}

async fn status_json(State(state): State<AppState>) -> impl IntoResponse {
    Json(report(&state))
}

fn jobs(state: &AppState) -> Vec<JobView> {
    state.jobs.as_ref().map(|j| j.lock().expect("live lock").jobs()).unwrap_or_default()
}

/// Provisional results (the server decides; PLAN §6b).
async fn jobs_json(State(state): State<AppState>) -> impl IntoResponse {
    Json(jobs(&state))
}

fn when(ms: i64) -> String {
    let age_s = (crate::now_ms() - ms).max(0) / 1000;
    match age_s {
        s if s < 120 => format!("{s} s ago"),
        s if s < 7200 => format!("{} min ago", s / 60),
        s if s < 172_800 => format!("{} h ago", s / 3600),
        s => format!("{} days ago", s / 86_400),
    }
}

fn job_rows(list: &[JobView]) -> String {
    if list.is_empty() {
        return "<p>No jobs yet. Jobs appear here as you drive.</p>".into();
    }
    let mut rows = String::from(
        "<table class=jobs><tr><th>Started</th><th>Game</th><th>Cargo</th><th>Route</th><th>State</th>
         <th>Result</th><th>Points</th><th>1:1 km</th><th>Game km</th><th>Notes</th></tr>",
    );
    for j in list {
        let game = match j.game {
            pt_core::Game::Ets2 => "ETS2",
            pt_core::Game::Ats => "ATS",
        };
        let enum_name = |v: serde_json::Value| v.as_str().unwrap_or_default().replace('_', " ");
        let mut notes = j.reasons.join(", ");
        if j.start == pt_core::timeline::StartKind::LateStart && !notes.contains("late_start") {
            notes = if notes.is_empty() { "late start".into() } else { format!("late start, {notes}") };
        }
        rows.push_str(&format!(
            "<tr><td>{}</td><td>{game}</td><td>{}</td><td>{} → {}</td><td>{}</td><td>{}</td><td>{:.1}</td>
             <td>{:.1}</td><td>{:.0}</td><td>{}</td></tr>",
            when(j.started_ms),
            esc(&j.cargo),
            esc(&j.source_city),
            esc(&j.destination_city),
            enum_name(serde_json::to_value(j.state).unwrap_or_default()),
            enum_name(serde_json::to_value(j.outcome).unwrap_or_default()),
            j.points,
            j.world_km,
            j.game_km,
            esc(&notes.replace('_', " ")),
        ));
    }
    rows.push_str("</table>");
    rows
}

fn esc(s: &str) -> String {
    s.replace('&', "&amp;").replace('<', "&lt;").replace('>', "&gt;").replace('"', "&quot;")
}

async fn status_page(State(state): State<AppState>) -> impl IntoResponse {
    let r = report(&state);
    let job_table = job_rows(&jobs(&state));
    let json = serde_json::to_value(&r).unwrap_or_default();
    let mut rows = String::new();
    if let Some(obj) = json.as_object() {
        for (k, v) in obj {
            let v = match v {
                serde_json::Value::String(s) => s.clone(),
                other => other.to_string(),
            };
            rows.push_str(&format!("<tr><th>{}</th><td>{}</td></tr>", esc(k), esc(&v)));
        }
    }
    Html(format!(
        "<!doctype html><html><head><meta charset=utf-8><meta http-equiv=refresh content=5>\
         <title>PlasmaTrack client</title><style>body{{font-family:system-ui,sans-serif;margin:16px}}\
         th{{text-align:left;padding-right:16px}}td{{font-family:monospace}}\
         .jobs td,.jobs th{{padding:2px 12px 2px 0;font-family:system-ui,sans-serif}}</style></head>\
         <body><h1>PlasmaTrack client</h1><h2>Jobs</h2>\
         <p>Provisional: the server's result is the one that counts.</p>{job_table}\
         <h2>Client</h2><table>{rows}</table></body></html>"
    ))
}

/// Header `plasmatrack-client stop` sends with `POST /quit`.
pub const QUIT_HEADER: (&str, &str) = ("x-plasmatrack", "quit");

/// Stops the client (`plasmatrack-client stop`, the installer). Browsers cannot
/// trigger it: they send `Origin` on cross-site POSTs, and the custom header
/// needs a CORS preflight this server never grants.
async fn quit(State(state): State<AppState>, headers: HeaderMap) -> StatusCode {
    let asked = headers.get(QUIT_HEADER.0).is_some_and(|v| v == QUIT_HEADER.1);
    if !asked || headers.contains_key("origin") {
        return StatusCode::FORBIDDEN;
    }
    state.shutdown.notify_one();
    StatusCode::NO_CONTENT
}

pub fn router(status: SharedStatus, db: Arc<Mutex<Db>>, shutdown: Arc<Notify>, jobs: Option<Arc<Mutex<LiveJobs>>>) -> Router {
    Router::new()
        .route("/", get(status_page))
        .route("/status.json", get(status_json))
        .route("/jobs.json", get(jobs_json))
        .route("/quit", post(quit))
        .with_state(AppState { status, db, shutdown, jobs })
}

/// Serves the status page until the task is dropped. Only loopback addresses
/// are accepted by the config validation.
pub async fn serve(
    addr: SocketAddr,
    status: SharedStatus,
    db: Arc<Mutex<Db>>,
    shutdown: Arc<Notify>,
    jobs: Option<Arc<Mutex<LiveJobs>>>,
) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    let listener = tokio::net::TcpListener::bind(addr).await?;
    axum::serve(listener, router(status, db, shutdown, jobs)).await
}

```rs
//! Finds ETS2/ATS installs in every Steam library (native Steam, Flatpak and
//! Snap Steam on Linux) and maintains `plasmatrack.ini` next to the plugin.

use std::collections::BTreeSet;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use pt_core::Game;

pub const PLUGIN_FILE_WINDOWS: &str = "plasmatrack.dll";
pub const PLUGIN_FILE_LINUX: &str = "plasmatrack.so";
pub const INI_FILE: &str = "plasmatrack.ini";

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)]
pub struct GameInstall {
    pub game: Game,
    /// `bin/win_x64/plugins` (Windows DLL, also used under Proton) or
    /// `bin/linux_x64/plugins` (native Linux build).
    pub plugins_dir: PathBuf,
    pub windows_build: bool,
}

impl GameInstall {
    pub fn plugin_path(&self) -> PathBuf {
        self.plugins_dir.join(if self.windows_build { PLUGIN_FILE_WINDOWS } else { PLUGIN_FILE_LINUX })
    }
}

fn game_folder(game: Game) -> &'static str {
    match game {
        Game::Ets2 => "Euro Truck Simulator 2",
        Game::Ats => "American Truck Simulator",
    }
}

/// Candidate Steam installation roots for this OS.
pub fn steam_roots() -> Vec<PathBuf> {
    let mut roots = Vec::new();
    #[cfg(windows)]
    {
        use winreg::enums::HKEY_CURRENT_USER;
        if let Ok(key) = winreg::RegKey::predef(HKEY_CURRENT_USER).open_subkey("Software\\Valve\\Steam") {
            if let Ok(p) = key.get_value::<String, _>("SteamPath") {
                roots.push(PathBuf::from(p));
            }
        }
        roots.push(PathBuf::from(r"C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam"));
    }
    #[cfg(not(windows))]
    {
        if let Some(home) = dirs::home_dir() {
            for rel in [
                ".local/share/Steam",
                ".steam/steam",
                ".var/app/com.valvesoftware.Steam/.local/share/Steam", // Flatpak Steam
                "snap/steam/common/.local/share/Steam",                 // Snap Steam
            ] {
                roots.push(home.join(rel));
            }
        }
    }
    roots
}

/// Extracts the `"path"` values from Steam's `libraryfolders.vdf`.
pub fn parse_library_paths(vdf: &str) -> Vec<PathBuf> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for line in vdf.lines() {
        let line = line.trim();
        let Some(rest) = line.strip_prefix("\"path\"") else { continue };
        let rest = rest.trim();
        let Some(inner) = rest.strip_prefix('"').and_then(|r| r.strip_suffix('"')) else { continue };
        out.push(PathBuf::from(inner.replace("\\\\", "\\")));
    }
    out
}

/// Every Steam library folder reachable from the known roots.
pub fn library_folders(roots: &[PathBuf]) -> Vec<PathBuf> {
    let mut libs = BTreeSet::new();
    for root in roots {
        if !root.join("steamapps").is_dir() {
            continue;
        }
        libs.insert(normalize(root));
        if let Ok(text) = std::fs::read_to_string(root.join("steamapps").join("libraryfolders.vdf")) {
            for p in parse_library_paths(&text) {
                if p.join("steamapps").is_dir() {
                    libs.insert(normalize(&p));
                }
            }
        }
    }
    libs.into_iter().collect()
}

fn normalize(p: &Path) -> PathBuf {
    let canon = std::fs::canonicalize(p).unwrap_or_else(|_| p.to_path_buf());
    // Windows canonical paths are verbatim (`\\?\C:\...`); keep plain drive paths
    // readable in logs and manifests. UNC paths stay verbatim.
    let s = canon.to_string_lossy();
    match s.strip_prefix(r"\\?\") {
        Some(rest) if rest.as_bytes().get(1) == Some(&b':') => PathBuf::from(rest),
        _ => canon,
    }
}

/// All ETS2/ATS installs in the given libraries.
pub fn find_installs(libraries: &[PathBuf]) -> Vec<GameInstall> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for lib in libraries {
        for game in [Game::Ets2, Game::Ats] {
            let bin = lib.join("steamapps").join("common").join(game_folder(game)).join("bin");
            for (sub, windows_build) in [("win_x64", true), ("linux_x64", false)] {
                if bin.join(sub).is_dir() {
                    out.push(GameInstall { game, plugins_dir: bin.join(sub).join("plugins"), windows_build });
                }
            }
        }
    }
    out.sort();
    out
}

pub fn discover() -> Vec<GameInstall> {
    find_installs(&library_folders(&steam_roots()))
}

/// Keys the client manages in `plasmatrack.ini`; every other line (e.g.
/// `capture = 1`, comments) is preserved.
pub fn merge_ini(existing: &str, managed: &[(&str, String)]) -> String {
    let mut out = String::new();
    let mut written = BTreeSet::new();
    for line in existing.lines() {
        let key = line.split(['=', '#', ';']).next().unwrap_or("").trim();
        if let Some((k, v)) = managed.iter().find(|(k, _)| *k == key && line.contains('=')) {
            if written.insert(*k) {
                out.push_str(&format!("{k} = {v}\n"));
            }
        } else {
            out.push_str(line);
            out.push('\n');
        }
    }
    for (k, v) in managed {
        if !written.contains(k) {
            out.push_str(&format!("{k} = {v}\n"));
        }
    }
    out
}

/// Writes/updates `plasmatrack.ini` in a plugins folder. Returns true if the
/// file changed. The folder must already exist (the plugin is installed there).
pub fn write_ini(plugins_dir: &Path, managed: &[(&str, String)]) -> std::io::Result<bool> {
    let path = plugins_dir.join(INI_FILE);
    let existing = std::fs::read_to_string(&path).unwrap_or_default();
    let merged = merge_ini(&existing, managed);
    if merged == existing {
        return Ok(false);
    }
    std::fs::write(&path, merged)?;
    Ok(true)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn parses_libraryfolders_vdf() {
        let vdf = r#""libraryfolders"
{
	"0"
	{
		"path"		"C:\\Program Files (x86)\\Steam"
		"label"		""
		"apps"
		{
			"227300"		"30106738302"
		}
	}
	"1"
	{
		"path"		"D:\\SteamLibrary"
	}
}"#;
        assert_eq!(
            parse_library_paths(vdf),
            vec![PathBuf::from(r"C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam"), PathBuf::from(r"D:\SteamLibrary")]
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn ini_merge_preserves_unmanaged_lines() {
        let existing = "; comment\ncapture = 1\nport = 1234\njournal_max_mib = 8\n";
        let merged = merge_ini(existing, &[("port", "30455".into()), ("sample_rate_hz", "20".into())]);
        assert_eq!(merged, "; comment\ncapture = 1\nport = 30455\njournal_max_mib = 8\nsample_rate_hz = 20\n");
        // Idempotent.
        assert_eq!(merge_ini(&merged, &[("port", "30455".into()), ("sample_rate_hz", "20".into())]), merged);
    }

    #[test]
    fn finds_installs_in_a_fake_library() {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let lib = dir.path().to_path_buf();
        std::fs::create_dir_all(lib.join("steamapps/common/American Truck Simulator/bin/win_x64")).unwrap();
        std::fs::create_dir_all(lib.join("steamapps/common/Euro Truck Simulator 2/bin/linux_x64")).unwrap();
        let installs = find_installs(std::slice::from_ref(&lib));
        assert_eq!(installs.len(), 2);
        assert!(installs.iter().any(|i| i.game == Game::Ats && i.windows_build));
        assert!(installs.iter().any(|i| i.game == Game::Ets2 && !i.windows_build));
        let ats = installs.iter().find(|i| i.game == Game::Ats).unwrap();
        assert!(ats.plugin_path().ends_with("plugins/plasmatrack.dll") || ats.plugin_path().ends_with("plugins\\plasmatrack.dll"));
    }
}

`crates/pt-client/src/tray.rs`:

```rs
//! Notification-area (tray) icon of the windowless client on Windows, drawn
//! with Shell_NotifyIconW on a hidden window. The icon shows that PlasmaTrack
//! runs; its tooltip and menu show the game connection and the upload state.
//!
//! The window is a hidden top-level window, so `taskkill` without `/F` asks it
//! to close (WM_CLOSE) and the client shuts down cleanly.
//!
//! Everything here runs on the thread that calls [`run`]. Callbacks only take
//! shared borrows of the thread-local state, because menus and shell calls
//! pump messages and re-enter the window procedure.

use std::cell::{Cell, RefCell};
use std::ptr::null;

use windows_sys::Win32::Foundation::{HWND, LPARAM, LRESULT, POINT, WPARAM};
use windows_sys::Win32::System::LibraryLoader::GetModuleHandleW;
use windows_sys::Win32::UI::Shell::{
    ShellExecuteW, Shell_NotifyIconW, NIF_ICON, NIF_INFO, NIF_MESSAGE, NIF_TIP, NIIF_WARNING, NIM_ADD, NIM_DELETE, NIM_MODIFY,
    NOTIFYICONDATAW,
};
use windows_sys::Win32::UI::WindowsAndMessaging::{
    AppendMenuW, CreateIcon, CreatePopupMenu, CreateWindowExW, DefWindowProcW, DestroyIcon, DestroyMenu, DestroyWindow,
    DispatchMessageW, GetCursorPos, GetMessageW, KillTimer, MessageBoxW, PostMessageW, PostQuitMessage, RegisterClassW,
    RegisterWindowMessageW, SetForegroundWindow, SetMenuDefaultItem, SetTimer, TrackPopupMenu, TranslateMessage, HICON,
    MB_ICONERROR, MB_OK, MF_GRAYED, MF_SEPARATOR, MF_STRING, MSG, SW_SHOWNORMAL, TPM_NONOTIFY, TPM_RETURNCMD,
    TPM_RIGHTBUTTON, WM_APP, WM_CLOSE, WM_CONTEXTMENU, WM_DESTROY, WM_LBUTTONDBLCLK, WM_NULL, WM_RBUTTONUP, WM_TIMER,
    WNDCLASSW,
};

const WM_TRAY: u32 = WM_APP + 1;
const WM_EXIT: u32 = WM_APP + 2;
const TIMER_REFRESH: usize = 1;
const TIMER_FORCE_EXIT: usize = 2;
const ID_STATUS_PAGE: usize = 10;
const ID_DATA_FOLDER: usize = 11;
const ID_QUIT: usize = 12;

/// What the tray shows and does. `lines` are status lines for the tooltip and
/// the menu; they are re-read every two seconds.
pub struct Callbacks {
    pub title: String,
    pub lines: Box<dyn Fn() -> Vec<String>>,
    pub open_status: Box<dyn Fn()>,
    pub open_data: Box<dyn Fn()>,
    pub quit: Box<dyn Fn()>,
}

struct State {
    cb: Callbacks,
    icon: HICON,
    taskbar_created: u32,
    quitting: Cell<bool>,
}

thread_local! {
    static STATE: RefCell<Option<State>> = const { RefCell::new(None) };
}

fn with_state<R>(f: impl FnOnce(&State) -> R) -> Option<R> {
    STATE.with(|s| s.try_borrow().ok().and_then(|s| s.as_ref().map(f)))
}

fn wide(s: &str) -> Vec<u16> {
    s.encode_utf16().chain(std::iter::once(0)).collect()
}

/// Ends the tray loop from any thread (after the client stopped).
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub struct Exit(usize);

impl Exit {
    pub fn post(self) {
        unsafe { PostMessageW(self.0 as HWND, WM_EXIT, 0, 0) };
    }
}

impl Exit {
    /// A handle for desktop notifications from the same icon.
    pub fn notifier(self) -> Notifier {
        Notifier(self.0)
    }
}

/// Shows notifications from the tray icon (any thread). Windows 10 and 11 show
/// them as toasts; focus assist may hold them while a game runs fullscreen.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub struct Notifier(usize);

impl Notifier {
    pub fn show(self, title: &str, text: &str) {
        let mut nid: NOTIFYICONDATAW = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };
        nid.cbSize = std::mem::size_of::<NOTIFYICONDATAW>() as u32;
        nid.hWnd = self.0 as HWND;
        nid.uID = 1;
        nid.uFlags = NIF_INFO;
        nid.dwInfoFlags = NIIF_WARNING;
        let copy = |dst: &mut [u16], src: &str| {
            let max = dst.len() - 1;
            for (d, s) in dst.iter_mut().zip(src.encode_utf16().take(max)) {
                *d = s;
            }
        };
        copy(&mut nid.szInfoTitle, title);
        copy(&mut nid.szInfo, text);
        unsafe { Shell_NotifyIconW(NIM_MODIFY, &nid) };
    }
}

/// Opens a URL or folder with its default program.
pub fn open(target: &str) {
    let (verb, target) = (wide("open"), wide(target));
    unsafe { ShellExecuteW(std::ptr::null_mut(), verb.as_ptr(), target.as_ptr(), null(), null(), SW_SHOWNORMAL) };
}

/// Shows an error dialog (any thread).
pub fn error_box(text: &str) {
    let (text, title) = (wide(text), wide("PlasmaTrack"));
    unsafe { MessageBoxW(std::ptr::null_mut(), text.as_ptr(), title.as_ptr(), MB_OK | MB_ICONERROR) };
}

/// 32×32 RGBA: a purple disc with a white "P".
pub fn icon_rgba() -> Vec<u8> {
    const N: usize = 32;
    let mut px = vec![0u8; N * N * 4];
    for y in 0..N {
        for x in 0..N {
            let (fx, fy) = (x as f32 + 0.5, y as f32 + 0.5);
            let d = ((fx - 16.0).powi(2) + (fy - 16.0).powi(2)).sqrt();
            let alpha = (15.5 - d).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
            if alpha == 0.0 {
                continue;
            }
            let stem = (10.0..14.0).contains(&fx) && (7.0..25.0).contains(&fy);
            let b = ((fx - 15.0).powi(2) + (fy - 12.5).powi(2)).sqrt();
            let bowl = fx >= 12.0 && (3.0..6.5).contains(&b);
            let rgb = if stem || bowl { [255, 255, 255] } else { [106, 61, 232] };
            let i = (y * N + x) * 4;
            px[i..i + 3].copy_from_slice(&rgb);
            px[i + 3] = (alpha * 255.0) as u8;
        }
    }
    px
}

unsafe fn make_icon() -> HICON {
    let mut bgra = icon_rgba();
    // CreateIcon wants BGRA colour bits and an AND mask (inverted alpha).
    let mask: Vec<u8> = bgra.chunks_exact(4).map(|p| 255 - p[3]).collect();
    for p in bgra.chunks_exact_mut(4) {
        p.swap(0, 2);
    }
    CreateIcon(GetModuleHandleW(null()), 32, 32, 1, 32, mask.as_ptr(), bgra.as_ptr())
}

fn notify_data(hwnd: HWND, icon: HICON, tip: &str) -> NOTIFYICONDATAW {
    let mut nid: NOTIFYICONDATAW = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };
    nid.cbSize = std::mem::size_of::<NOTIFYICONDATAW>() as u32;
    nid.hWnd = hwnd;
    nid.uID = 1;
    nid.uFlags = NIF_MESSAGE | NIF_ICON | NIF_TIP;
    nid.uCallbackMessage = WM_TRAY;
    nid.hIcon = icon;
    let max = nid.szTip.len() - 1; // keep the terminating NUL
    for (dst, src) in nid.szTip.iter_mut().zip(tip.encode_utf16().take(max)) {
        *dst = src;
    }
    nid
}

fn tooltip() -> String {
    with_state(|s| {
        let mut t = s.cb.title.clone();
        for l in (s.cb.lines)() {
            t.push('\n');
            t.push_str(&l);
        }
        t
    })
    .unwrap_or_default()
}

unsafe fn set_icon(hwnd: HWND, op: u32) {
    let tip = tooltip();
    if let Some(icon) = with_state(|s| s.icon) {
        Shell_NotifyIconW(op, &notify_data(hwnd, icon, &tip));
    }
}

unsafe fn show_menu(hwnd: HWND) {
    let Some((title, lines)) = with_state(|s| (s.cb.title.clone(), (s.cb.lines)())) else { return };
    let menu = CreatePopupMenu();
    let item = |flags, id: usize, text: &str| {
        let t = wide(text);
        AppendMenuW(menu, flags, id, t.as_ptr());
    };
    item(MF_STRING | MF_GRAYED, 0, &title);
    for l in &lines {
        item(MF_STRING | MF_GRAYED, 0, l);
    }
    AppendMenuW(menu, MF_SEPARATOR, 0, null());
    item(MF_STRING, ID_STATUS_PAGE, "Open status page");
    item(MF_STRING, ID_DATA_FOLDER, "Open data folder");
    AppendMenuW(menu, MF_SEPARATOR, 0, null());
    item(MF_STRING, ID_QUIT, "Quit PlasmaTrack");
    SetMenuDefaultItem(menu, ID_STATUS_PAGE as u32, 0);

    let mut pt = POINT { x: 0, y: 0 };
    GetCursorPos(&mut pt);
    SetForegroundWindow(hwnd); // so the menu closes when clicking elsewhere
    let cmd = TrackPopupMenu(menu, TPM_RETURNCMD | TPM_NONOTIFY | TPM_RIGHTBUTTON, pt.x, pt.y, 0, hwnd, null());
    PostMessageW(hwnd, WM_NULL, 0, 0);
    DestroyMenu(menu);
    match cmd as usize {
        ID_STATUS_PAGE => {
            with_state(|s| (s.cb.open_status)());
        }
        ID_DATA_FOLDER => {
            with_state(|s| (s.cb.open_data)());
        }
        ID_QUIT => request_quit(hwnd),
        _ => {}
    }
}

/// Asks the client to stop; the tray goes away when it has (WM_EXIT). If the
/// client does not stop within 10 s, the process exits anyway.
unsafe fn request_quit(hwnd: HWND) {
    let first = with_state(|s| !s.quitting.replace(true)).unwrap_or(false);
    if first {
        with_state(|s| (s.cb.quit)());
        SetTimer(hwnd, TIMER_FORCE_EXIT, 10_000, None);
    }
}

unsafe extern "system" fn wndproc(hwnd: HWND, msg: u32, wparam: WPARAM, lparam: LPARAM) -> LRESULT {
    match msg {
        WM_TRAY => {
            match lparam as u32 {
                WM_LBUTTONDBLCLK => {
                    with_state(|s| (s.cb.open_status)());
                }
                WM_RBUTTONUP | WM_CONTEXTMENU => show_menu(hwnd),
                _ => {}
            }
            0
        }
        WM_TIMER if wparam == TIMER_REFRESH => {
            set_icon(hwnd, NIM_MODIFY);
            0
        }
        WM_TIMER if wparam == TIMER_FORCE_EXIT => {
            if let Some(icon) = with_state(|s| s.icon) {
                Shell_NotifyIconW(NIM_DELETE, &notify_data(hwnd, icon, ""));
            }
            std::process::exit(0);
        }
        WM_CLOSE => {
            request_quit(hwnd);
            0
        }
        WM_EXIT => {
            KillTimer(hwnd, TIMER_REFRESH);
            if let Some(icon) = with_state(|s| s.icon) {
                Shell_NotifyIconW(NIM_DELETE, &notify_data(hwnd, icon, ""));
            }
            DestroyWindow(hwnd);
            0
        }
        WM_DESTROY => {
            PostQuitMessage(0);
            0
        }
        m if Some(m) == with_state(|s| s.taskbar_created) => {
            set_icon(hwnd, NIM_ADD); // Explorer restarted
            0
        }
        _ => DefWindowProcW(hwnd, msg, wparam, lparam),
    }
}

/// Shows the icon and runs the message loop until [`Exit::post`]. `started`
/// gets the exit handle once the window exists; start the client there.
pub fn run(cb: Callbacks, started: impl FnOnce(Exit)) -> Result<(), String> {
    unsafe {
        let hinstance = GetModuleHandleW(null());
        let class = wide("PlasmaTrackTray");
        let mut wc: WNDCLASSW = std::mem::zeroed();
        wc.lpfnWndProc = Some(wndproc);
        wc.hInstance = hinstance;
        wc.lpszClassName = class.as_ptr();
        if RegisterClassW(&wc) == 0 {
            return Err("cannot register the tray window class".into());
        }
        let title = wide("PlasmaTrack");
        let hwnd = CreateWindowExW(
            0,
            class.as_ptr(),
            title.as_ptr(),
            0,
            0,
            0,
            0,
            0,
            std::ptr::null_mut(),
            std::ptr::null_mut(),
            hinstance,
            null(),
        );
        if hwnd.is_null() {
            return Err("cannot create the tray window".into());
        }
        let icon = make_icon();
        let taskbar_created = RegisterWindowMessageW(wide("TaskbarCreated").as_ptr());
        STATE.with(|s| *s.borrow_mut() = Some(State { cb, icon, taskbar_created, quitting: Cell::new(false) }));
        set_icon(hwnd, NIM_ADD);
        SetTimer(hwnd, TIMER_REFRESH, 2000, None);

        started(Exit(hwnd as usize));

        let mut msg: MSG = std::mem::zeroed();
        while GetMessageW(&mut msg, std::ptr::null_mut(), 0, 0) > 0 {
            TranslateMessage(&msg);
            DispatchMessageW(&msg);
        }
        STATE.with(|s| s.borrow_mut().take());
        DestroyIcon(icon);
    }
    Ok(())
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    #[test]
    fn icon_is_a_disc_with_a_letter() {
        let px = super::icon_rgba();
        assert_eq!(px.len(), 32 * 32 * 4);
        let at = |x: usize, y: usize| &px[(y * 32 + x) * 4..(y * 32 + x) * 4 + 4];
        assert_eq!(at(0, 0)[3], 0, "corner transparent");
        assert_eq!(at(24, 24), [106, 61, 232, 255], "disc");
        assert_eq!(at(11, 20), [255, 255, 255, 255], "stem of the P");
    }
}
