`crates/pt-client/src/uninstall.rs`:

```rs
//! Removing PlasmaTrack from a PC, and its entry in Windows' "Installed apps".
//!
//! Three ways in, all running [`uninstall`]:
//! - `PlasmaTrack-Uninstall.exe` ([`gui_main`]), which anyone can download and
//!   which Windows starts from "Installed apps";
//! - `plasmatrack-client uninstall [--delete-data] [--json]`;
//! - PlasmaTrack Setup's Uninstall button, which runs that command.
//!
//! It works with nothing installed, and with only parts of an install left.

use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::time::Duration;

use serde::Serialize;

use crate::{paths, setup, steam, updater};

/// `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\PlasmaTrack`.
pub const UNINSTALL_KEY: &str = "Software\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Uninstall\\PlasmaTrack";
pub const RUN_KEY: &str = "Software\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Run";
pub const RUN_VALUE: &str = "PlasmaTrack";
/// The uninstaller's name in `bin`.
pub const UNINSTALLER_EXE: &str = "plasmatrack-uninstall.exe";
const CLIENT_PROCESSES: [&str; 2] = ["plasmatrack-clientw.exe", "plasmatrack-client.exe"];
/// Start menu shortcuts made by Setup.
const SHORTCUTS: [&str; 2] = ["PlasmaTrack.lnk", "Uninstall PlasmaTrack.lnk"];
/// What the updater leaves next to `bin` (updater.rs).
const LEFTOVERS: [&str; 5] = ["bin", "updates", "bin.new", "bin.old", "bin.failed"];

/// One thing done, as Setup shows it.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]
pub struct Step {
    pub ok: bool,
    pub text: String,
    pub detail: Option<String>,
}

fn step(ok: bool, text: impl Into<String>, detail: Option<String>) -> Step {
    Step { ok, text: text.into(), detail }
}

/// Where the config and data are.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Paths {
    pub config: PathBuf,
    pub data_dir: PathBuf,
}

impl Default for Paths {
    fn default() -> Paths {
        Paths { config: paths::default_config_path(), data_dir: paths::default_data_dir() }
    }
}

/// Asks a running client to quit through its status page, like
/// `plasmatrack-client stop`, without an HTTP library.
fn ask_to_quit(config: &Path) {
    use std::io::Write;
    let cfg = std::fs::read_to_string(config).ok().and_then(|t| pt_core::Config::from_toml_str(&t).ok());
    let (host, port) = cfg.map_or(("127.0.0.1".to_string(), 30456), |c| (c.local.listen_address, c.local.status_port));
    let Ok(addr) = format!("{host}:{port}").parse::<std::net::SocketAddr>() else { return };
    if let Ok(mut s) = std::net::TcpStream::connect_timeout(&addr, Duration::from_secs(1)) {
        let _ = s.set_read_timeout(Some(Duration::from_secs(2)));
        let (k, v) = crate::status::QUIT_HEADER;
        let _ = write!(s, "POST /quit HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: {host}\r\n{k}: {v}\r\nContent-Length: 0\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n");
        let _ = std::io::Read::read(&mut s, &mut [0u8; 256]);
    }
}

/// Stops every PlasmaTrack client: politely first, then by force.
fn stop_clients(config: &Path) -> Step {
    let running = || updater::processes(&CLIENT_PROCESSES).unwrap_or_default();
    if running().is_empty() {
        return step(true, "PlasmaTrack was not running", None);
    }
    ask_to_quit(config);
    for _ in 0..50 {
        if running().is_empty() {
            return step(true, "Stopped PlasmaTrack", None);
        }
        std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(100));
    }
    for pid in running() {
        kill(pid);
    }
    std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(500));
    match running().as_slice() {
        [] => step(true, "Stopped PlasmaTrack", None),
        left => step(false, "Could not stop PlasmaTrack", Some(format!("still running: process {left:?}"))),
    }
}

#[cfg(windows)]
fn kill(pid: u32) {
    use std::os::windows::process::CommandExt;
    const CREATE_NO_WINDOW: u32 = 0x0800_0000;
    let _ = std::process::Command::new("taskkill")
        .args(["/F", "/PID", &pid.to_string()])
        .creation_flags(CREATE_NO_WINDOW)
        .stdout(std::process::Stdio::null())
        .stderr(std::process::Stdio::null())
        .status();
}

#[cfg(not(windows))]
fn kill(pid: u32) {
    let _ = std::process::Command::new("kill").args(["-9", &pid.to_string()]).status();
}

/// Removes a folder of ours; a folder that is not there counts as removed.
fn remove_dir(dir: &Path) -> Result<bool, String> {
    match std::fs::remove_dir_all(dir) {
        Ok(()) => Ok(true),
        Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => Ok(false),
        Err(e) => Err(format!("{}: {e}", dir.display())),
    }
}

/// Only folders named like ours are deleted wholesale, whatever a path
/// argument says.
fn ours(dir: &Path) -> bool {
    dir.file_name().is_some_and(|n| n.to_string_lossy().eq_ignore_ascii_case("plasmatrack"))
}

#[cfg(windows)]
fn start_menu() -> Option<PathBuf> {
    dirs::config_dir().map(|d| d.join("Microsoft").join("Windows").join("Start Menu").join("Programs"))
}

#[cfg(windows)]
fn unregister_windows() -> Vec<Step> {
    use winreg::enums::{HKEY_CURRENT_USER, KEY_SET_VALUE};
    let hkcu = winreg::RegKey::predef(HKEY_CURRENT_USER);
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    if let Ok(run) = hkcu.open_subkey_with_flags(RUN_KEY, KEY_SET_VALUE) {
        if run.delete_value(RUN_VALUE).is_ok() {
            out.push(step(true, "Removed PlasmaTrack from startup", None));
        }
    }
    let mut links = 0;
    for name in SHORTCUTS {
        if let Some(p) = start_menu().map(|d| d.join(name)) {
            links += std::fs::remove_file(p).is_ok() as usize;
        }
    }
    if links > 0 {
        out.push(step(true, "Removed PlasmaTrack from the Start menu", None));
    }
    if hkcu.delete_subkey_all(UNINSTALL_KEY).is_ok() {
        out.push(step(true, "Removed PlasmaTrack from Installed apps", None));
    }
    out
}

#[cfg(not(windows))]
fn unregister_windows() -> Vec<Step> {
    Vec::new()
}

/// Removes everything PlasmaTrack put on this PC. Local data, settings and the
/// token stay unless `delete_data`. Every step runs even when an earlier one
/// failed; the caller shows the list.
pub fn uninstall(p: &Paths, delete_data: bool) -> Vec<Step> {
    let mut steps = vec![stop_clients(&p.config)];
    steps.extend(unregister_windows());

    let folders = setup::uninstall_plugin(&steam::discover());
    for f in folders.iter().filter(|f| f.changed || f.error.is_some()) {
        let game = match f.game {
            pt_core::Game::Ats => "American Truck Simulator",
            pt_core::Game::Ets2 => "Euro Truck Simulator 2",
        };
        steps.push(match &f.error {
            None => step(true, format!("Removed the plugin from {game}"), Some(f.plugins_dir.display().to_string())),
            Some(e) => step(false, format!("Could not remove the plugin from {game}"), Some(e.clone())),
        });
    }

    steps.extend(remove_files(p, delete_data));
    steps
}

/// The file part of [`uninstall`]: program files, and local data when asked.
/// It touches nothing outside `p` (the tests run it).
pub fn remove_files(p: &Paths, delete_data: bool) -> Vec<Step> {
    let mut steps = Vec::new();
    let mut removed = false;
    for name in LEFTOVERS {
        match remove_dir(&p.data_dir.join(name)) {
            Ok(r) => removed |= r,
            Err(e) => steps.push(step(false, format!("Could not remove PlasmaTrack's {name} folder"), Some(e))),
        }
    }
    if removed {
        steps.push(step(true, "Removed the PlasmaTrack program files", Some(p.data_dir.join("bin").display().to_string())));
    }

    if delete_data {
        let config_dir = p.config.parent().map(Path::to_path_buf);
        for dir in [Some(p.data_dir.clone()), config_dir].into_iter().flatten() {
            let result = if ours(&dir) { remove_dir(&dir).map(|_| ()) } else { Err(format!("{} is not a PlasmaTrack folder", dir.display())) };
            if let Err(e) = result {
                steps.push(step(false, "Could not delete all local data", Some(e)));
            }
        }
        if ours(&p.data_dir) && !p.data_dir.exists() {
            steps.push(step(true, "Deleted local data, settings and the token", None));
        }
    } else if p.data_dir.exists() || p.config.exists() {
        steps.push(step(
            true,
            "Kept local data and settings",
            Some(format!("{} and {}", p.data_dir.display(), p.config.display())),
        ));
    }
    steps
}

/// Adds or refreshes PlasmaTrack in "Installed apps" (Setup, and every update):
/// the uninstaller in `bin`, the version, the size.
#[cfg(windows)]
pub fn register(bin: &Path, version: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
    use winreg::enums::HKEY_CURRENT_USER;
    let (key, _) = winreg::RegKey::predef(HKEY_CURRENT_USER).create_subkey(UNINSTALL_KEY).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    let uninstaller = bin.join(UNINSTALLER_EXE);
    let size_kb: u64 = std::fs::read_dir(bin).into_iter().flatten().flatten().filter_map(|e| e.metadata().ok()).map(|m| m.len()).sum::<u64>() / 1024;
    let s = |name: &str, v: &str| key.set_value(name, &v.to_string()).map_err(|e| e.to_string());
    let d = |name: &str, v: u32| key.set_value(name, &v).map_err(|e| e.to_string());
    s("DisplayName", "PlasmaTrack")?;
    s("DisplayVersion", version)?;
    s("Publisher", "PlasmaTrack")?;
    s("DisplayIcon", &bin.join("plasmatrack-clientw.exe").display().to_string())?;
    s("InstallLocation", &bin.display().to_string())?;
    s("UninstallString", &format!("\"{}\"", uninstaller.display()))?;
    s("QuietUninstallString", &format!("\"{}\" --quiet", uninstaller.display()))?;
    d("EstimatedSize", size_kb.min(u32::MAX as u64) as u32)?;
    d("NoModify", 1)?;
    d("NoRepair", 1)?;
    Ok(())
}

#[cfg(not(windows))]
pub fn register(_bin: &Path, _version: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
    Ok(())
}

#[cfg(windows)]
mod gui {
    use windows_sys::Win32::UI::WindowsAndMessaging::{
        MessageBoxW, IDRETRY, IDYES, MB_DEFBUTTON2, MB_ICONERROR, MB_ICONINFORMATION, MB_ICONQUESTION, MB_ICONWARNING, MB_OK,
        MB_RETRYCANCEL, MB_YESNO,
    };

    fn wide(s: &str) -> Vec<u16> {
        s.encode_utf16().chain(std::iter::once(0)).collect()
    }

    fn show(text: &str, flags: u32) -> i32 {
        let (text, title) = (wide(text), wide("Uninstall PlasmaTrack"));
        // SAFETY: both strings are NUL-terminated and outlive the call.
        unsafe { MessageBoxW(std::ptr::null_mut(), text.as_ptr(), title.as_ptr(), flags) }
    }

    pub fn yes(text: &str, default_no: bool) -> bool {
        show(text, MB_YESNO | MB_ICONQUESTION | if default_no { MB_DEFBUTTON2 } else { 0 }) == IDYES
    }

    pub fn retry(text: &str) -> bool {
        show(text, MB_RETRYCANCEL | MB_ICONWARNING) == IDRETRY
    }

    pub fn info(text: &str, failed: bool) {
        show(text, MB_OK | if failed { MB_ICONERROR } else { MB_ICONINFORMATION });
    }
}

/// When this program runs from the `bin` folder it is about to delete, it
/// continues from a copy in the temp folder instead.
#[cfg(windows)]
fn relocate(data_dir: &Path) -> Option<std::process::ExitCode> {
    use std::os::windows::process::CommandExt;
    let exe = std::env::current_exe().ok()?;
    let inside = exe.parent().zip(data_dir.join("bin").canonicalize().ok()).is_some_and(|(p, bin)| p.canonicalize().is_ok_and(|p| p == bin));
    if !inside {
        return None;
    }
    let copy = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("PlasmaTrack-Uninstall-{}.exe", std::process::id()));
    std::fs::copy(&exe, &copy).ok()?;
    const DETACHED_PROCESS: u32 = 0x0000_0008;
    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().skip(1).chain(std::iter::once("--relocated".to_string())).collect();
    std::process::Command::new(&copy).args(args).creation_flags(DETACHED_PROCESS).spawn().ok()?;
    Some(std::process::ExitCode::SUCCESS)
}

/// `PlasmaTrack-Uninstall.exe [--quiet] [--delete-data]`: asks, removes, and
/// says what it did. `--quiet` asks nothing and keeps local data unless
/// `--delete-data` is given.
#[cfg(windows)]
pub fn gui_main() -> std::process::ExitCode {
    use std::process::ExitCode;
    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().skip(1).collect();
    let has = |a: &str| args.iter().any(|x| x == a);
    let quiet = has("--quiet");
    let p = Paths::default();
    if !has("--relocated") {
        if let Some(code) = relocate(&p.data_dir) {
            return code;
        }
    }
    if !quiet
        && !gui::yes(
            "Remove PlasmaTrack from this PC?\n\nThis stops PlasmaTrack, removes its plugin from Euro Truck Simulator 2 and \
             American Truck Simulator, and removes it from startup and the Start menu.",
            false,
        )
    {
        return ExitCode::SUCCESS;
    }
    while updater::games_running() {
        if quiet || !gui::retry("Close Euro Truck Simulator 2 and American Truck Simulator first, then choose Retry.") {
            return ExitCode::FAILURE;
        }
    }
    let delete_data = has("--delete-data")
        || (!quiet
            && gui::yes(
                "Also delete PlasmaTrack's local data and settings, including your token?\n\nJobs already uploaded stay on the \
                 server. Choose No to keep them for a later reinstall.",
                true,
            ));
    let steps = uninstall(&p, delete_data);
    let failed: Vec<&Step> = steps.iter().filter(|s| !s.ok).collect();
    if !quiet {
        let text = if failed.is_empty() {
            "PlasmaTrack was removed from this PC.".to_string()
        } else {
            let lines: Vec<String> =
                failed.iter().map(|s| format!("• {}{}", s.text, s.detail.as_ref().map(|d| format!(": {d}")).unwrap_or_default())).collect();
            format!("PlasmaTrack was removed, except:\n\n{}\n\nClose the games and run this again.", lines.join("\n"))
        };
        gui::info(&text, !failed.is_empty());
    }
    if failed.is_empty() {
        ExitCode::SUCCESS
    } else {
        ExitCode::FAILURE
    }
}

#[cfg(not(windows))]
pub fn gui_main() -> std::process::ExitCode {
    let steps = uninstall(&Paths::default(), std::env::args().any(|a| a == "--delete-data"));
    println!("{}", serde_json::to_string_pretty(&steps).unwrap_or_default());
    if steps.iter().all(|s| s.ok) {
        std::process::ExitCode::SUCCESS
    } else {
        std::process::ExitCode::FAILURE
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn removes_program_files_and_keeps_or_deletes_data() {
```

`crates/pt-client/src/updater.rs`:

```rs
//! Automatic updates (docs/UPDATES.md).
//!
//! The windowless client asks the server for a newer release every few hours.
//! It downloads the release's files into `updates/<version>` in the data
//! directory, checking each against the update manifest, which must carry a
//! signature by a release key built into this client (`pt_core::update`).
//! Once no game is running, it starts `plasmatrack-clientw apply-update` from
//! that folder and quits. The new program then swaps the `bin` folder,
//! carries the player's `[local]` settings into the config it ships, copies the
//! plugin into every game that has it, and starts the new client. If the new
//! client does not come up, the old `bin` folder is put back.

use std::io::Read;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::time::Duration;

use pt_core::update::{self, UpdateManifest, DOWNLOAD_PATH, UPDATE_PATH};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};

use crate::{log, setup, steam};

pub const UPDATES_DIR: &str = "updates";
/// The update manifest and its signature, kept next to the staged files.
pub const STAGED_MANIFEST: &str = "update.json";
pub const STAGED_SIGNATURE: &str = "update.sig";
/// Written by `apply-update` for the new client to announce, then removed.
pub const UPDATED_FILE: &str = "updated.json";
/// Written when an update could not be installed; that version is not tried
/// again for [`RETRY_FAILED`].
pub const FAILED_FILE: &str = "update-failed.json";
pub const RETRY_FAILED: Duration = Duration::from_secs(6 * 3600);
pub const GAME_PROCESSES: [&str; 2] = ["eurotrucks2.exe", "amtrucks.exe"];
pub const PLATFORM: &str = if cfg!(windows) { "windows" } else { "linux" };

/// An update the server offers, with its signature checked.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Offer {
    pub manifest: UpdateManifest,
    pub text: String,
    pub signature: String,
}

#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct OfferBody {
    update: Option<OfferJson>,
}

#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct OfferJson {
    manifest: String,
    signature: String,
}

#[derive(Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Outcome {
    pub version: String,
    pub from: String,
    pub at_ms: i64,
    pub error: Option<String>,
}

pub fn newer(version: &str, than: &str) -> bool {
    match (update::parse_version(version), update::parse_version(than)) {
        (Some(a), Some(b)) => a > b,
        _ => false,
    }
}

fn hex_sha256(bytes: &[u8]) -> String {
    Sha256::digest(bytes).iter().map(|b| format!("{b:02x}")).collect()
}

/// Asks the server whether there is something newer than `current`.
pub async fn fetch_offer(http: &reqwest::Client, server_url: &str, token: &str, current: &str, keys: &[[u8; 32]]) -> Result<Option<Offer>, String> {
    let url = format!("{}{UPDATE_PATH}?platform={PLATFORM}&version={current}", server_url.trim_end_matches('/'));
    let res = http.get(url).bearer_auth(token.trim()).send().await.map_err(|e| format!("update check: {e}"))?;
    if !res.status().is_success() {
        return Err(format!("update check: server returned {}", res.status()));
    }
    let text = res.text().await.map_err(|e| format!("update check: {e}"))?;
    let body: OfferBody = serde_json::from_str(&text).map_err(|e| format!("update check: {e}"))?;
    let Some(o) = body.update else { return Ok(None) };
    let manifest = update::verify_with(&o.manifest, &o.signature, keys).map_err(|e| format!("update refused: {e}"))?;
    if manifest.platform != PLATFORM || !newer(&manifest.version, current) {
        return Err(format!("update refused: {} {} is not newer for {PLATFORM}", manifest.platform, manifest.version));
    }
    Ok(Some(Offer { manifest, text: o.manifest, signature: o.signature }))
}

fn file_matches(path: &Path, f: &update::UpdateFile) -> bool {
    std::fs::metadata(path).is_ok_and(|m| m.len() == f.size) && crate::manifest::sha256_file(path).is_ok_and(|h| h == f.sha256)
}

/// Downloads every file of the offer into `updates_dir/<version>`; files
/// already there with the right hash are kept, so an interrupted download
/// resumes. The manifest and signature are written last: their presence means
/// the folder is complete.
pub async fn stage(http: &reqwest::Client, server_url: &str, token: &str, offer: &Offer, updates_dir: &Path) -> Result<PathBuf, String> {
    let m = &offer.manifest;
    let dir = updates_dir.join(&m.version);
    let io = |e: std::io::Error| format!("{}: {e}", dir.display());
    let _ = std::fs::remove_file(dir.join(STAGED_MANIFEST));
    for f in &m.files {
        let dest = f.local_path(&dir);
        if file_matches(&dest, f) {
            continue;
        }
        let url = format!("{}{DOWNLOAD_PATH}{}", server_url.trim_end_matches('/'), m.key(f));
        let res = http.get(&url).bearer_auth(token.trim()).send().await.map_err(|e| format!("{url}: {e}"))?;
        if !res.status().is_success() {
            return Err(format!("{url}: server returned {}", res.status()));
        }
        if res.content_length().is_some_and(|n| n != f.gz_size) {
            return Err(format!("{url}: unexpected size"));
        }
        let gz = res.bytes().await.map_err(|e| format!("{url}: {e}"))?;
        if gz.len() as u64 != f.gz_size {
            return Err(format!("{url}: {} bytes, expected {}", gz.len(), f.gz_size));
        }
        let mut data = Vec::with_capacity(f.size as usize);
        flate2::read::GzDecoder::new(&gz[..]).take(f.size + 1).read_to_end(&mut data).map_err(|e| format!("{url}: {e}"))?;
        if data.len() as u64 != f.size || hex_sha256(&data) != f.sha256 {
            return Err(format!("{}: does not match the signed manifest", f.path));
        }
        if let Some(parent) = dest.parent() {
            std::fs::create_dir_all(parent).map_err(io)?;
        }
        let part = dest.with_extension("part");
        std::fs::write(&part, &data).map_err(io)?;
        std::fs::rename(&part, &dest).map_err(io)?;
    }
    std::fs::write(dir.join(STAGED_SIGNATURE), &offer.signature).map_err(io)?;
    std::fs::write(dir.join(STAGED_MANIFEST), &offer.text).map_err(io)?;
    Ok(dir)
}

/// A complete staged update in `dir`: signature good, every file present and
/// unchanged.
pub fn verify_staged(dir: &Path, keys: &[[u8; 32]]) -> Result<UpdateManifest, String> {
    let read = |name: &str| std::fs::read_to_string(dir.join(name)).map_err(|e| format!("{}: {e}", dir.join(name).display()));
    let m = update::verify_with(&read(STAGED_MANIFEST)?, &read(STAGED_SIGNATURE)?, keys).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    for f in &m.files {
        if !file_matches(&f.local_path(dir), f) {
            return Err(format!("{} is missing or changed", f.path));
        }
    }
    Ok(m)
}

/// The newest complete staged update newer than `current`.
pub fn staged(updates_dir: &Path, current: &str, keys: &[[u8; 32]]) -> Option<(PathBuf, UpdateManifest)> {
    let mut found: Vec<(PathBuf, UpdateManifest)> = std::fs::read_dir(updates_dir)
        .ok()?
        .flatten()
        .map(|e| e.path())
        .filter(|p| p.join(STAGED_MANIFEST).is_file())
        .filter_map(|p| verify_staged(&p, keys).ok().map(|m| (p, m)))
        .filter(|(_, m)| m.platform == PLATFORM && newer(&m.version, current))
        .collect();
    found.sort_by_key(|(_, m)| update::parse_version(&m.version));
    found.pop()
}

/// Removes staged updates that are not newer than `current` (installed, or
/// superseded).
pub fn clean(updates_dir: &Path, current: &str) {
    for e in std::fs::read_dir(updates_dir).into_iter().flatten().flatten() {
        let name = e.file_name().to_string_lossy().to_string();
        if update::parse_version(&name).is_some() && !newer(&name, current) {
            let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(e.path());
        }
    }
}

/// IDs of running processes with one of these (lowercase) file names, except
/// this one. `None` when the process list cannot be read.
#[cfg(windows)]
pub fn processes(names: &[&str]) -> Option<Vec<u32>> {
    use windows_sys::Win32::Foundation::{CloseHandle, INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE};
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::Diagnostics::ToolHelp::{
        CreateToolhelp32Snapshot, Process32FirstW, Process32NextW, PROCESSENTRY32W, TH32CS_SNAPPROCESS,
    };
    let me = std::process::id();
    // SAFETY: a process snapshot is walked with a correctly sized entry and closed.
    unsafe {
        let snap = CreateToolhelp32Snapshot(TH32CS_SNAPPROCESS, 0);
        if snap == INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE {
            return None;
        }
        let mut e: PROCESSENTRY32W = std::mem::zeroed();
        e.dwSize = std::mem::size_of::<PROCESSENTRY32W>() as u32;
        let mut found = Vec::new();
        let mut more = Process32FirstW(snap, &mut e) != 0;
        while more {
            let len = e.szExeFile.iter().position(|&c| c == 0).unwrap_or(e.szExeFile.len());
            let name = String::from_utf16_lossy(&e.szExeFile[..len]).to_ascii_lowercase();
            if names.contains(&name.as_str()) && e.th32ProcessID != me {
                found.push(e.th32ProcessID);
            }
            more = Process32NextW(snap, &mut e) != 0;
        }
        CloseHandle(snap);
        Some(found)
    }
}

/// Linux: the same question asked of `/proc`. Under Proton the games are Wine
/// processes, so the Windows file name has to be recognised in a Linux process.
/// Per process, `/proc/<pid>/comm` is the kernel name (Wine sets it to the .exe
/// name, cut to 15 bytes: "eurotrucks2.exe" just fits) and `/proc/<pid>/cmdline`
/// is NUL-separated argv, where Wine's argv[0] is a Windows path such as
/// `Z:\home\me\...\bin\win_x64\eurotrucks2.exe` (backslashes, any letter case).
#[cfg(not(windows))]
pub fn processes(names: &[&str]) -> Option<Vec<u32>> {
    let me = std::process::id();
    let mut found = Vec::new();
    for entry in std::fs::read_dir("/proc").ok()? {
        let Some(pid) = entry.ok().and_then(|e| e.file_name().to_str()?.parse::<u32>().ok()) else { continue };
        if pid == me {
            continue;
        }
        let dir = Path::new("/proc").join(pid.to_string());
        // A process can exit between read_dir and these reads; it then just doesn't match.
        let comm = std::fs::read_to_string(dir.join("comm")).unwrap_or_default();
        let cmdline = std::fs::read(dir.join("cmdline")).unwrap_or_default();
        if process_matches(&comm, &cmdline, names) {
            found.push(pid);
        }
    }
    Some(found)
}

/// Whether a process with this `comm` and raw `cmdline` is one of `names`: by the
/// last component of argv[0] (split on `/` and `\`), or by the kernel name, which
/// is a prefix of a longer name when the kernel cut it to 15 bytes. Never by a
/// later argument, so `grep eurotrucks2.exe` is not the game.
#[cfg(not(windows))]
fn process_matches(comm: &str, cmdline: &[u8], names: &[&str]) -> bool {
    let argv0 = String::from_utf8_lossy(cmdline.split(|&b| b == 0).next().unwrap_or_default());
    let exe = argv0.rsplit(['/', '\\']).next().unwrap_or_default().to_ascii_lowercase();
    let comm = comm.trim_end_matches('\n').to_ascii_lowercase();
    names.iter().map(|n| n.to_ascii_lowercase()).any(|n| {
        (!exe.is_empty() && exe == n) || comm == n || (comm.len() == 15 && n.len() > 15 && n.starts_with(&comm))
    })
}

/// True while ETS2 or ATS runs (their plugin DLL cannot be replaced then).
/// When the process list cannot be read, it says yes, to be safe.
pub fn games_running() -> bool {
    processes(&GAME_PROCESSES).is_none_or(|p| !p.is_empty())
}

/// The client's `bin` folder when this program runs from the installed one
/// (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\PlasmaTrack\bin`). Only then does it update itself.
pub fn installed_bin(data_dir: &Path) -> Option<PathBuf> {
    let exe = std::env::current_exe().ok()?;
    let bin = exe.parent()?.to_path_buf();
    let expected = data_dir.join("bin");
    let same = match (bin.canonicalize(), expected.canonicalize()) {
        (Ok(a), Ok(b)) => a == b,
        _ => false,
    };
    (same && cfg!(windows)).then_some(bin)
}

/// Builds the new `bin` from the staged files (and the `manifest.json` the
/// installer would write), then swaps it in. Returns where the old one went.
/// Renaming `bin` fails while any program in it runs, so this retries for a
/// while after the old client quit.
pub fn swap_bin(staged: &Path, m: &UpdateManifest, bin: &Path) -> Result<PathBuf, String> {
    let parent = bin.parent().ok_or("bin has no parent folder")?;
    let new = parent.join("bin.new");
    let old = parent.join("bin.old");
    let io = |what: &str, e: std::io::Error| format!("{what}: {e}");
    let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&new);
    let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&old);
    std::fs::create_dir_all(&new).map_err(|e| io("bin.new", e))?;
    let mut listing = serde_json::Map::new();
    for f in &m.files {
        let dest = f.local_path(&new);
        if let Some(p) = dest.parent() {
            std::fs::create_dir_all(p).map_err(|e| io("bin.new", e))?;
        }
        std::fs::copy(f.local_path(staged), &dest).map_err(|e| io(&f.path, e))?;
        listing.insert(f.path.clone(), f.sha256.clone().into());
    }
    let listing = serde_json::to_string_pretty(&listing).unwrap_or_default() + "\n";
    std::fs::write(new.join("manifest.json"), listing).map_err(|e| io("manifest.json", e))?;
    if !verify_copy(&new, m) {
        return Err("the copied files do not match the update".into());
    }
    let mut last = String::new();
    for _ in 0..40 {
        match std::fs::rename(bin, &old) {
            Ok(()) => {
                return match std::fs::rename(&new, bin) {
                    Ok(()) => Ok(old),
                    Err(e) => {
                        let _ = std::fs::rename(&old, bin);
                        Err(io("installing the new bin", e))
                    }
                };
            }
            Err(e) => last = e.to_string(),
        }
        std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(500));
    }
    Err(format!("bin is still in use: {last}"))
}

fn verify_copy(dir: &Path, m: &UpdateManifest) -> bool {
    m.files.iter().all(|f| file_matches(&f.local_path(dir), f))
}

/// Puts the old `bin` back after a failed update.
pub fn restore_bin(bin: &Path, old: &Path) -> Result<(), String> {
    let failed = bin.with_file_name("bin.failed");
    let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&failed);
    for _ in 0..20 {
        if std::fs::rename(bin, &failed).is_ok() || !bin.exists() {
            return std::fs::rename(old, bin).map_err(|e| format!("restoring bin: {e}"));
        }
        std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(500));
    }
    Err("bin is in use; could not restore the previous version".into())
}

/// Copies the plugin in `bin` into every game where a different PlasmaTrack
/// plugin is installed. Games without the plugin are left alone (the player
/// may have removed it). Skipped while a game runs.
pub fn sync_plugins(bin: &Path, ini: &[(&str, String)]) -> Vec<setup::FolderResult> {
    let dll = bin.join(steam::PLUGIN_FILE_WINDOWS);
    if !dll.is_file() || games_running() {
        return Vec::new();
    }
    let Ok(want) = crate::manifest::sha256_file(&dll) else { return Vec::new() };
    let stale: Vec<steam::GameInstall> = steam::discover()
        .into_iter()
        .filter(|i| i.windows_build && i.plugin_path().is_file())
        .filter(|i| crate::manifest::sha256_file(&i.plugin_path()).ok().as_deref() != Some(want.as_str()))
        .collect();
    if stale.is_empty() {
        return Vec::new();
    }
    let results = setup::install_plugin(&stale, &dll, ini);
    for r in &results {
        match &r.error {
            None => log!("plugin updated in {}", r.plugins_dir.display()),
            Some(e) => log!("plugin not updated in {}: {e}", r.plugins_dir.display()),
        }
    }
    results
}

pub fn read_outcome(path: &Path) -> Option<Outcome> {
    serde_json::from_str(&std::fs::read_to_string(path).ok()?).ok()
}

pub fn write_outcome(path: &Path, o: &Outcome) {
    let _ = std::fs::write(path, serde_json::to_string(o).unwrap_or_default());
}

/// Whether `version` failed to install recently (see [`FAILED_FILE`]).
pub fn failed_recently(data_dir: &Path, version: &str, now_ms: i64) -> Option<String> {
    let o = read_outcome(&data_dir.join(FAILED_FILE))?;
    (o.version == version && now_ms - o.at_ms < RETRY_FAILED.as_millis() as i64).then(|| o.error.unwrap_or_default())
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[cfg(not(windows))]
    #[test]
    fn linux_process_names_match_wine_games() {
        let games = ["eurotrucks2.exe", "amtrucks.exe"];
        let wine_argv = b"Z:\\home\\me\\Euro Truck Simulator 2\\bin\\win_x64\\eurotrucks2.exe\0-homedir\0x\0";
        assert!(process_matches("eurotrucks2.exe\n", wine_argv, &games));
        // Seen live 2026-11-15 (tinkergame + proton-cachyos): Proton's S: game drive, and
        // /proc/<pid>/exe is Wine's preloader, so only argv[0] / comm name the game.
        let seen = b"S:\\steamapps\\common\\Euro Truck Simulator 2\\bin\\win_x64\\eurotrucks2.exe\0";
        assert!(process_matches("eurotrucks2.exe\n", seen, &games));
        assert!(process_matches("wine-preloader\n", seen, &games), "argv[0] alone is enough");
        assert!(process_matches("wine64-preload\n", b"C:\\Games\\AMTRUCKS.EXE\0", &games), "argv[0], any case");
        assert!(process_matches("amtrucks.exe\n", b"", &games), "kernel name alone (cmdline unreadable)");
        assert!(!process_matches("grep\n", b"/usr/bin/grep\0eurotrucks2.exe\0", &games), "a later argument is not the process");
        assert!(!process_matches("eurotrucks2.ex\n", b"", &games), "a shorter kernel name is not a cut one");
        assert!(process_matches("plasmatrack-cli\n", b"", &["plasmatrack-client"]), "15-byte kernel names are prefixes");
        // Whatever names GAME_PROCESSES holds must match their own (cut) kernel name.
        for n in GAME_PROCESSES {
            let comm: String = n.chars().take(15).collect();
            assert!(process_matches(&format!("{comm}\n"), b"", &[n]), "{n}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn compares_versions() {
        assert!(newer("0.2.0", "0.1.1"));
        assert!(newer("0.10.0", "0.9.0"));
        assert!(!newer("0.2.0", "0.2.0"));
        assert!(!newer("garbage", "0.1.0"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn cleans_installed_and_older_versions_only() {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        for v in ["0.1.0", "0.2.0", "0.3.0", "notes"] {
            std::fs::create_dir_all(dir.path().join(v)).unwrap();
        }
        clean(dir.path(), "0.2.0");
        let mut left: Vec<String> = std::fs::read_dir(dir.path()).unwrap().map(|e| e.unwrap().file_name().to_string_lossy().to_string()).collect();
        left.sort();
        assert_eq!(left, ["0.3.0", "notes"]);
    }
}
```

`crates/pt-client/src/uploader.rs`:

```rs
//! Uploads raw frames to the server (`POST /api/v1/chunks`). A failed upload is
//! retried at a fixed interval (`[sync] retry_interval_wall_s`, 20 s by default)
//! forever, until it succeeds; unsent frames stay queued in SQLite, so this
//! survives restarts of the client and the PC.

use std::io::Write;
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
use std::time::Duration;

use flate2::write::GzEncoder;
use flate2::Compression;
use pt_core::config::Multiplayer;
use pt_core::upload::{ManifestEntry, UploadAck, UploadChunk, CHUNKS_PATH, UPLOAD_PROTOCOL};
use pt_core::wire::redact_modules;
use serde_json::value::RawValue;

use crate::db::{Db, PendingChunk};
use crate::log;
use crate::status::SharedStatus;

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct UploaderConfig {
    pub server_url: String,
    pub token: String,
    pub retry_interval: Duration,
    /// How often to look for new frames when the queue is empty.
    pub idle_poll: Duration,
    /// Frames wait this long to be sent together, unless a chunk is full or
    /// carries a game event (owner, 2026-10-16: sending every few frames made
    /// 60-145 requests a minute per driver, which capped the server at about
    /// 50-100 drivers at once).
    pub batch_interval: Duration,
    pub max_frames: usize,
    pub max_bytes: usize,
    /// What `modules` messages keep when they are redacted.
    pub multiplayer: Multiplayer,
    pub config_hash: String,
    pub config_canonical_json: String,
}

impl UploaderConfig {
    pub fn is_configured(&self) -> bool {
        !self.token.trim().is_empty() && !self.server_url.contains(".invalid")
    }
}

/// Builds the request body for one pending chunk (modules redacted).
pub fn build_chunk(cfg: &UploaderConfig, pending: &PendingChunk, manifest: &[ManifestEntry]) -> Result<UploadChunk, String> {
    let raw = |s: String| RawValue::from_string(s).map_err(|e| e.to_string());
    Ok(UploadChunk {
        protocol: UPLOAD_PROTOCOL,
        client_version: crate::CLIENT_VERSION.to_string(),
        sess: pending.sess.clone(),
        hello: pending.hello.clone().map(raw).transpose()?,
        seq_from: pending.seq_from,
        seq_to: pending.seq_to,
        frames: pending
            .frames
            .iter()
            .map(|f| raw(redact_modules(f, &cfg.multiplayer)))
            .collect::<Result<_, _>>()?,
        config_hash: cfg.config_hash.clone(),
        config: raw(cfg.config_canonical_json.clone())?,
        manifest: manifest.to_vec(),
    })
}

pub fn gzip(bytes: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut enc = GzEncoder::new(Vec::new(), Compression::default());
    enc.write_all(bytes).expect("in-memory write");
    enc.finish().expect("in-memory finish")
}

async fn post(client: &reqwest::Client, cfg: &UploaderConfig, chunk: &UploadChunk) -> Result<UploadAck, String> {
    let body = gzip(&serde_json::to_vec(chunk).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?);
    let url = format!("{}{}", cfg.server_url.trim_end_matches('/'), CHUNKS_PATH);
    let resp = client
        .post(url)
        .bearer_auth(cfg.token.trim())
        .header(reqwest::header::CONTENT_TYPE, "application/json")
        .header(reqwest::header::CONTENT_ENCODING, "gzip")
        .body(body)
        .send()
        .await
        .map_err(|e| format!("request failed: {e}"))?;
    let code = resp.status();
    let text = resp.text().await.map_err(|e| format!("reading response: {e}"))?;
    if !code.is_success() {
        return Err(format!("server returned {code}: {}", text.chars().take(200).collect::<String>()));
    }
    let ack: UploadAck = serde_json::from_str(&text).map_err(|e| format!("bad ack: {e}"))?;
    if ack.sess != chunk.sess || ack.accepted_through < chunk.seq_from {
        return Err(format!("ack does not cover the chunk: {ack:?}"));
    }
    Ok(ack)
}

/// Runs forever. `manifest` is refreshed by the caller when files change.
pub async fn run(cfg: UploaderConfig, db: Arc<Mutex<Db>>, status: SharedStatus, manifest: Arc<Mutex<Vec<ManifestEntry>>>) {
    let client = reqwest::Client::builder()
        .timeout(Duration::from_secs(60))
        .user_agent(format!("plasmatrack-client/{}", crate::CLIENT_VERSION))
        .build()
        .expect("HTTP client");
    status.lock().expect("status").upload_configured = cfg.is_configured();

    loop {
        let next = {
            let db = db.clone();
            let (max_frames, max_bytes) = (cfg.max_frames, cfg.max_bytes);
            tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || -> rusqlite::Result<Option<PendingChunk>> {
                let db = db.lock().expect("db");
                for sess in db.pending_sessions()? {
                    if let Some(c) = db.next_chunk(&sess, max_frames, max_bytes)? {
                        return Ok(Some(c));
                    }
                }
                Ok(None)
            })
            .await
        };
        let pending = match next {
            Ok(Ok(Some(p))) if p.full || p.urgent => p,
            Ok(Ok(Some(p))) => {
                let wait = cfg.batch_interval.as_millis() as i64 - (crate::now_ms() - p.oldest_ms);
                if wait > 0 {
                    tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(wait as u64).min(cfg.idle_poll)).await;
                    continue;
                }
                p
            }
            Ok(Ok(None)) => {
                tokio::time::sleep(cfg.idle_poll).await;
                continue;
            }
            Ok(Err(e)) => {
                log!("upload queue read failed: {e}");
                tokio::time::sleep(cfg.retry_interval).await;
                continue;
            }
            Err(e) => {
                log!("upload task failed: {e}");
                tokio::time::sleep(cfg.retry_interval).await;
                continue;
            }
        };

        let now = crate::now_ms();
        status.lock().expect("status").last_upload_attempt_ms = Some(now);
        let result = if cfg.is_configured() {
            let manifest = manifest.lock().expect("manifest").clone();
            match build_chunk(&cfg, &pending, &manifest) {
                Ok(chunk) => post(&client, &cfg, &chunk).await,
                Err(e) => Err(format!("building chunk: {e}")),
            }
        } else {
            Err("not configured: set [local] server_url and token".to_string())
        };

        match result {
            Ok(ack) => {
                let through = ack.accepted_through.min(pending.seq_to);
                let db = db.clone();
                let p = pending.clone();
                let _ = tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || {
                    let mut db = db.lock().expect("db");
                    db.mark_uploaded(&p.sess, through)?;
                    if through >= p.seq_to {
                        db.mark_notes_uploaded(&p.note_ids)?;
                    }
                    db.record_upload(&p.sess, p.seq_from, through, true, "ok", crate::now_ms())
                })
                .await;
                let mut st = status.lock().expect("status");
                st.last_upload_ok_ms = Some(crate::now_ms());
                st.last_upload_error = None;
            }
            Err(err) => {
                log!("upload of {} {}..{} failed: {err}; retrying in {:?}", pending.sess, pending.seq_from, pending.seq_to, cfg.retry_interval);
                {
                    let db = db.clone();
                    let p = pending.clone();
                    let detail = err.clone();
                    let _ = tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || {
                        db.lock().expect("db").record_upload(&p.sess, p.seq_from, p.seq_to, false, &detail, crate::now_ms())
                    })
                    .await;
                }
                status.lock().expect("status").last_upload_error = Some(err);
                tokio::time::sleep(cfg.retry_interval).await;
            }
        }
    }
}
```

`crates/pt-client/tests/e2e.rs`:

```rs
//! End-to-end: a fake plugin talks to the real listener over loopback, and the
//! real uploader sends everything to a fake server that fails at first.

use std::collections::BTreeMap;
use std::io::Read;
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

use axum::body::Bytes;
use axum::extract::State;
use axum::http::{HeaderMap, StatusCode};
use axum::routing::post;
use axum::Router;
use pt_client::db::Db;
use pt_client::status::Status;
use pt_client::uploader::UploaderConfig;
use pt_core::config::Multiplayer;
use pt_core::upload::{ManifestEntry, UploadAck, UploadChunk};
use pt_core::wire::{encode_frame, FrameDecoder};
use tokio::io::{AsyncReadExt, AsyncWriteExt};
use tokio::net::{TcpListener, TcpStream};

const S1: &str = "aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa";
const S0: &str = "0000000000000000000000000000000f"; // an older session replayed from the plugin journal
const TOKEN: &str = "player-token-123";
const RETRY: Duration = Duration::from_millis(300);
const FAIL_FIRST: usize = 2;

#[derive(Default)]
struct FakeServer {
    fail_first: usize,
    requests: Vec<Instant>,
    stored: BTreeMap<(String, u64), String>,
    chunks: Vec<(String, u64, u64, String, usize)>, // sess, from, to, config_hash, manifest entries
}

async fn chunks(State(srv): State<Arc<Mutex<FakeServer>>>, headers: HeaderMap, body: Bytes) -> (StatusCode, String) {
    let mut s = srv.lock().unwrap();
    s.requests.push(Instant::now());
    if s.requests.len() <= s.fail_first {
        return (StatusCode::SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE, "try later".into());
    }
    assert_eq!(headers["authorization"], format!("Bearer {TOKEN}"));
    assert_eq!(headers["content-encoding"], "gzip");
    let mut json = String::new();
    flate2::read::GzDecoder::new(&body[..]).read_to_string(&mut json).unwrap();
    let chunk: UploadChunk = serde_json::from_str(&json).unwrap();
    for f in &chunk.frames {
        let v: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(f.get()).unwrap();
        let seq = v["seq"].as_u64().unwrap();
        s.stored.insert((chunk.sess.clone(), seq), f.get().to_string());
    }
    s.chunks.push((chunk.sess.clone(), chunk.seq_from, chunk.seq_to, chunk.config_hash.clone(), chunk.manifest.len()));
    let ack = UploadAck { sess: chunk.sess, accepted_through: chunk.seq_to };
    (StatusCode::OK, serde_json::to_string(&ack).unwrap())
}

fn frame(sess: &str, kind: &str, seq: Option<u64>, extra: &str) -> Vec<u8> {
    let json = match seq {
        Some(s) => format!("{{\"v\":1,\"kind\":\"{kind}\",\"sess\":\"{sess}\",\"seq\":{s},\"wall_ms\":1{extra}}}"),
        None => format!("{{\"v\":1,\"kind\":\"{kind}\",\"sess\":\"{sess}\",\"wall_ms\":1{extra}}}"),
    };
    encode_frame(&json)
}

/// Acks received from the client on one connection (highest seq per session).
#[derive(Default)]
struct Acks {
    dec: FrameDecoder,
    max: BTreeMap<String, u64>,
}

/// Reads acks from the client until the one for `sess` reaches `seq`.
async fn wait_ack(stream: &mut TcpStream, acks: &mut Acks, sess: &str, seq: u64) {
    let deadline = Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(5);
    let mut buf = [0u8; 4096];
    loop {
        while let Some(f) = acks.dec.next_frame().unwrap() {
            let v: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(&f).unwrap();
            assert_eq!(v["kind"], "ack");
            let e = acks.max.entry(v["sess"].as_str().unwrap().to_string()).or_default();
            *e = (*e).max(v["seq"].as_u64().unwrap());
        }
        if acks.max.get(sess).is_some_and(|s| *s >= seq) {
            return;
        }
        assert!(Instant::now() < deadline, "no ack for {sess} {seq}");
        let n = tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(5), stream.read(&mut buf)).await.unwrap().unwrap();
        assert!(n > 0, "client closed the connection");
        acks.dec.push(&buf[..n]);
    }
}

#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 4)]
async fn plugin_to_client_to_server() {
    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let db = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Db::open(&dir.path().join("client.sqlite")).unwrap()));
    let status = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Status::default()));

    // Real listener on an ephemeral loopback port.
    let plugin_listener = TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0").await.unwrap();
    let plugin_addr = plugin_listener.local_addr().unwrap();
    tokio::spawn(pt_client::listener::serve(plugin_listener, db.clone(), status.clone(), None));

    // Fake server.
    let srv = Arc::new(Mutex::new(FakeServer { fail_first: FAIL_FIRST, ..Default::default() }));
    let app = Router::new().route("/api/v1/chunks", post(chunks)).with_state(srv.clone());
    let server_listener = TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0").await.unwrap();
    let server_url = format!("http://{}", server_listener.local_addr().unwrap());
    tokio::spawn(async move { axum::serve(server_listener, app).await.unwrap() });

    // Real uploader.
    let cfg = pt_core::Config::from_toml_str(pt_client::paths::SAMPLE_CONFIG).unwrap();
    let ucfg = UploaderConfig {
        server_url,
        token: TOKEN.into(),
        retry_interval: RETRY,
        idle_poll: Duration::from_millis(50),
        batch_interval: Duration::ZERO,
        max_frames: 25,
        max_bytes: 1 << 20,
        multiplayer: Multiplayer { truckersmp_module_names: vec!["core_atsmp.dll".into()], mods: vec![] },
        config_hash: cfg.integrity_hash(),
        config_canonical_json: cfg.integrity_canonical_json(),
    };
    let manifest = Arc::new(Mutex::new(vec![ManifestEntry { role: "plugin".into(), path: "p".into(), sha256: "00".into() }]));
    tokio::spawn(pt_client::uploader::run(ucfg, db.clone(), status.clone(), manifest));

    // ---- fake plugin, first connection --------------------------------------
    let mut conn = TcpStream::connect(plugin_addr).await.unwrap();
    let mut acks = Acks::default();
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    out.extend(frame(S1, "hello", None, ",\"last_seq\":0"));
    out.extend(frame(S1, "snapshot", None, ",\"paused\":true,\"configs\":[],\"last_sample\":null"));
    out.extend(frame(S0, "shutdown", Some(900), "")); // replayed from the journal of an older session
    out.extend(frame(S1, "init", Some(1), ",\"game_id\":\"ats\""));
    out.extend(frame(S1, "modules", Some(2), ",\"modules\":[\"KERNEL32.DLL\",\"Core_ATSMP.dll\",\"private-mod.dll\"]"));
    out.extend(frame(S1, "config", Some(3), ",\"id\":\"job\",\"attrs\":[]"));
    for s in (4..=60).filter(|s| *s != 51) {
        out.extend(frame(S1, "sample", Some(s), ",\"ch\":{\"truck.speed\":20.5}"));
    }
    // Split writes at awkward boundaries.
    for piece in out.chunks(777) {
        conn.write_all(piece).await.unwrap();
    }
    wait_ack(&mut conn, &mut acks, S1, 60).await;
    wait_ack(&mut conn, &mut acks, S0, 900).await;
    drop(conn);

    // ---- reconnect: plugin replays 55..=60 (unacked from its view) + new frames --
    let mut conn = TcpStream::connect(plugin_addr).await.unwrap();
    let mut acks = Acks::default();
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    out.extend(frame(S1, "hello", None, ",\"last_seq\":60"));
    for s in 55..=70 {
        out.extend(frame(S1, "sample", Some(s), ",\"ch\":{\"truck.speed\":21}"));
    }
    conn.write_all(&out).await.unwrap();
    wait_ack(&mut conn, &mut acks, S1, 70).await;

    // Local log: no duplicates, the dropped seq stays missing, game recorded.
    {
        let db = db.lock().unwrap();
        let seqs = db.frame_seqs(S1).unwrap();
        let expected: Vec<u64> = (1..=70).filter(|s| *s != 51).collect();
        assert_eq!(seqs, expected);
        assert_eq!(db.session_game(S1).unwrap().as_deref(), Some("ats"));
    }

    // ---- server receives everything despite the initial failures -------------
    let deadline = Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(20);
    loop {
        let done = {
            let s = srv.lock().unwrap();
            s.stored.len() == 69 + 1
        };
        if done && db.lock().unwrap().stats().unwrap().frames_pending_upload == 0 {
            break;
        }
        assert!(Instant::now() < deadline, "uploads did not complete");
        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50)).await;
    }

    let s = srv.lock().unwrap();
    // Fixed-interval retries after each failure.
    for w in s.requests.windows(2).take(FAIL_FIRST) {
        assert!(w[1] - w[0] >= RETRY - Duration::from_millis(20), "retry came after {:?}", w[1] - w[0]);
    }
    // Chunks respect max_frames and carry the config hash and manifest.
    assert!(s.chunks.iter().all(|c| c.2 - c.1 < 25 + 1 && c.3 == cfg.integrity_hash() && c.4 == 1));
    // Privacy: the module list never leaves the PC; only TruckersMP matches do.
    let modules = &s.stored[&(S1.to_string(), 2)];
    assert!(!modules.contains("private-mod.dll") && !modules.contains("KERNEL32"));
    assert!(modules.contains("\"truckersmp_matches\":[\"Core_ATSMP.dll\"]"));
    assert!(modules.contains("\"module_count\":3"));
    // Frames are byte-identical otherwise.
    assert!(s.stored[&(S1.to_string(), 70)].contains("\"truck.speed\":21"));
    assert!(s.stored.contains_key(&(S0.to_string(), 900)));

    let st = status.lock().unwrap();
    assert!(st.last_upload_ok_ms.is_some());
    assert!(st.frames_received >= 70);
}

/// Frames wait for the batch interval and go together; a game event (a
/// delivery) goes at once (owner, 2026-10-16).
#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 4)]
async fn uploads_are_batched_but_deliveries_go_at_once() {
    const BATCH: Duration = Duration::from_millis(1500);
    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let db = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Db::open(&dir.path().join("client.sqlite")).unwrap()));
    let status = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Status::default()));
    let plugin_listener = TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0").await.unwrap();
    let plugin_addr = plugin_listener.local_addr().unwrap();
    tokio::spawn(pt_client::listener::serve(plugin_listener, db.clone(), status.clone(), None));
    let srv = Arc::new(Mutex::new(FakeServer::default()));
    let app = Router::new().route("/api/v1/chunks", post(chunks)).with_state(srv.clone());
    let server_listener = TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0").await.unwrap();
    let server_url = format!("http://{}", server_listener.local_addr().unwrap());
    tokio::spawn(async move { axum::serve(server_listener, app).await.unwrap() });
    let cfg = pt_core::Config::from_toml_str(pt_client::paths::SAMPLE_CONFIG).unwrap();
    let ucfg = UploaderConfig {
        server_url,
        token: TOKEN.into(),
        retry_interval: RETRY,
        idle_poll: Duration::from_millis(50),
        batch_interval: BATCH,
        max_frames: 5000,
        max_bytes: 4 << 20,
        multiplayer: Multiplayer { truckersmp_module_names: vec![], mods: vec![] },
        config_hash: cfg.integrity_hash(),
        config_canonical_json: cfg.integrity_canonical_json(),
    };
    let manifest = Arc::new(Mutex::new(vec![]));
    tokio::spawn(pt_client::uploader::run(ucfg, db.clone(), status.clone(), manifest));

    let mut conn = TcpStream::connect(plugin_addr).await.unwrap();
    let mut acks = Acks::default();
    let start = Instant::now();
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    out.extend(frame(S1, "hello", None, ",\"last_seq\":0"));
    out.extend(frame(S1, "init", Some(1), ",\"game_id\":\"ats\""));
    // Samples trickling in, as while driving.
    for s in 2..=11 {
        out.extend(frame(S1, "sample", Some(s), ",\"ch\":{\"truck.speed\":20.5}"));
    }
    conn.write_all(&out).await.unwrap();
    wait_ack(&mut conn, &mut acks, S1, 11).await;
    for s in 12..=21 {
        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50)).await;
        conn.write_all(&frame(S1, "sample", Some(s), ",\"ch\":{\"truck.speed\":20.5}")).await.unwrap();
    }
    tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(300)).await;
    assert!(srv.lock().unwrap().chunks.is_empty(), "sent before the batch interval");

    // Then one upload with all of them, about BATCH after the first.
    let deadline = Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(10);
    while srv.lock().unwrap().chunks.is_empty() {
        assert!(Instant::now() < deadline, "the batch never went");
        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(20)).await;
    }
    assert!(start.elapsed() >= BATCH - Duration::from_millis(100), "{:?}", start.elapsed());
    {
        let s = srv.lock().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(s.chunks.len(), 1, "{:?}", s.chunks);
        assert_eq!((s.chunks[0].1, s.chunks[0].2), (1, 21));
    }

    // A delivery does not wait.
    let sent = Instant::now();
    conn.write_all(&frame(S1, "gameplay", Some(22), ",\"id\":\"job.delivered\",\"attrs\":[]")).await.unwrap();
    while srv.lock().unwrap().chunks.len() < 2 {
        assert!(sent.elapsed() < BATCH / 2, "the delivery waited for the batch");
        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(10)).await;
    }
    assert_eq!(srv.lock().unwrap().chunks[1].2, 22);
}
```

`crates/pt-client/tests/updater.rs`:

```rs
//! The updater against a fake server: it downloads only what a release key
//! signed, resumes, refuses tampered files, and swaps `bin` (and back).

use std::collections::BTreeMap;
use std::io::Write;
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};

use axum::extract::{Path as UrlPath, State};
use axum::http::{HeaderMap, StatusCode};
use axum::routing::get;
use axum::{Json, Router};
use ed25519_dalek::{Signer, SigningKey};
use pt_client::updater;
use pt_core::update::{UpdateFile, UpdateManifest, PRODUCT, SIGNING_CONTEXT};
use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};

#[derive(Default)]
struct Fake {
    offer: Option<serde_json::Value>,
    files: BTreeMap<String, Vec<u8>>,
    downloads: usize,
}

type Shared = Arc<Mutex<Fake>>;

const TOKEN: &str = "pt_live_test-token";

fn authorized(h: &HeaderMap) -> bool {
    h.get("authorization").is_some_and(|v| v == &format!("Bearer {TOKEN}"))
}

async fn offer(State(s): State<Shared>, h: HeaderMap) -> Result<Json<serde_json::Value>, StatusCode> {
    if !authorized(&h) {
        return Err(StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED);
    }
    Ok(Json(serde_json::json!({"update": s.lock().unwrap().offer.clone()})))
}

async fn file(State(s): State<Shared>, UrlPath(key): UrlPath<String>, h: HeaderMap) -> Result<Vec<u8>, StatusCode> {
    if !authorized(&h) {
        return Err(StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED);
    }
    let mut s = s.lock().unwrap();
    s.downloads += 1;
    s.files.get(&key).cloned().ok_or(StatusCode::NOT_FOUND)
}

fn key() -> SigningKey {
    SigningKey::from_bytes(&[5; 32])
}

fn keys() -> Vec<[u8; 32]> {
    vec![key().verifying_key().to_bytes()]
}

fn gzip(b: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut e = flate2::write::GzEncoder::new(Vec::new(), flate2::Compression::default());
    e.write_all(b).unwrap();
    e.finish().unwrap()
}

fn sha(b: &[u8]) -> String {
    Sha256::digest(b).iter().map(|x| format!("{x:02x}")).collect()
}

/// A release with two files; returns the manifest text.
fn release(fake: &Shared, version: &str, signer: &SigningKey) -> String {
    let contents = [("plasmatrack-clientw.exe", format!("new client {version}")), ("licenses/LICENSE.txt", "licence".to_string())];
    let mut m = UpdateManifest { product: PRODUCT.into(), platform: updater::PLATFORM.into(), version: version.into(), files: vec![] };
    let mut f = fake.lock().unwrap();
    for (path, body) in contents {
        let gz = gzip(body.as_bytes());
        let uf = UpdateFile { path: path.into(), sha256: sha(body.as_bytes()), size: body.len() as u64, gz_size: gz.len() as u64 };
        f.files.insert(m.key(&uf), gz);
        m.files.push(uf);
    }
    let text = serde_json::to_string(&m).unwrap();
    let sig: String = signer.sign(&[SIGNING_CONTEXT, text.as_bytes()].concat()).to_bytes().iter().map(|b| format!("{b:02x}")).collect();
    f.offer = Some(serde_json::json!({"manifest": text, "signature": sig}));
    text
}

async fn serve(fake: Shared) -> String {
    let app = Router::new()
        .route("/api/v1/client/update", get(offer))
        .route("/dl/releases/{*key}", get(file))
        .with_state(fake);
    let l = tokio::net::TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0").await.unwrap();
    let url = format!("http://{}", l.local_addr().unwrap());
    tokio::spawn(async move { axum::serve(l, app).await.unwrap() });
    url
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn downloads_verifies_and_resumes() {
    let fake: Shared = Arc::default();
    let url = serve(fake.clone()).await;
    let http = reqwest::Client::new();
    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let updates = dir.path().join("updates");

    assert!(updater::fetch_offer(&http, &url, TOKEN, "0.1.0", &keys()).await.unwrap().is_none(), "nothing offered");
    release(&fake, "0.2.0", &key());
    let offer = updater::fetch_offer(&http, &url, TOKEN, "0.1.0", &keys()).await.unwrap().unwrap();
    assert!(updater::fetch_offer(&http, &url, TOKEN, "0.2.0", &keys()).await.is_err(), "not newer: refused");
    assert!(updater::fetch_offer(&http, &url, "wrong", "0.1.0", &keys()).await.unwrap_err().contains("401"));
    let staged = updater::stage(&http, &url, TOKEN, &offer, &updates).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(std::fs::read_to_string(staged.join("plasmatrack-clientw.exe")).unwrap(), "new client 0.2.0");
    assert_eq!(std::fs::read_to_string(staged.join("licenses").join("LICENSE.txt")).unwrap(), "licence");
    let (found, m) = updater::staged(&updates, "0.1.0", &keys()).unwrap();
    assert_eq!((found, m.version.as_str()), (staged.clone(), "0.2.0"));
    assert!(updater::staged(&updates, "0.2.0", &keys()).is_none(), "already installed");

    // Staging again downloads nothing; a damaged file is fetched again.
    let before = fake.lock().unwrap().downloads;
    updater::stage(&http, &url, TOKEN, &offer, &updates).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(fake.lock().unwrap().downloads, before);
    std::fs::write(staged.join("plasmatrack-clientw.exe"), "tampered").unwrap();
    assert!(updater::staged(&updates, "0.1.0", &keys()).is_none(), "a changed file is not installed");
    updater::stage(&http, &url, TOKEN, &offer, &updates).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(fake.lock().unwrap().downloads, before + 1);
    assert!(updater::staged(&updates, "0.1.0", &keys()).is_some());
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn refuses_unsigned_and_tampered_releases() {
    let fake: Shared = Arc::default();
    let url = serve(fake.clone()).await;
    let http = reqwest::Client::new();
    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();

    release(&fake, "0.2.0", &SigningKey::from_bytes(&[6; 32]));
    let e = updater::fetch_offer(&http, &url, TOKEN, "0.1.0", &keys()).await.unwrap_err();
    assert!(e.contains("release key"), "{e}");

    // Signed, but the server hands out a different file.
    release(&fake, "0.2.0", &key());
    let offer = updater::fetch_offer(&http, &url, TOKEN, "0.1.0", &keys()).await.unwrap().unwrap();
    let k = offer.manifest.key(&offer.manifest.files[0]);
    let evil = gzip(b"evil client 0.2.0");
    let same_size = {
        let mut v = evil.clone();
        v.resize(offer.manifest.files[0].gz_size as usize, 0);
        v
    };
    fake.lock().unwrap().files.insert(k, same_size);
    let e = updater::stage(&http, &url, TOKEN, &offer, &dir.path().join("updates")).await.unwrap_err();
    assert!(e.contains("does not match") || e.contains("expected"), "{e}");
    assert!(updater::staged(&dir.path().join("updates"), "0.1.0", &keys()).is_none());
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn swaps_bin_and_restores_it() {
    let fake: Shared = Arc::default();
    let url = serve(fake.clone()).await;
    let http = reqwest::Client::new();
    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let bin = dir.path().join("bin");
    std::fs::create_dir_all(&bin).unwrap();
    std::fs::write(bin.join("plasmatrack-clientw.exe"), "old client").unwrap();
    std::fs::write(bin.join("old-only.txt"), "x").unwrap();

    release(&fake, "0.2.0", &key());
    let offer = updater::fetch_offer(&http, &url, TOKEN, "0.1.0", &keys()).await.unwrap().unwrap();
    let staged = updater::stage(&http, &url, TOKEN, &offer, &dir.path().join("updates")).await.unwrap();
    let m = updater::verify_staged(&staged, &keys()).unwrap();
    let old = updater::swap_bin(&staged, &m, &bin).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(std::fs::read_to_string(bin.join("plasmatrack-clientw.exe")).unwrap(), "new client 0.2.0");
    assert!(!bin.join("old-only.txt").exists(), "bin holds exactly the release");
    let listing: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(&std::fs::read_to_string(bin.join("manifest.json")).unwrap()).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(listing["licenses/LICENSE.txt"], sha(b"licence"));
    assert_eq!(std::fs::read_to_string(old.join("plasmatrack-clientw.exe")).unwrap(), "old client");

    updater::restore_bin(&bin, &old).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(std::fs::read_to_string(bin.join("plasmatrack-clientw.exe")).unwrap(), "old client");
    assert!(bin.join("old-only.txt").exists());
}
```

`crates/pt-core/src/config.rs`:

```rs
//! Typed configuration. Mirrors `config/plasmatrack.sample.toml` exactly: unknown
//! keys are rejected so the sample file and the code cannot drift apart.

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

use crate::game::Game;
use crate::job::JobType;

#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum ConfigError {
    #[error("config parse error: {0}")]
    Parse(#[from] toml::de::Error),
    #[error("invalid config: {0}")]
    Invalid(String),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct Config {
    pub config_version: u32,
    pub rules: Rules,
    pub review_policy: ReviewPolicy,
    pub review_flags: ReviewFlags,
    pub timeline: Timeline,
    pub map: Map,
    pub notifications: Notifications,
    pub multiplayer: Multiplayer,
    pub plugin: Plugin,
    pub sync: Sync,
    /// Per-driver settings; the only part excluded from the integrity hash.
    pub local: Local,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct Rules {
    pub manual_review_over_world_km: f64,
    /// A whole job averaging more than this many 1:1 km per real (unpaused)
    /// minute is held for review (5 = 300 km/h; you, 2026-10-14).
    pub review_over_average_world_km_per_min: f64,
    /// Jobs with less driving time than this are not averaged (too noisy).
    pub average_pace_min_driving_s: f64,
    /// The same check timed by the game's own clock: 1:1 km per minute, where
    /// in-game minutes are turned back into real minutes at the game's time rate
    /// (`local.scale` in singleplayer, `truckersmp_game_min_per_real_min` on
    /// TruckersMP). 5 = 300 km/h. Used in tandem with the above.
    pub review_over_average_world_km_per_game_clock_min: f64,
    /// TruckersMP's server clock: one in-game minute every 10 real seconds.
    pub truckersmp_game_min_per_real_min: f64,
    /// Jobs with fewer in-game minutes of driving than this are not averaged.
    pub average_pace_min_game_min: f64,
    /// A delivery paying more than this per mile of the game's delivery
    /// distance (in the game's currency: USD in ATS, EUR in ETS2) is held for
    /// review (you, 2026-10-16: 400). Absent: not checked.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub review_over_income_per_game_mi: Option<f64>,
    /// A delivery paying more than this in all is held for review (you,
    /// 2026-10-16: 500,000). A very long job or a future game version can
    /// pass it honestly, so it is a review, never invalid. Absent: not checked.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub review_over_income: Option<f64>,
    pub speed_penalty_factor: f64,
    pub points_per_world_mi: f64,
    pub points_decimals: u32,
    pub speed: SpeedRules,
    pub distance: DistanceRules,
    pub fuel: FuelRules,
    pub refuel: RefuelHeuristic,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct SpeedRules {
    pub sustained_window_s: f64,
    pub compare_precision_mph: f64,
    pub ats: SpeedLimits,
    pub ets2: SpeedLimits,
}

impl SpeedRules {
    pub fn limits(&self, game: Game) -> &SpeedLimits {
        match game {
            Game::Ats => &self.ats,
            Game::Ets2 => &self.ets2,
        }
    }

    /// (penalty, invalid) mph for a job: a road trip's own limits when the
    /// game has them, else the game's.
    pub fn limits_for(&self, game: Game, job_type: JobType) -> (f64, f64) {
        let l = self.limits(game);
        match (&l.road_trip, job_type) {
            (Some(r), JobType::Car) => (r.penalty_over_mph, r.invalid_over_mph),
            _ => (l.penalty_over_mph, l.invalid_over_mph),
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct SpeedLimits {
    pub penalty_over_mph: f64,
    pub invalid_over_mph: f64,
    /// Road trips (`car_job`, a car or pickup) drive faster than trucks.
    /// Absent: they use the limits above.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub road_trip: Option<RoadTripSpeed>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct RoadTripSpeed {
    pub penalty_over_mph: f64,
    pub invalid_over_mph: f64,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct DistanceRules {
    pub compare_precision_km: f64,
    pub odometer_epsilon_km: f64,
    pub delivered_vs_trace_tolerance_pct: f64,
    pub delivered_vs_trace_tolerance_min_mi: f64,
    pub delivered_vs_trace_short_job_under_mi: f64,
    pub delivered_vs_trace_short_job_max_pct: f64,
    /// `distance.km` is reported in whole km, so the comparison always allows this
    /// much on top of the tolerance (measured: 1.8 tracked vs 1 reported, 238.87 vs
    /// 239, 1232.14 vs 1233).
    pub delivered_distance_resolution_km: f64,
}

impl Rules {
    /// Floors a job's point total to `points_decimals` places (never rounds up).
    /// Rounds away float noise first, so 3.7 stays 3.7 rather than 3.6999… -> 3.6.
    pub fn floor_points(&self, total: f64) -> f64 {
        let scale = 10f64.powi(self.points_decimals as i32);
        ((total * scale * 1e6).round() / 1e6).floor() / scale
    }
}

impl DistanceRules {
    /// Allowed difference, in miles, between the game's `job.delivered` distance and
    /// the tracker's own figure. Everything is measured on the SDK-reported delivery
    /// distance (`delivered_mi`, i.e. `distance.km` in miles): the greater of the
    /// percentage and the floor, except that a job shorter than `short_job_under_mi`
    /// is hard-capped at `short_job_max_pct`.
    pub fn delivered_vs_trace_tolerance_mi(&self, delivered_mi: f64) -> f64 {
        let t = (delivered_mi * self.delivered_vs_trace_tolerance_pct / 100.0)
            .max(self.delivered_vs_trace_tolerance_min_mi);
        if delivered_mi < self.delivered_vs_trace_short_job_under_mi {
            t.min(delivered_mi * self.delivered_vs_trace_short_job_max_pct / 100.0)
        } else {
            t
        }
    }
}
```
