```rs
/// Route map settings (PLAN §8).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct Map {
    pub scale: MapScales,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct MapScales {
    pub ats: VanillaScale,
    pub ets2: VanillaScale,
}

impl MapScales {
    pub fn vanilla(&self, game: Game) -> &VanillaScale {
        match game {
            Game::Ats => &self.ats,
            Game::Ets2 => &self.ets2,
        }
    }
}

/// The `local.scale` values the unmodded game uses (common_channels.h:13-23).
/// A game can have more than one road scale: ETS2 uses 19, and 15 in the UK
/// (measured 2026-10-13). The first is the main one.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct VanillaScale {
    pub city_local_scale: f64,
    pub road_local_scales: Vec<f64>,
}

/// How a stretch of route is coloured on the map (PLAN §8).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum ScaleClass {
    City,
    Road,
    OneToOne,
    Nonstandard,
    Unknown,
}

impl VanillaScale {
    /// The main road scale, for jobs too short to measure their own mix.
    pub fn main_road_local_scale(&self) -> f64 {
        self.road_local_scales.first().copied().unwrap_or(1.0)
    }

    pub fn classify(&self, local_scale: Option<f64>) -> ScaleClass {
        let Some(s) = local_scale else { return ScaleClass::Unknown };
        if s == self.city_local_scale {
            ScaleClass::City
        } else if self.road_local_scales.contains(&s) {
            ScaleClass::Road
        } else if s == 1.0 {
            ScaleClass::OneToOne
        } else {
            ScaleClass::Nonstandard
        }
    }
}

/// Desktop notifications for a delivery marked Invalid (rule 2) and for the
/// speed penalty (rule 5) activating. The client draws each delay uniformly
/// from [min, max] at microsecond resolution (pt-core itself has no RNG).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct Notifications {
    pub enabled: bool,
    pub delay_min_wall_s: f64,
    pub delay_max_wall_s: f64,
}

impl Notifications {
    /// Inclusive delay range in whole microseconds.
    pub fn delay_range_us(&self) -> (u64, u64) {
        let us = |s: f64| (s * 1_000_000.0).round() as u64;
        (us(self.delay_min_wall_s), us(self.delay_max_wall_s))
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct Multiplayer {
    /// Module file names whose presence in the game process means TruckersMP.
    /// PROVISIONAL: filled in from captures (the SDK cannot identify TruckersMP).
    pub truckersmp_module_names: Vec<String>,
    /// Other multiplayer mods, each recognised by its own module names (HaulMP,
    /// 2026-10-22). Absent: none, and the published hash stays as before.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]
    pub mods: Vec<MultiplayerMod>,
}

impl Multiplayer {
    /// The mod whose `kind` this is.
    pub fn find_mod(&self, kind: &str) -> Option<&MultiplayerMod> {
        self.mods.iter().find(|m| m.kind == kind)
    }

    /// The server clock rate of mod `kind`, if it has one.
    pub fn mod_clock(&self, kind: Option<&str>) -> Option<f64> {
        kind.and_then(|k| self.find_mod(k)).and_then(|m| m.game_min_per_real_min)
    }

    /// The kind of every mod one of whose module names is in `names`
    /// (case-insensitive), in config order.
    pub fn mods_matching(&self, names: &[&str]) -> Vec<String> {
        self.mods
            .iter()
            .filter(|m| names.iter().any(|n| m.module_names.iter().any(|w| w.eq_ignore_ascii_case(n))))
            .map(|m| m.kind.clone())
            .collect()
    }

    /// The names in `names` that identify a mod (case-insensitive), as given.
    pub fn mod_module_matches<'a>(&self, names: &[&'a str]) -> Vec<&'a str> {
        names
            .iter()
            .copied()
            .filter(|n| self.mods.iter().any(|m| m.module_names.iter().any(|w| w.eq_ignore_ascii_case(n))))
            .collect()
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct MultiplayerMod {
    /// The job's `multiplayer.kind` (1-32 lowercase letters, digits, `_`).
    pub kind: String,
    /// Shown to players, e.g. "HaulMP".
    pub name: String,
    /// Any of these module file names loaded in the game process means this
    /// mod for the rest of the session.
    pub module_names: Vec<String>,
    /// The server's game clock, when the mod sets one (TrucklineMP,
    /// 2026-10-23): it replaces `local.scale` in the game-clock pace check,
    /// and save loads are matched without the game time, as on TruckersMP.
    /// Absent: the clock runs as in singleplayer (HaulMP).
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub game_min_per_real_min: Option<f64>,
    /// Jobs on this mod are discarded for Singleplayer Division players, the
    /// way TruckersMP jobs always are (you, 2026-10-22).
    pub singleplayer_division_discard: bool,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct Local {
    pub listen_address: String,
    pub port: u16,
    pub server_url: String,
    pub status_port: u16,
    pub token: String,
}

impl Config {
    pub fn from_toml_str(s: &str) -> Result<Config, ConfigError> {
        let cfg: Config = toml::from_str(s)?;
        cfg.validate()?;
        Ok(cfg)
    }

    /// Canonical JSON of every setting that must match a server-published
    /// config version: everything except `[local]`. Keys are sorted (serde_json
    /// `Value` maps are ordered), so formatting, comments and key order in the
    /// TOML file do not affect it.
    pub fn integrity_canonical_json(&self) -> String {
        let mut v = serde_json::to_value(self).expect("config always serializes");
        v.as_object_mut()
            .expect("config serializes to an object")
            .remove("local");
        v.to_string()
    }

    /// SHA-256 (lowercase hex) of [`Self::integrity_canonical_json`]. The client
    /// uploads it; the server discards jobs whose hash matches no published
    /// version (rule 0).
    pub fn integrity_hash(&self) -> String {
        use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};
        Sha256::digest(self.integrity_canonical_json().as_bytes())
            .iter()
            .map(|b| format!("{b:02x}"))
            .collect()
    }

    pub fn validate(&self) -> Result<(), ConfigError> {
        fn positive(errs: &mut Vec<String>, name: &str, v: f64) {
            if !(v.is_finite() && v > 0.0) {
                errs.push(format!("{name} must be > 0 (got {v})"));
            }
        }
        let mut errs = Vec::new();
        let r = &self.rules;
        for (name, v) in [
            ("rules.manual_review_over_world_km", r.manual_review_over_world_km),
            ("rules.review_over_average_world_km_per_min", r.review_over_average_world_km_per_min),
            ("rules.review_over_income_per_game_mi", r.review_over_income_per_game_mi.unwrap_or(1.0)),
            ("rules.review_over_income", r.review_over_income.unwrap_or(1.0)),
            ("rules.average_pace_min_driving_s", r.average_pace_min_driving_s),
            ("rules.review_over_average_world_km_per_game_clock_min", r.review_over_average_world_km_per_game_clock_min),
            ("rules.truckersmp_game_min_per_real_min", r.truckersmp_game_min_per_real_min),
            ("rules.average_pace_min_game_min", r.average_pace_min_game_min),
            ("rules.points_per_world_mi", r.points_per_world_mi),
            ("rules.speed.sustained_window_s", r.speed.sustained_window_s),
            ("rules.speed.compare_precision_mph", r.speed.compare_precision_mph),
            ("rules.distance.compare_precision_km", r.distance.compare_precision_km),
            ("rules.distance.odometer_epsilon_km", r.distance.odometer_epsilon_km),
            ("rules.distance.delivered_vs_trace_tolerance_pct", r.distance.delivered_vs_trace_tolerance_pct),
            ("rules.distance.delivered_vs_trace_tolerance_min_mi", r.distance.delivered_vs_trace_tolerance_min_mi),
            ("rules.distance.delivered_vs_trace_short_job_under_mi", r.distance.delivered_vs_trace_short_job_under_mi),
            ("rules.distance.delivered_vs_trace_short_job_max_pct", r.distance.delivered_vs_trace_short_job_max_pct),
            ("rules.distance.delivered_distance_resolution_km", r.distance.delivered_distance_resolution_km),
            ("plugin.sample_rate_hz", self.plugin.sample_rate_hz),
            ("sync.retry_interval_wall_s", self.sync.retry_interval_wall_s),
            ("timeline.reopen_window_wall_h", self.timeline.reopen_window_wall_h),
        ] {
            positive(&mut errs, name, v);
        }
        for (g, l) in [("ats", &r.speed.ats), ("ets2", &r.speed.ets2)] {
            let road_trip = l.road_trip.as_ref().map(|t| (format!("{g}.road_trip"), t.penalty_over_mph, t.invalid_over_mph));
            for (name, penalty, invalid) in std::iter::once((g.to_string(), l.penalty_over_mph, l.invalid_over_mph)).chain(road_trip) {
                positive(&mut errs, &format!("rules.speed.{name}.penalty_over_mph"), penalty);
                if invalid <= penalty {
                    errs.push(format!(
                        "rules.speed.{name}: invalid_over_mph ({invalid}) must be above penalty_over_mph ({penalty})"
                    ));
                }
            }
        }
        if !(r.speed_penalty_factor > 0.0 && r.speed_penalty_factor <= 1.0) {
            errs.push(format!(
                "rules.speed_penalty_factor must be in (0, 1] (got {})",
                r.speed_penalty_factor
            ));
        }
        if r.points_decimals > 6 {
            errs.push(format!("rules.points_decimals must be 0..=6 (got {})", r.points_decimals));
        }
        if r.distance.delivered_vs_trace_short_job_max_pct < r.distance.delivered_vs_trace_tolerance_pct {
            errs.push("rules.distance.delivered_vs_trace_short_job_max_pct must be >= delivered_vs_trace_tolerance_pct".into());
        }
        if r.fuel.negative_fuel_tolerance_l < 0.0 || r.fuel.mid_job_jump_tolerance_l < 0.0 {
            errs.push("rules.fuel tolerances must be >= 0".into());
        }
        let n = &self.notifications;
        if !(n.delay_min_wall_s >= 0.0 && n.delay_min_wall_s <= n.delay_max_wall_s && n.delay_max_wall_s.is_finite()) {
            errs.push(format!(
                "notifications: need 0 <= delay_min_wall_s ({}) <= delay_max_wall_s ({})",
                n.delay_min_wall_s, n.delay_max_wall_s
            ));
        }
        if r.refuel.min_rate_l_per_s > r.refuel.max_rate_l_per_s {
            errs.push("rules.refuel.min_rate_l_per_s must not exceed max_rate_l_per_s".into());
        }
        let mp = &self.multiplayer;
        for (i, m) in mp.mods.iter().enumerate() {
            let ok_kind = (1..=32).contains(&m.kind.len())
                && m.kind.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_lowercase() || b.is_ascii_digit() || b == b'_')
                && !matches!(m.kind.as_str(), "singleplayer" | "convoy" | "truckersmp" | "unknown");
            if !ok_kind {
                errs.push(format!(
                    "multiplayer.mods[{i}].kind must be 1-32 lowercase letters, digits or _, and not a built-in kind (got {:?})",
                    m.kind
                ));
            }
            if mp.mods[..i].iter().any(|o| o.kind == m.kind) {
                errs.push(format!("multiplayer.mods: kind {:?} appears twice", m.kind));
            }
            if m.name.trim().is_empty() {
                errs.push(format!("multiplayer.mods[{i}].name must not be empty"));
            }
            if m.module_names.is_empty() {
                errs.push(format!("multiplayer.mods[{i}].module_names must not be empty"));
            }
            if let Some(rate) = m.game_min_per_real_min {
                positive(&mut errs, &format!("multiplayer.mods[{i}].game_min_per_real_min"), rate);
            }
            for n in &m.module_names {
                let elsewhere = mp.truckersmp_module_names.iter().any(|t| t.eq_ignore_ascii_case(n))
                    || mp.mods[..i].iter().any(|o| o.module_names.iter().any(|t| t.eq_ignore_ascii_case(n)));
                if elsewhere {
                    errs.push(format!("multiplayer: module name {n:?} belongs to more than one kind"));
                }
            }
        }
        if self.local.listen_address != "127.0.0.1" && self.local.listen_address != "::1" {
            errs.push("local.listen_address must be a loopback address".into());
        }
        if self.local.status_port == self.local.port {
            errs.push("local.status_port must differ from local.port".into());
        }
        if errs.is_empty() {
            Ok(())
        } else {
            Err(ConfigError::Invalid(errs.join("; ")))
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    const SAMPLE: &str = include_str!("../../../config/plasmatrack.sample.toml");

    #[test]
    fn sample_config_parses_and_matches_spec_defaults() {
        let c = Config::from_toml_str(SAMPLE).expect("sample config must be valid");
        assert_eq!(c.rules.speed.limits(Game::Ats).penalty_over_mph, 105.0);
        assert_eq!(c.rules.speed.limits(Game::Ats).invalid_over_mph, 125.0);
        assert_eq!(c.rules.speed.limits(Game::Ets2).penalty_over_mph, 100.0);
        assert_eq!(c.rules.speed.limits(Game::Ets2).invalid_over_mph, 150.0);
        assert_eq!(c.rules.speed.limits_for(Game::Ats, JobType::Car), (155.0, 200.0));
        assert_eq!(c.rules.speed.limits_for(Game::Ats, JobType::Freight), (105.0, 125.0));
        assert_eq!(c.rules.speed.limits_for(Game::Ets2, JobType::Car), (100.0, 150.0));
        assert_eq!(c.rules.manual_review_over_world_km, 150.0);
        assert_eq!(c.rules.speed_penalty_factor, 0.85);
        assert_eq!(c.rules.speed.sustained_window_s, 3.0);
        assert_eq!(c.sync.retry_interval_wall_s, 20.0);
        assert!(!c.review_flags.odometer_jump);
        assert!(!c.review_flags.impossible_delivery_time);
        assert_eq!(c.review_policy.gap, ReviewAction::Review);
        assert_eq!(c.review_policy.late_start, ReviewAction::Review);
        assert_eq!(c.review_policy.trace_checks, ReviewAction::Review);
        assert!(c.notifications.enabled);
        assert_eq!(c.notifications.delay_range_us(), (5_000_000, 30_000_000));
    }

    #[test]
    fn scale_classes() {
        let c = Config::from_toml_str(SAMPLE).unwrap();
        let ats = c.map.scale.vanilla(Game::Ats);
        let ets2 = c.map.scale.vanilla(Game::Ets2);
        assert_eq!(ats.classify(Some(20.0)), ScaleClass::Road);
        assert_eq!(ets2.classify(Some(19.0)), ScaleClass::Road);
        assert_eq!(ets2.classify(Some(15.0)), ScaleClass::Road, "ETS2 UK roads");
        assert_eq!(ats.classify(Some(15.0)), ScaleClass::Nonstandard);
        assert_eq!(ets2.main_road_local_scale(), 19.0);
        assert_eq!(ets2.classify(Some(20.0)), ScaleClass::Nonstandard);
        assert_eq!(ats.classify(Some(3.0)), ScaleClass::City);
        assert_eq!(ats.classify(Some(1.0)), ScaleClass::OneToOne);
        assert_eq!(ats.classify(Some(10.0)), ScaleClass::Nonstandard);
        assert_eq!(ats.classify(None), ScaleClass::Unknown);
    }

    #[test]
    fn points_floor_to_one_decimal() {
        let r = Config::from_toml_str(SAMPLE).unwrap().rules;
        assert_eq!(r.points_decimals, 1);
        assert_eq!(r.floor_points(3.70), 3.7);
        assert_eq!(r.floor_points(3.79), 3.7);
        assert_eq!(r.floor_points(0.1 + 0.2), 0.3); // 0.30000000000000004
        assert_eq!(r.floor_points(3.0 * 1.1), 3.3); // 3.3000000000000003
        assert_eq!(r.floor_points(0.0), 0.0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn delivered_vs_trace_tolerance() {
        let d = Config::from_toml_str(SAMPLE).unwrap().rules.distance;
        let t = |mi: f64| d.delivered_vs_trace_tolerance_mi(mi);
        // Delivered distance under 100 mi: the 30 mi floor is hard-capped at 5%.
        assert!((t(10.0) - 0.5).abs() < 1e-9);
        assert!((t(99.0) - 4.95).abs() < 1e-9);
        // From 100 mi: greater of 1% and 30 mi.
        assert_eq!(t(100.0), 30.0);
        assert_eq!(t(2999.0), 30.0);
        assert!((t(5000.0) - 50.0).abs() < 1e-9);
    }

    #[test]
    fn old_flag_action_is_rejected() {
        let bad = SAMPLE.replace("gap = \"review\"", "gap = \"flag\"");
        assert!(matches!(Config::from_toml_str(&bad), Err(ConfigError::Parse(_))));
        let bad = SAMPLE.replace("delay_min_wall_s = 5.0", "delay_min_wall_s = 31.0");
        assert!(matches!(Config::from_toml_str(&bad), Err(ConfigError::Invalid(_))));
    }

    #[test]
    fn integrity_hash_ignores_local_and_formatting() {
        let base = Config::from_toml_str(SAMPLE).unwrap();
        let h = base.integrity_hash();
        assert_eq!(h.len(), 64);

        let local_changed = SAMPLE
            .replace("port = 30455", "port = 40000")
            .replace("https://plasmatrack.example.invalid", "https://other.invalid");
        assert_eq!(Config::from_toml_str(&local_changed).unwrap().integrity_hash(), h);

        let reformatted = SAMPLE.replace("sustained_window_s = 3.0", "sustained_window_s   =   3.00 # same");
        assert_eq!(Config::from_toml_str(&reformatted).unwrap().integrity_hash(), h);
        let canon = base.integrity_canonical_json();
        for local_key in ["\"local\"", "\"listen_address\"", "\"server_url\"", "\"port\"", "\"token\"", "\"status_port\""] {
            assert!(!canon.contains(local_key), "{local_key} leaked into the integrity hash");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn integrity_hash_detects_any_compared_change() {
        let h = Config::from_toml_str(SAMPLE).unwrap().integrity_hash();
        for (from, to) in [
            ("sustained_window_s = 3.0", "sustained_window_s = 3.5"),
            ("invalid_over_mph = 150.0", "invalid_over_mph = 250.0"),
            ("negative_fuel_tolerance_l = 0.5", "negative_fuel_tolerance_l = 50.0"),
            ("gap = \"review\"", "gap = \"off\""),
            ("delay_max_wall_s = 30.0", "delay_max_wall_s = 60.0"),
            ("odometer_jump = false", "odometer_jump = true"),
            ("sample_rate_hz = 20.0", "sample_rate_hz = 5.0"),
            ("retry_interval_wall_s = 20.0", "retry_interval_wall_s = 60.0"),
            ("singleplayer_division_discard = true", "singleplayer_division_discard = false"),
            ("\"haulmp-telemetry.dll\"]", "\"haulmp-telemetry.dll\", \"haulmp_extra.dll\"]"),
        ] {
            let changed = SAMPLE.replace(from, to);
            assert_ne!(changed, SAMPLE, "fixture did not apply: {from}");
            let c = Config::from_toml_str(&changed).unwrap();
            assert_ne!(c.integrity_hash(), h, "change not detected: {to}");
        }
    }

    const HAULMP: &str = "[[multiplayer.mods]]\nkind = \"haulmp\"\nname = \"HaulMP\"\nmodule_names = [\"haulmp_stub.dll\", \"haulmp-telemetry.dll\"]\nsingleplayer_division_discard = true\n";

    #[test]
    fn multiplayer_mods_are_optional_and_checked() {
        let c = Config::from_toml_str(SAMPLE).unwrap();
        let m = c.multiplayer.find_mod("haulmp").expect("sample lists HaulMP");
        assert!(m.singleplayer_division_discard);
        assert_eq!(c.multiplayer.mods_matching(&["KERNEL32.DLL", "HaulMP_Stub.dll"]), vec!["haulmp".to_string()]);

        // Without mods the canonical JSON has no `mods` key, so configs
        // published before mods existed keep their hash.
        assert!(SAMPLE.contains(HAULMP), "sample's HaulMP block changed; update HAULMP");
        let from = SAMPLE.find("# HaulMP (ETS2)").expect("first mod block");
        let to = from + SAMPLE[from..].find("# ----").expect("next section");
        let without = Config::from_toml_str(&format!("{}{}", &SAMPLE[..from], &SAMPLE[to..])).unwrap();
        assert!(without.multiplayer.mods.is_empty());
        assert!(!without.integrity_canonical_json().contains("\"mods\""));

        for (from, to) in [
            ("kind = \"haulmp\"", "kind = \"convoy\""),
            ("kind = \"haulmp\"", "kind = \"HaulMP\""),
            ("kind = \"haulmp\"", "kind = \"\""),
            ("name = \"HaulMP\"", "name = \" \""),
            ("[\"haulmp_stub.dll\", \"haulmp-telemetry.dll\"]", "[]"),
            ("[\"haulmp_stub.dll\", \"haulmp-telemetry.dll\"]", "[\"Core_ETS2MP.dll\"]"),
        ] {
            let bad = SAMPLE.replace(HAULMP, &HAULMP.replace(from, to));
            assert!(matches!(Config::from_toml_str(&bad), Err(ConfigError::Invalid(_))), "accepted: {to}");
        }
        let twice = SAMPLE.replace(HAULMP, &format!("{HAULMP}{}", HAULMP.replace("haulmp_stub", "other")));
        assert!(matches!(Config::from_toml_str(&twice), Err(ConfigError::Invalid(_))), "duplicate kind accepted");
    }

    #[test]
    fn unknown_keys_are_rejected() {
        let bad = SAMPLE.replace("[sync]", "[sync]\nretry_interval_s = 5");
        assert!(matches!(Config::from_toml_str(&bad), Err(ConfigError::Parse(_))));
    }

    #[test]
    fn invalid_values_are_rejected() {
        let bad = SAMPLE.replace("invalid_over_mph = 125.0", "invalid_over_mph = 100.0");
        assert!(matches!(Config::from_toml_str(&bad), Err(ConfigError::Invalid(_))));
        let bad = SAMPLE.replace("listen_address = \"127.0.0.1\"", "listen_address = \"0.0.0.0\"");
        assert!(matches!(Config::from_toml_str(&bad), Err(ConfigError::Invalid(_))));
    }
}
```

`crates/pt-core/src/game.rs`:

```rs
//! Game identity. ATS and ETS2 are kept separate everywhere: jobs, totals,
//! leaderboards, maps and timeline state are all partitioned by [`Game`].

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
pub enum Game {
    Ets2,
    Ats,
}

impl Game {
    /// Maps the SDK's `scs_sdk_init_params_v100_t::game_id` (scssdk.h:156-169).
    ///
    /// Values: `SCS_GAME_ID_EUT2` = "eut2" (eurotrucks2/scssdk_eut2.h:16),
    /// `SCS_GAME_ID_ATS` = "ats" (amtrucks/scssdk_ats.h:16).
    pub fn from_sdk_game_id(game_id: &str) -> Option<Game> {
        match game_id {
            "eut2" => Some(Game::Ets2),
            "ats" => Some(Game::Ats),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    /// The API name (`"ets2"` / `"ats"`), the same as the serde form.
    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Game::Ets2 => "ets2",
            Game::Ats => "ats",
        }
    }

    pub fn from_api(s: &str) -> Option<Game> {
        match s {
            "ets2" => Some(Game::Ets2),
            "ats" => Some(Game::Ats),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    pub fn sdk_game_id(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Game::Ets2 => "eut2",
            Game::Ats => "ats",
        }
    }

    /// Minimum telemetry game version (major, minor) we support: the version
    /// that added `planned_distance.km`, both at game patch 1.36.
    /// ETS2: SCS_TELEMETRY_EUT2_GAME_VERSION_1_15 (eurotrucks2/scssdk_telemetry_eut2.h:53,74).
    /// ATS:  SCS_TELEMETRY_ATS_GAME_VERSION_1_02 (amtrucks/scssdk_telemetry_ats.h:32,40).
    /// Gameplay events (job.delivered etc.) arrived one version earlier.
    pub fn min_telemetry_game_version(self) -> (u16, u16) {
        match self {
            Game::Ets2 => (1, 15),
            Game::Ats => (1, 2),
        }
    }

    /// `game_version` is packed with SCS_MAKE_VERSION (major << 16 | minor), scssdk.h:124.
    pub fn is_supported_version(self, packed_game_version: u32) -> bool {
        let major = (packed_game_version >> 16) as u16;
        let minor = (packed_game_version & 0xffff) as u16;
        (major, minor) >= self.min_telemetry_game_version()
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn maps_sdk_game_ids() {
        assert_eq!(Game::from_sdk_game_id("eut2"), Some(Game::Ets2));
        assert_eq!(Game::from_sdk_game_id("ats"), Some(Game::Ats));
        assert_eq!(Game::from_sdk_game_id("ets2"), None);
        for g in [Game::Ets2, Game::Ats] {
            assert_eq!(Game::from_sdk_game_id(g.sdk_game_id()), Some(g));
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn minimum_version_gate() {
        let v = |maj: u32, min: u32| (maj << 16) | min;
        assert!(!Game::Ets2.is_supported_version(v(1, 14)));
        assert!(Game::Ets2.is_supported_version(v(1, 15)));
        assert!(Game::Ets2.is_supported_version(v(1, 18)));
        assert!(!Game::Ats.is_supported_version(v(1, 1)));
        assert!(Game::Ats.is_supported_version(v(1, 2)));
    }
}
```

`crates/pt-core/src/job.rs`:

```rs
//! Job identity (PLAN §5 "Job identity") and the delivery event.
//!
//! Attribute names: common/scssdk_telemetry_common_configs.h (job config) and
//! common/scssdk_telemetry_common_gameplay_events.h (job.delivered).
//!
//! Road trips (a car or pickup, ATS 2026-10-16) arrive as a `car_job` config
//! and `car_job.delivered` / `car_job.cancelled`, with the same attributes
//! except the market (`car_job.market`); they are tracked like freight.

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use serde_json::Value;

use crate::game::Game;
use crate::trace::{attr, Attr};

/// Which kind of job the game reported. One job is active at a time.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum JobType {
    /// `job`: truck freight.
    #[default]
    Freight,
    /// `car_job`: a road trip in a car or pickup.
    Car,
}

impl JobType {
    /// The config id, which also prefixes the gameplay events.
    pub fn config_id(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            JobType::Freight => "job",
            JobType::Car => "car_job",
        }
    }

    pub fn from_config_id(id: &str) -> Option<JobType> {
        match id {
            "job" => Some(JobType::Freight),
            "car_job" => Some(JobType::Car),
            _ => None,
        }
    }
}

/// Where the job leads and when it is due. Stays the same for a job's whole
/// life, across save loads (verified byte-identical over six loads, PLAN §3).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct RouteKey {
    pub game: Game,
    pub source_city: String,
    pub source_company: String,
    pub destination_city: String,
    pub destination_company: String,
    /// Absolute in-game deadline (`delivery.time`, minutes).
    pub delivery_time: Option<u64>,
    pub planned_distance_km: Option<u64>,
    pub job_market: String,
    pub is_special_job: Option<bool>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub job_type: JobType,
}

/// What is hauled. A different cargo key on the same route is a `cargo_switch`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct CargoKey {
    pub cargo_id: String,
    /// `cargo.mass` in kg, compared exactly as the game reports it (f32 bits).
    pub cargo_mass_bits: Option<u64>,
    pub cargo_unit_count: Option<u64>,
    pub income: Option<u64>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Fingerprint {
    pub route: RouteKey,
    pub cargo: CargoKey,
}

/// A parsed, non-empty `job` config.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct JobInfo {
    pub fingerprint: Fingerprint,
    pub cargo_name: String,
    pub cargo_mass_kg: Option<f64>,
    /// `cargo.loaded`: false while driving to the pickup with an owned trailer.
    pub cargo_loaded: bool,
    /// Display names (configs.h:532-586): shown, never part of the identity.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub names: JobNames,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct JobNames {
    pub source_city: String,
    pub source_company: String,
    pub destination_city: String,
    pub destination_company: String,
}

/// `job.market` values (configs.h:627-641).
pub fn is_world_of_trucks_market(market: &str) -> bool {
    matches!(market, "external_contracts" | "external_market")
}

impl JobInfo {
    /// `None` for an empty job config ("no job", configs.h:125).
    pub fn from_config(game: Game, attrs: &[Attr]) -> Option<JobInfo> {
        JobInfo::from_config_of(game, JobType::Freight, attrs)
    }

    /// The same for a `job_type` config (`job` or `car_job`).
    pub fn from_config_of(game: Game, job_type: JobType, attrs: &[Attr]) -> Option<JobInfo> {
        if attrs.is_empty() {
            return None;
        }
        let s = |k: &str| attr(attrs, k).and_then(Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default().to_string();
        let u = |k: &str| attr(attrs, k).and_then(Value::as_u64);
        let mass = attr(attrs, "cargo.mass").and_then(Value::as_f64);
        Some(JobInfo {
            fingerprint: Fingerprint {
                route: RouteKey {
                    game,
                    source_city: s("source.city.id"),
                    source_company: s("source.company.id"),
                    destination_city: s("destination.city.id"),
                    destination_company: s("destination.company.id"),
                    // A road trip's deadline moved by a minute across a load
                    // (2026-10-16), so it is not part of its identity.
                    delivery_time: if job_type == JobType::Car { None } else { u("delivery.time") },
                    planned_distance_km: u("planned_distance.km"),
                    job_market: s(&format!("{}.market", job_type.config_id())),
                    is_special_job: attr(attrs, "is.special.job").and_then(Value::as_bool),
                    job_type,
                },
                cargo: CargoKey {
                    cargo_id: s("cargo.id"),
                    cargo_mass_bits: mass.map(|m| (m as f32).to_bits() as u64),
                    cargo_unit_count: u("cargo.unit.count"),
                    income: u("income"),
                },
            },
            cargo_name: s("cargo"),
            cargo_mass_kg: mass,
            // Older game versions lack the attribute; then the cargo is loaded.
            cargo_loaded: attr(attrs, "cargo.loaded").and_then(Value::as_bool).unwrap_or(true),
            names: JobNames {
                source_city: s("source.city"),
                source_company: s("source.company"),
                destination_city: s("destination.city"),
                destination_company: s("destination.company"),
            },
        })
    }

    pub fn is_world_of_trucks(&self) -> bool {
        is_world_of_trucks_market(&self.fingerprint.route.job_market)
    }
}

/// The `job.delivered` gameplay event (gameplay_events.h:20-35, 100-132).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Delivered {
    /// The game's own job distance: game scale, includes the empty drive to
    /// the pickup, whole km, and taken from the save (so it can be edited).
    pub distance_km: Option<f64>,
    pub revenue: Option<i64>,
    pub earned_xp: Option<i64>,
    pub cargo_damage: Option<f64>,
    /// In-game minutes the job took.
    pub delivery_time_min: Option<u64>,
    pub auto_park_used: Option<bool>,
    pub auto_load_used: Option<bool>,
}

impl Delivered {
    pub fn from_attrs(attrs: &[Attr]) -> Delivered {
        Delivered {
            distance_km: attr(attrs, "distance.km").and_then(Value::as_f64),
            revenue: attr(attrs, "revenue").and_then(Value::as_i64),
            earned_xp: attr(attrs, "earned.xp").and_then(Value::as_i64),
            cargo_damage: attr(attrs, "cargo.damage").and_then(Value::as_f64),
            delivery_time_min: attr(attrs, "delivery.time").and_then(Value::as_u64),
            auto_park_used: attr(attrs, "auto.park.used").and_then(Value::as_bool),
            auto_load_used: attr(attrs, "auto.load.used").and_then(Value::as_bool),
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use serde_json::json;

    fn a(name: &str, value: Value) -> Attr {
        Attr { name: name.into(), index: None, value }
    }

    fn tyres(loaded: bool, cargo: &str) -> Vec<Attr> {
        vec![
            a("cargo.id", json!(cargo)),
            a("cargo.mass", json!(18257.25)),
            a("cargo.unit.count", json!(25)),
            a("source.city.id", json!("port_angeles")),
            a("source.company.id", json!("apa_car_whs")),
            a("destination.city.id", json!("tacoma")),
            a("destination.company.id", json!("pt_trk_dlr")),
            a("income", json!(11626)),
            a("delivery.time", json!(10401816)),
            a("planned_distance.km", json!(235)),
            a("cargo.loaded", json!(loaded)),
            a("job.market", json!("cargo_market")),
            a("is.special.job", json!(false)),
        ]
    }

    #[test]
    fn cargo_loaded_is_not_part_of_the_fingerprint() {
        let before = JobInfo::from_config(Game::Ats, &tyres(false, "tyres")).unwrap();
        let after = JobInfo::from_config(Game::Ats, &tyres(true, "tyres")).unwrap();
        assert!(!before.cargo_loaded && after.cargo_loaded);
        assert_eq!(before.fingerprint, after.fingerprint);
        assert!(JobInfo::from_config(Game::Ats, &[]).is_none());
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_road_trip_is_its_own_kind_of_job() {
        // The owner's ATS road trip (2026-10-16): no cargo.loaded, its own market key.
        let attrs = vec![
            a("cargo.id", json!("xfer_seals")),
            a("cargo", json!("Intermodal Transfer Seals")),
            a("source.city.id", json!("new_orleans")),
            a("destination.city.id", json!("new_orleans")),
            a("planned_distance.km", json!(34)),
            a("car_job.market", json!("dispatch_job")),
        ];
        let car = JobInfo::from_config_of(Game::Ats, JobType::Car, &attrs).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(car.fingerprint.route.job_type, JobType::Car);
        assert_eq!(car.fingerprint.route.job_market, "dispatch_job");
        assert!(car.cargo_loaded);
        let freight = JobInfo::from_config(Game::Ats, &attrs).unwrap();
        assert_ne!(freight.fingerprint.route, car.fingerprint.route);
    }

    #[test]
    fn cargo_switch_keeps_the_route_key() {
        let a1 = JobInfo::from_config(Game::Ats, &tyres(true, "tyres")).unwrap();
        let a2 = JobInfo::from_config(Game::Ats, &tyres(true, "dynamite")).unwrap();

    }

        assert_eq!(d.auto_load_used, None);
    }
```

`crates/pt-core/src/projection.rs`:

```rs
//! Game world X/Z (metres) → WGS84 longitude/latitude (PLAN §8), so a route
//! lines up with basemap tiles generated by truckermudgeon/maps.
//!
//! Both games use a spherical Lambert conformal conic projection whose
//! parameters are in each game's `def/climate.sii`. The maths is the standard
//! one (Snyder, "Map Projections: A Working Manual", USGS 1987, §15), written
//! here from the formulas. The ETS2 UK correction (UK content is authored 0.75×
//! smaller, around Calais) follows truckermudgeon/maps, credited, not copied.

use crate::game::Game;

/// The sphere's radius cancels out (game metres are scaled by a length per
/// degree of the same sphere); Clarke 1866 authalic, as the basemap uses.
const EARTH_RADIUS_M: f64 = 6_370_997.0;

fn length_of_degree() -> f64 {
    EARTH_RADIUS_M * std::f64::consts::PI / 180.0
}

/// A spherical Lambert conformal conic with two standard parallels.
struct Lcc {
    n: f64,
    rf: f64,
    rho0: f64,
    lon0: f64,
}

fn t(lat: f64) -> f64 {
    (std::f64::consts::FRAC_PI_4 + lat / 2.0).tan()
}

impl Lcc {
    fn new(lat1: f64, lat2: f64, lat0: f64, lon0: f64) -> Lcc {
        let (p1, p2, p0) = (lat1.to_radians(), lat2.to_radians(), lat0.to_radians());
        let n = (p1.cos() / p2.cos()).ln() / (t(p2) / t(p1)).ln();
        let rf = EARTH_RADIUS_M * p1.cos() * t(p1).powf(n) / n;
        Lcc { n, rf, rho0: rf / t(p0).powf(n), lon0: lon0.to_radians() }
    }

    /// Projected metres → (lon, lat) in degrees.
    fn inverse(&self, x: f64, y: f64) -> [f64; 2] {
        let s = self.n.signum();
        let dy = self.rho0 - y;
        let rho = s * (x * x + dy * dy).sqrt();
        let theta = (s * x).atan2(s * dy);
        let lat = 2.0 * (self.rf / rho).powf(1.0 / self.n).atan() - std::f64::consts::FRAC_PI_2;
        [(self.lon0 + theta / self.n).to_degrees(), lat.to_degrees()]
    }

    /// (lon, lat) in degrees → projected metres.
    fn forward(&self, lon: f64, lat: f64) -> [f64; 2] {
        let rho = self.rf / t(lat.to_radians()).powf(self.n);
        let theta = self.n * (lon.to_radians() - self.lon0);
        [rho * theta.sin(), self.rho0 - rho * theta.cos()]
    }
}

/// One game's `def/climate.sii` projection.
struct Params {
    lat1: f64,
    lat2: f64,
    lat0: f64,
    lon0: f64,
    /// `map_factor`: [for Z, for X].
    factor: [f64; 2],
    /// `map_offset`, subtracted first (ETS2 only).
    offset: [f64; 2],
}

const ATS: Params = Params {
    lat1: 33.0,
    lat2: 45.0,
    lat0: 39.0,
    lon0: -96.0,
    factor: [-0.00017706234, 0.000176689948],
    offset: [0.0, 0.0],
};

const ETS2: Params = Params {
    lat1: 37.0,
    lat2: 65.0,
    lat0: 50.0,
    lon0: 15.0,
    factor: [-0.000171570875, 0.0001729241463],
    offset: [16660.0, 4150.0],
};

/// ETS2's UK: 4 km map sectors up and to the left of the one holding Calais.
const SECTOR_M: f64 = 4000.0;
const UK_SCALE: f64 = 0.75;
const CALAIS: [f64; 2] = [-31100.0, -5500.0];

fn in_uk(x: f64, z: f64) -> bool {
    let (sx, sz) = ((x / SECTOR_M).floor(), (z / SECTOR_M).floor());
    sx <= -8.0 && sz <= -2.0 && !(sx == -8.0 && sz == -2.0)
}

fn params(game: Game) -> &'static Params {
    match game {
        Game::Ats => &ATS,
        Game::Ets2 => &ETS2,
    }
}

fn lcc(p: &Params) -> Lcc {
    Lcc::new(p.lat1, p.lat2, p.lat0, p.lon0)
}

/// Game world X and Z (the SDK's `placement` x and z, metres) → `[lon, lat]`.
pub fn to_lon_lat(game: Game, x: f64, z: f64) -> [f64; 2] {
    let p = params(game);
    let (mut gx, mut gz) = (x - p.offset[0], z - p.offset[1]);
    if game == Game::Ets2 && in_uk(x, z) {
        gx = (gx + CALAIS[0] / 2.0) * UK_SCALE;
        gz = (gz + CALAIS[1] / 2.0) * UK_SCALE;
    }
    let deg = length_of_degree();
    lcc(p).inverse(gx * p.factor[1] * deg, gz * p.factor[0] * deg)
}

/// `[lon, lat]` → game world X and Z; the inverse of [`to_lon_lat`].
pub fn from_lon_lat(game: Game, lon: f64, lat: f64) -> [f64; 2] {
    let p = params(game);
    let deg = length_of_degree();
    let [px, py] = lcc(p).forward(lon, lat);
    let (mut gx, mut gz) = (px / p.factor[1] / deg, py / p.factor[0] / deg);
    if game == Game::Ets2 {
        let (ux, uz) = (gx / UK_SCALE - CALAIS[0] / 2.0, gz / UK_SCALE - CALAIS[1] / 2.0);
        if in_uk(ux + p.offset[0], uz + p.offset[1]) {
            (gx, gz) = (ux, uz);
        }
    }
    [gx + p.offset[0], gz + p.offset[1]]
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    /// Reference points from truckermudgeon/maps' own tests, so routes line up
    /// with its tiles: (game, game X/Z, lon/lat).
    const POINTS: [(Game, [f64; 2], [f64; 2]); 4] = [
        (Game::Ats, [-85_672.0, 7870.0], [-114.92606131601985, 36.00959614633237]), // near Las Vegas
        (Game::Ets2, [-40_169.0, -10_685.0], [-0.5943602137854889, 51.29443960532431]), // south of London (UK)
        (Game::Ets2, [62_276.0, 84_880.0], [24.63877984644102, 35.391305791648065]), // Crete
        (Game::Ets2, [-30_120.0, 5_847.0], [2.2454398875049852, 48.96983557895307]), // Paris
    ];

    #[test]
    fn known_points() {
        for (game, xz, ll) in POINTS {
            let got = to_lon_lat(game, xz[0], xz[1]);
            assert!((got[0] - ll[0]).abs() < 1e-9 && (got[1] - ll[1]).abs() < 1e-9, "{game:?} {xz:?}: {got:?} != {ll:?}");
            let back = from_lon_lat(game, ll[0], ll[1]);
            assert!((back[0] - xz[0]).abs() < 1e-5 && (back[1] - xz[1]).abs() < 1e-5, "{game:?} {ll:?}: {back:?} != {xz:?}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn uk_sectors() {
        assert!(in_uk(-40_169.0, -10_685.0));
        assert!(!in_uk(-30_120.0, 5_847.0));
        // The sector holding Calais itself is the continent.
        assert!(!in_uk(-31_100.0, -5_500.0));
        assert!(in_uk(-32_001.0, -5_500.0));
    }
}
```

```rs
//! Scoring (PLAN §6), evaluated on a job's kept timeline.
//!
//! Distances (decided and measured 2026-09-28):
//! - Only loaded, hitched driving counts; World of Trucks jobs count everything.
//! - The game's `job.delivered` `distance.km` is game scale, whole km, includes
//!   the empty leg and comes from the save. It is cross-checked against the
//!   tracked whole-job odometer distance; the uncounted legs are then subtracted
//!   and the rest converted to 1:1 with the job's own world/game ratio.

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

use crate::config::{Config, ReviewAction, ScaleClass};
use crate::job::JobInfo;
use crate::store::{InMemory, Resolve};
use crate::timeline::{Job, Point, StartKind};

/// A bonus-cargo entry (server-side table, PLAN §7 `bonus_cargo`).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Bonus {
    /// Server id (`bon_…`); empty in tests.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub id: String,
    pub game: crate::game::Game,
    /// Matched against `cargo.id`, ignoring case: equal when `exact`, else a glob
    /// where `*` is any run of characters and `?` one character.
    pub cargo_match: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub exact: bool,
    pub kind: BonusKind,
    pub amount: f64,

    /// delivery time.
    pub active_from_ms: Option<i64>,
    pub active_to_ms: Option<i64>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]

/// Facts from outside the trace.

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(tag = "reason", rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum ReviewReason {
    /// Rule 3.
    LongJob { world_km: f64 },
    /// The whole job averaged more than the threshold in 1:1 km per real
    /// (unpaused) minute: a speed hack or a boosted truck.
    FastAverage { world_km: f64, driving_min: f64, world_km_per_min: f64 },
    /// The same timed by the game's clock (in-game minutes converted back to
    /// real minutes at the game's time rate).
    FastAverageGame { world_km: f64, game_clock_min: f64, world_km_per_min: f64 },
    /// Rule 4: fuel used below −tolerance in a tracked run.
    NegativeFuel { run: u32, used_l: f64 },
    /// Rule 4: fuel rose outside a detected refuel.

    DistanceMismatch { delivered_km: f64, tracked_km: f64, tolerance_km: f64 },

    /// `review_over_income_per_game_mi`, or more in all than `review_over_income`.

    /// The game ran faster than real time (the `warp` console command): the
    /// fastest 30 s of real time, and the game seconds gained over all of them.

}

impl ReviewReason {

            ReviewReason::LongJob { .. } => "long_job",
            ReviewReason::FastAverage { .. } => "fast_average",
            ReviewReason::FastAverageGame { .. } => "fast_average_game",
            ReviewReason::NegativeFuel { .. } => "negative_fuel",
            ReviewReason::FuelJump { .. } => "fuel_jump",
            ReviewReason::Gap { .. } => "gap",
            ReviewReason::LateStart => "late_start",
            ReviewReason::CargoSwitch => "cargo_switch",
            ReviewReason::DistanceMismatch { .. } => "distance_mismatch",
            ReviewReason::NoDeliveredDistance => "no_delivered_distance",
            ReviewReason::TimeWarp { .. } => "time_warp",
            ReviewReason::HighIncome { .. } => "high_income",
        }
    }
}

fn glob(pat: &str, s: &str) -> bool {
    match pat.split_once('*') {
        None => pat.len() == s.len() && pat.chars().zip(s.chars()).all(|(p, c)| p == '?' || p == c),
        Some((pre, rest)) => {
            if s.len() < pre.len() || !s.is_char_boundary(pre.len()) || !glob(pre, &s[..pre.len()]) {
                return false;
            }
            let tail = &s[pre.len()..];
            (0..=tail.len()).any(|i| tail.is_char_boundary(i) && glob(rest, &tail[i..]))
        }
    }
}

/// The `warp` console command (0.0001-60) runs every game clock faster than
/// real time: simulation, paused simulation, render and the in-game clock (the
/// owner's ATS test, 2026-10-16). The truck's speed and the pace checks look
/// normal, so only the player's PC clock (`wall_ms`) shows it. Game time is
/// compared with real time over windows of this much real driving.
pub const TIME_WARP_WINDOW_S: f64 = 30.0;
/// A window whose game time ran more than this much faster than real time is
/// warped. Honest play stays within 1.047 (38 sessions, both games, capture
/// mode included); `warp 2` reads 2.0.
pub const TIME_WARP_OVER: f64 = 1.15;
/// Pairs further apart in real time are a pause or a stall, and are left out
/// (they would only lower the ratio, so pausing cannot hide a warp).
const TIME_WARP_MAX_STEP_S: f64 = 5.0;

/// The fastest warped window and the game seconds gained in all of them.
fn time_warp(kept: impl Iterator<Item = Point>) -> Option<(f64, f64)> {
    let (mut sim, mut wall, mut max, mut gained) = (0.0, 0.0, 0.0f64, 0.0);
    for (a, b) in pairs(kept) {
        let ds = b.sim_us.saturating_sub(a.sim_us) as f64 / 1e6;
        let dw = (b.wall_ms - a.wall_ms) as f64 / 1000.0;
        if ds <= 0.0 || ds > 60.0 || dw <= 0.0 || dw >= TIME_WARP_MAX_STEP_S {
            continue;
        }
        sim += ds;
        wall += dw;
        if wall >= TIME_WARP_WINDOW_S {
            let factor = sim / wall;
            if factor > TIME_WARP_OVER {
                max = max.max(factor);
                gained += sim - wall;
            }
            (sim, wall) = (0.0, 0.0);
        }
    }
    (max > 0.0).then_some((max, gained))
}

/// Neighbouring kept points of the same run: the only pairs that accumulate.
fn pairs(kept: impl Iterator<Item = Point>) -> impl Iterator<Item = (Point, Point)> {
    let mut prev: Option<Point> = None;
    kept.filter_map(move |b| {
        let a = prev.replace(b.clone());
        a.filter(|a| a.run == b.run && a.truck == b.truck).map(|a| (a, b))
    })
}

fn distances<P, R: Resolve<P> + ?Sized>(job: &Job<P>, pts: &R, cfg: &Config) -> Distances {
    let wot = job.info.is_world_of_trucks();
    let vanilla = cfg.map.scale.vanilla(job.game);
    let eps = cfg.rules.distance.odometer_epsilon_km;
    let mut d = Distances::default();
    let mut by_scale: Vec<(ScaleClass, f64)> = Vec::new();
    let mut world_by_scale: Vec<(ScaleClass, f64)> = Vec::new();
    let mut add = |d: &mut Distances, km: f64, counted: bool, scale: f64| {
        d.tracked_whole_game_km += km;
        if counted || wot {
            d.tracked_counted_game_km += km;
            d.tracked_counted_world_km += km / scale;
            let class = vanilla.classify(Some(scale));
            for (list, v) in [(&mut by_scale, km), (&mut world_by_scale, km / scale)] {
                match list.iter_mut().find(|(c, _)| *c == class) {
                    Some((_, x)) => *x += v,
                    None => list.push((class, v)),
                }
            }
        } else {
            d.tracked_uncounted_game_km += km;
        }
    };
    for (a, b) in pairs(pts.iter(&job.kept)) {
        let (Some(x), Some(y)) = (a.odometer_km, b.odometer_km) else { continue };
        let km = y - x;
        if km < -eps {
            d.negative_km += -km;
            continue;
        }
        d.driven_whole_world_km += km.max(0.0) / b.local_scale;
        d.driven_s += b.sim_us.saturating_sub(a.sim_us) as f64 / 1e6;
        if let (Some(ta), Some(tb)) = (a.game_time_min, b.game_time_min) {
            let mod_clock = if b.truckersmp { None } else { cfg.multiplayer.mod_clock(b.mp_mod.as_deref()) };
            // A mod's server pulls the game's own steps back by a minute
            // (TrucklineMP, 2026-10-23: 100 times in 18 min), so its steps
            // count signed and cancel; elsewhere a step back counts as 0.
            let game_min = if mod_clock.is_some() { tb as f64 - ta as f64 } else { tb.saturating_sub(ta) as f64 };
            // Singleplayer time runs at local.scale; TruckersMP and some mods at their server rate.
            let rate = if b.truckersmp { cfg.rules.truckersmp_game_min_per_real_min } else { mod_clock.unwrap_or(b.local_scale) };
            d.driven_game_min += game_min;
            d.driven_game_clock_min += game_min / rate;
        }
        let counted = b.cargo_loaded && b.trailer_connected;
        if counted || wot {
            d.driven_counted_game_km += km.max(0.0);
            d.driven_counted_world_km += km.max(0.0) / b.local_scale;
        }
        add(&mut d, km.max(0.0), counted, b.local_scale);
    }
    for g in job.active_gaps_in(pts) {
        if let Some(km) = g.game_km.filter(|k| *k > 0.0) {
            add(&mut d, km, g.counted, g.local_scale);
        }
    }
    d.game_km_by_scale = by_scale;
    d.world_km_by_scale = world_by_scale;
    d
}

fn speed<P, R: Resolve<P> + ?Sized>(job: &Job<P>, pts: &R, cfg: &Config) -> SpeedStats {
    let (penalty_mph, invalid_mph) = cfg.rules.speed.limits_for(job.game, job.info.fingerprint.route.job_type);
    let prec = cfg.rules.speed.compare_precision_mph;
    let window = cfg.rules.speed.sustained_window_s;
    let mut s = SpeedStats::default();
    // Episodes: consecutive over-limit points of one run, timed in paused
    // simulation time, so pausing neither adds time nor splits an episode.
    let mut ep_pen: Option<u64> = None;
    let mut ep_inv: Option<u64> = None;
    let mut prev: Option<Point> = None;
    for p in pts.iter(&job.kept) {
        s.peak_mph = s.peak_mph.max(p.mph());
        if prev.as_ref().is_some_and(|q| q.run != p.run) || p.after_teleport {
            ep_pen = None;
            ep_inv = None;
        }
        if let Some(q) = prev.as_ref().filter(|q| q.run == p.run && !p.after_teleport) {
            let dt = p.sim_us.saturating_sub(q.sim_us) as f64 / 1e6;
            if exceeds(q.mph(), penalty_mph, prec) && exceeds(p.mph(), penalty_mph, prec) {
                s.over_penalty_s += dt;
            }
            if exceeds(q.mph(), invalid_mph, prec) && exceeds(p.mph(), invalid_mph, prec) {
                s.over_invalid_s += dt;
            }
        }
        for (limit, ep, flag) in [
            (penalty_mph, &mut ep_pen, &mut s.penalty),
            (invalid_mph, &mut ep_inv, &mut s.invalid),
        ] {
            if exceeds(p.mph(), limit, prec) {
                let since = *ep.get_or_insert(p.sim_us);
                if p.sim_us.saturating_sub(since) as f64 / 1e6 > window {
                    *flag = true;
                }
            } else {
                *ep = None;
            }
        }
        prev = Some(p);
    }
    s
}

/// What the fuel rules read of a point. One run at a time is held in memory,
/// so this keeps it small.
struct FuelPoint {
    run: u32,
    wall_ms: i64,
    sim_us: u64,
    fuel_l: Option<f64>,
    mph: f64,
    after_teleport: bool,
}

impl FuelPoint {
    fn of(p: &Point) -> FuelPoint {
        FuelPoint {
            run: p.run,
            wall_ms: p.wall_ms,
            sim_us: p.sim_us,
            fuel_l: p.fuel_l,
            mph: p.mph(),
            after_teleport: p.after_teleport,
        }
    }
}

/// Refuel episodes and rule 4 per run.
fn fuel<P, R: Resolve<P> + ?Sized>(job: &Job<P>, pts: &R, cfg: &Config, review: &mut Vec<ReviewReason>) -> Vec<Refuel> {
    let mut refuels = Vec::new();
    // A run ends where the run id or the truck changes.
    let mut run: Vec<FuelPoint> = Vec::new();
    let mut key: Option<(u32, u32)> = None;
    for p in pts.iter(&job.kept) {
        if key.is_some_and(|k| k != (p.run, p.truck)) {
            fuel_run(&run, cfg, review, &mut refuels);
            run.clear();
        }
        key = Some((p.run, p.truck));
        run.push(FuelPoint::of(&p));
    }
    if !run.is_empty() {
        fuel_run(&run, cfg, review, &mut refuels);
    }
    refuels
}

fn fuel_run(run: &[FuelPoint], cfg: &Config, review: &mut Vec<ReviewReason>, refuels: &mut Vec<Refuel>) {
    let r = &cfg.rules.refuel;
    let f = &cfg.rules.fuel;
    // Fuel rises while stationary, in steps (every 0.3 s of simulation in
    // ATS 1.61), so zero-change samples inside an episode are allowed.
    let mut refuelled = 0.0;
    let mut in_refuel = vec![false; run.len()];
    let mut i = 1;
    while i < run.len() {
        let rising = |k: usize| match (run[k - 1].fuel_l, run[k].fuel_l) {
            (Some(a), Some(b)) => b - a > 1e-6,
            _ => false,
        };
        let still = |k: usize| run[k].mph < r.stationary_below_mph;
        if !(rising(i) && still(i)) {
            i += 1;
            continue;
        }
        let first = i;
        let mut last = i;
        let mut k = i + 1;
        while k < run.len() && still(k) && run[k].sim_us.saturating_sub(run[last].sim_us) <= 2_000_000 {
            if rising(k) {
                last = k;
            }
            k += 1;
        }
        let litres = run[last].fuel_l.unwrap_or(0.0) - run[first - 1].fuel_l.unwrap_or(0.0);
        let dur = run[last].sim_us.saturating_sub(run[first - 1].sim_us) as f64 / 1e6;
        let rate = if dur > 0.0 { litres / dur } else { f64::INFINITY };
        if dur >= r.min_duration_s && rate >= r.min_rate_l_per_s && rate <= r.max_rate_l_per_s {
            refuelled += litres;
            refuels.push(Refuel { wall_ms: run[first].wall_ms, litres, duration_s: dur });
            for flag in &mut in_refuel[first..=last] {
                *flag = true;
            }
        }
        i = last + 1;
    }
    // Fuel that changes across a teleport is ignored, like across a load:
    // World of Trucks event portals (Brackenreach, owner 2026-10-15) fill
    // the tank as they move the truck.
    let mut teleported = 0.0;
    for k in 1..run.len() {
        if let (Some(a), Some(b)) = (run[k - 1].fuel_l, run[k].fuel_l) {
            if run[k].after_teleport {
                teleported += b - a;
            } else if !in_refuel[k] && b - a > f.mid_job_jump_tolerance_l {
                review.push(ReviewReason::FuelJump { wall_ms: run[k].wall_ms, litres: b - a });
            }
        }
    }
    if let (Some(a), Some(b)) = (run.first().and_then(|p| p.fuel_l), run.last().and_then(|p| p.fuel_l)) {
        let used = a - b + refuelled + teleported;
        if used < -f.negative_fuel_tolerance_l {
            review.push(ReviewReason::NegativeFuel { run: run[0].run, used_l: used });
        }
    }
}

fn pick_bonus(info: &JobInfo, base: f64, ctx: &Context) -> Option<(Bonus, f64)> {
    let cargo = &info.fingerprint.cargo.cargo_id;
    let game = info.fingerprint.route.game;
    ctx.bonuses
        .iter()
        .filter(|b| {
            b.game == game
                && if b.exact {
                    b.cargo_match.eq_ignore_ascii_case(cargo)
                } else {
                    glob(&b.cargo_match.to_ascii_lowercase(), &cargo.to_ascii_lowercase())
                }
        })
        .filter(|b| match ctx.delivered_at_ms {
            Some(t) => b.active_from_ms.is_none_or(|from| from <= t) && b.active_to_ms.is_none_or(|to| t < to),
            None => true,
        })
        .map(|b| {
            let pts = match b.kind {
                BonusKind::Flat => base + b.amount,
                BonusKind::Multiplier => base * b.amount,
            };
            (b.clone(), pts)
        })
        .fold(None, |best: Option<(Bonus, f64)>, c| match best {
            Some(b) if b.1 >= c.1 => Some(b),
            _ => Some(c),
        })
}

/// Scores a job. Works on any state; only a delivered job gets an outcome
/// other than `Incomplete`.
pub fn evaluate(job: &Job, cfg: &Config, ctx: &Context) -> JobResult {
    evaluate_in(job, &InMemory, cfg, ctx)
}

/// [`evaluate`] for a job whose points are held anywhere (`pts` reads them):
/// a live timeline's [`crate::store::PointStore`]. It streams over the points
/// a few times and never holds more than one run of them.
pub fn evaluate_in<P, R: Resolve<P> + ?Sized>(job: &Job<P>, pts: &R, cfg: &Config, ctx: &Context) -> JobResult {
    let r = &cfg.rules;
    let mut review = Vec::new();
    let mut d = distances(job, pts, cfg);
    let speed = speed(job, pts, cfg);
    let refuels = fuel(job, pts, cfg, &mut review);
    let truckersmp = pts.iter(&job.kept).any(|p| p.truckersmp);
    // TruckersMP decides first; a job on a mod is that mod, not Convoy.
    let multiplayer_mod = if truckersmp { None } else { pts.iter(&job.kept).find_map(|p| p.mp_mod) };
    // TruckersMP also reports a multiplayer time offset (2026-09-28 capture), so a
    // non-zero offset means Convoy only when TruckersMP is not loaded.
    let convoy = !truckersmp && multiplayer_mod.is_none() && pts.iter(&job.kept).any(|p| p.mp_time_offset != 0);

    // Distance: the game's figure, cross-checked, minus uncounted legs, to 1:1.
    d.delivered_game_km = job.delivered.as_ref().and_then(|x| x.distance_km);
    // The job's own mix of city and road scale, from driving only: a gap (a
    // forward load, possibly a save edit) carries just one scale reading.
    let ratio = if d.driven_counted_game_km > 0.0 {
        d.driven_counted_world_km / d.driven_counted_game_km
    } else {
        1.0 / cfg.map.scale.vanilla(job.game).main_road_local_scale()
    };
    match d.delivered_game_km {
        Some(delivered) => {
            let tol_km = r.distance.delivered_vs_trace_tolerance_mi(km_to_mi(delivered)) / crate::units::MI_PER_KM
                + r.distance.delivered_distance_resolution_km;
            let off = match job.start {
                // Only the part that was seen can be checked: the game may know more.
                StartKind::LateStart => (d.tracked_whole_game_km - delivered).max(0.0),
                StartKind::Tracked => (delivered - d.tracked_whole_game_km).abs(),
            };
            if off > tol_km && cfg.review_policy.trace_checks == ReviewAction::Review {
                review.push(ReviewReason::DistanceMismatch {
                    delivered_km: delivered,
                    tracked_km: d.tracked_whole_game_km,
                    tolerance_km: tol_km,
                });
            }
            d.counted_game_km = if job.info.is_world_of_trucks() {
                delivered
            } else {
                (delivered - d.tracked_uncounted_game_km).max(0.0)
            };
        }
        None => {
            if job.delivered.is_some() {
                review.push(ReviewReason::NoDeliveredDistance);
            }
            d.counted_game_km = d.tracked_counted_game_km;
        }
    }
    d.world_km = d.counted_game_km * ratio;
    d.world_mi = km_to_mi(d.world_km);
    d.game_mi = km_to_mi(d.counted_game_km);

    // Review reasons from the timeline and rule 3.
    let policy = &cfg.review_policy;
    let gaps = job
        .active_gaps_in(pts)
        .into_iter()
        .filter(|g| g.kind == crate::timeline::GapKind::Load)
        .filter(|g| {
            let mi = km_to_mi(g.game_km.unwrap_or(f64::INFINITY).abs());
            !(mi < policy.min_gap_distance_mi && g.duration_s < policy.min_gap_duration_s)
        })
        .count();
    if gaps > 0 && policy.gap == ReviewAction::Review {
        review.push(ReviewReason::Gap { count: gaps });
    }
    if job.start == StartKind::LateStart && policy.late_start == ReviewAction::Review {
        review.push(ReviewReason::LateStart);
    }
    if job.cargo_switched {
        review.push(ReviewReason::CargoSwitch);
    }
    if exceeds(d.world_km, r.manual_review_over_world_km, r.distance.compare_precision_km) {
        review.push(ReviewReason::LongJob { world_km: d.world_km });
    }
    if let Some(income) = job.delivered.as_ref().and_then(|x| x.revenue) {
        let game_mi = km_to_mi(d.delivered_game_km.unwrap_or(d.tracked_whole_game_km));
        let per_game_mi = if game_mi > 0.0 { income as f64 / game_mi } else { 0.0 };
        let per_mile = r.review_over_income_per_game_mi.is_some_and(|limit| game_mi > 0.0 && per_game_mi > limit);
        let total = r.review_over_income.is_some_and(|limit| income as f64 > limit);
        if per_mile || total {
            review.push(ReviewReason::HighIncome { income, game_mi, per_game_mi });
        }
    }
    if d.driven_s >= r.average_pace_min_driving_s {
        let minutes = d.driven_s / 60.0;
        let pace = d.driven_whole_world_km / minutes;
        if pace > r.review_over_average_world_km_per_min {
            review.push(ReviewReason::FastAverage {
                world_km: d.driven_whole_world_km,
                driving_min: minutes,
                world_km_per_min: pace,
            });
        }
    }
    if d.driven_game_min >= r.average_pace_min_game_min && d.driven_game_clock_min > 0.0 {
        let pace = d.driven_whole_world_km / d.driven_game_clock_min;
        if pace > r.review_over_average_world_km_per_game_clock_min {
            review.push(ReviewReason::FastAverageGame {
                world_km: d.driven_whole_world_km,
                game_clock_min: d.driven_game_clock_min,
                world_km_per_min: pace,
            });
        }
    }
    if policy.trace_checks == ReviewAction::Review {
        if let Some((max_factor, gained_s)) = time_warp(pts.iter(&job.kept)) {
            review.push(ReviewReason::TimeWarp { max_factor, gained_s });
        }
    }

    // Points: rules 5, 6, 7 (bonus on the cargo first tracked after a switch).
    let accepted = if speed.penalty { d.world_mi * r.speed_penalty_factor } else { d.world_mi };
    let base = accepted * r.points_per_world_mi;
    let (bonus, points_raw) = match pick_bonus(&job.first_info, base, ctx) {
        Some((b, p)) => (Some(b), p),
        None => (None, base),
    };

    let discard = if ctx.integrity_ok == Some(false) {
        Some(DiscardReason::Integrity)
    } else if d.negative_km > r.distance.odometer_epsilon_km {
        Some(DiscardReason::NegativeDistance)
    } else if ctx.singleplayer_division && truckersmp {
        Some(DiscardReason::SingleplayerDivisionTruckersmp)
    } else if ctx.singleplayer_division
        && multiplayer_mod.as_deref().and_then(|k| cfg.multiplayer.find_mod(k)).is_some_and(|m| m.singleplayer_division_discard)
    {
        Some(DiscardReason::SingleplayerDivisionMultiplayerMod)
    } else {
        None
    };
    // A delivered job keeps its result even when a later load stops its tracking.
    let outcome = if job.delivered.is_none() {
        Outcome::Incomplete
    } else if discard.is_some() {
        Outcome::Discarded
    } else if speed.invalid {
        Outcome::Invalid
    } else if !review.is_empty() {
        Outcome::PendingReview
    } else {
        Outcome::Valid
    };
    let points = match outcome {
        Outcome::Discarded | Outcome::Invalid => 0.0,
        _ => r.floor_points(points_raw),
    };
    JobResult {
        outcome,
        discard,
        review,
        distances: d,
        speed,
        refuels,
        accepted_world_mi: accepted,
        bonus,
        points_raw,
        points,
        truckersmp,
        convoy,
        multiplayer_mod,
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn glob_matching() {
        assert!(glob("dynamite", "dynamite"));
        assert!(glob("dyna*", "dynamite"));
        assert!(glob("*mite", "dynamite"));
        assert!(glob("d*n*e", "dynamite"));
        assert!(!glob("dyna", "dynamite"));
        assert!(!glob("x*", "dynamite"));
        assert!(glob("dyn?mite", "dynamite"));
        assert!(glob("d?n*", "dynamite"));
        assert!(!glob("dyn?", "dynamite"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn review_codes_match_the_serialised_tag() {
        let all = [
            ReviewReason::LongJob { world_km: 1.0 },
            ReviewReason::FastAverage { world_km: 1.0, driving_min: 1.0, world_km_per_min: 1.0 },
            ReviewReason::FastAverageGame { world_km: 1.0, game_clock_min: 1.0, world_km_per_min: 1.0 },
            ReviewReason::NegativeFuel { run: 1, used_l: -1.0 },
            ReviewReason::FuelJump { wall_ms: 1, litres: 1.0 },
            ReviewReason::Gap { count: 1 },
            ReviewReason::LateStart,
            ReviewReason::CargoSwitch,
            ReviewReason::DistanceMismatch { delivered_km: 1.0, tracked_km: 1.0, tolerance_km: 1.0 },
            ReviewReason::NoDeliveredDistance,
            ReviewReason::TimeWarp { max_factor: 2.0, gained_s: 30.0 },
            ReviewReason::HighIncome { income: 1, game_mi: 1.0, per_game_mi: 1.0 },
        ];
        for r in all {
            assert_eq!(serde_json::to_value(&r).unwrap()["reason"], r.code());
        }
    }
}
```

`crates/pt-core/src/store.rs`:

```rs
//! Where a live timeline keeps its points (scorer memory, 2026-10-20).
//!
//! A job's kept timeline and each of its reverted branches is a *track*: an
//! ordered list of points behind a [`TrackId`]. The timeline only holds the ids;
//! the points live in a [`PointStore`]. The client keeps them in memory
//! ([`VecStore`]); the server's scorer keeps them on its Durable Object's disk,
//! so a job driven for days no longer has to fit in 128 MB.

use std::collections::BTreeMap;

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

use crate::timeline::Point;

/// One track of a [`PointStore`].
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(transparent)]
pub struct TrackId(pub u32);

/// Ordered point lists. Indexes are positions within a track, from 0.
pub trait PointStore {
    /// A new, empty track.
    fn create(&mut self) -> TrackId;
    /// Forgets a track and its points.
    fn remove(&mut self, t: TrackId);
    fn len(&self, t: TrackId) -> usize;
    fn get(&self, t: TrackId, i: usize) -> Option<Point>;
    fn push(&mut self, t: TrackId, p: Point);
    /// Moves the points from `at` on into a new track (empty when `at` is the
    /// length) and returns it.
    fn split_off(&mut self, t: TrackId, at: usize) -> TrackId;
    /// Moves every point of `src` to the end of `dst`; `src` is gone after.
    fn append(&mut self, dst: TrackId, src: TrackId);
    /// The points in order.
    fn iter(&self, t: TrackId) -> Box<dyn Iterator<Item = Point> + '_>;

    fn is_empty(&self, t: TrackId) -> bool {
        self.len(t) == 0
    }

    fn last(&self, t: TrackId) -> Option<Point> {
        self.len(t).checked_sub(1).and_then(|i| self.get(t, i))
    }

    /// Points that may lie within `radius` world metres of `pos`, with their
    /// index, in order. A store may return more (the caller still measures);
    /// it must not leave out a point that is within the radius.
    fn near(&self, t: TrackId, pos: [f64; 3], radius: f64) -> Box<dyn Iterator<Item = (usize, Point)> + '_> {
        let _ = (pos, radius);
        Box::new(self.iter(t).enumerate())
    }

    /// Index of the first point that satisfies `pred`.
    fn position(&self, t: TrackId, pred: &dyn Fn(&Point) -> bool) -> Option<usize> {
        self.iter(t).position(|p| pred(&p))
    }

    /// The whole track in memory.
    fn to_vec(&self, t: TrackId) -> Vec<Point> {
        self.iter(t).collect()
    }

    /// Gives back spare memory, where that means anything.
    fn shrink_to_fit(&mut self) {}
}

/// Every point in memory: the client, replays and tests.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct VecStore {
    next: u32,
    tracks: BTreeMap<TrackId, Vec<Point>>,
}

impl VecStore {
    pub fn new() -> VecStore {
        VecStore::default()
    }

    fn track(&self, t: TrackId) -> &[Point] {
        self.tracks.get(&t).map_or(&[], Vec::as_slice)
    }

    fn track_mut(&mut self, t: TrackId) -> &mut Vec<Point> {
        self.tracks.entry(t).or_default()
    }
}

impl PointStore for VecStore {
    fn create(&mut self) -> TrackId {
        let t = TrackId(self.next);
        self.next += 1;
        self.tracks.insert(t, Vec::new());
        t
    }

    fn remove(&mut self, t: TrackId) {
        self.tracks.remove(&t);
    }

    fn len(&self, t: TrackId) -> usize {
        self.track(t).len()
    }

    fn get(&self, t: TrackId, i: usize) -> Option<Point> {
        self.track(t).get(i).cloned()
    }

    fn push(&mut self, t: TrackId, p: Point) {
        self.track_mut(t).push(p);
    }

    fn split_off(&mut self, t: TrackId, at: usize) -> TrackId {
        let tail = self.track_mut(t).split_off(at);
        let n = self.create();
        *self.track_mut(n) = tail;
        n
    }

    fn append(&mut self, dst: TrackId, src: TrackId) {
        let mut moved = self.tracks.remove(&src).unwrap_or_default();
        self.track_mut(dst).append(&mut moved);
    }

    fn iter(&self, t: TrackId) -> Box<dyn Iterator<Item = Point> + '_> {
        Box::new(self.track(t).iter().cloned())
    }

    fn position(&self, t: TrackId, pred: &dyn Fn(&Point) -> bool) -> Option<usize> {
        self.track(t).iter().position(pred)
    }

    fn to_vec(&self, t: TrackId) -> Vec<Point> {
        self.track(t).to_vec()
    }

    fn shrink_to_fit(&mut self) {
        for v in self.tracks.values_mut() {
            v.shrink_to_fit();
        }
    }
}

/// Reads a job's point lists, whatever holds them: `Vec<Point>` (a finished,
/// stored job) through [`InMemory`], a [`TrackId`] through its store.
pub trait Resolve<P: ?Sized> {
    fn iter<'a>(&'a self, points: &'a P) -> Box<dyn Iterator<Item = Point> + 'a>;
}

/// Point lists that are plain vectors.
pub struct InMemory;

impl Resolve<Vec<Point>> for InMemory {
    fn iter<'a>(&'a self, points: &'a Vec<Point>) -> Box<dyn Iterator<Item = Point> + 'a> {
        Box::new(points.iter().cloned())
    }
}

impl<S: PointStore + ?Sized> Resolve<TrackId> for S {
    fn iter<'a>(&'a self, points: &'a TrackId) -> Box<dyn Iterator<Item = Point> + 'a> {
        PointStore::iter(self, *points)
    }
}

/// Points as compact bytes (a stored block or segment). Every field round-trips
/// bit for bit, so scores from decoded points are the same.
pub fn encode_points(points: &[Point]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(5 + points.len() * 96);
    out.push(CODEC_VERSION);
    out.extend_from_slice(&(points.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());
    for p in points {
        let flags: u16 = (p.odometer_km.is_some() as u16)
            | (p.fuel_l.is_some() as u16) << 1
            | (p.pos.is_some() as u16) << 2
            | (p.game_time_min.is_some() as u16) << 3
            | (p.cargo_loaded as u16) << 4
            | (p.trailer_connected as u16) << 5
            | (p.truckersmp as u16) << 6
            | (p.after_teleport as u16) << 7
            | (p.cargo_damage.is_some() as u16) << 8
            | (p.mp_mod.is_some() as u16) << 9;
        out.extend_from_slice(&flags.to_le_bytes());
        out.extend_from_slice(&p.sess.to_le_bytes());
        out.extend_from_slice(&p.seq.to_le_bytes());
        out.extend_from_slice(&p.wall_ms.to_le_bytes());
        out.extend_from_slice(&p.sim_us.to_le_bytes());
        out.extend_from_slice(&p.run.to_le_bytes());
        out.extend_from_slice(&p.speed_mps.to_le_bytes());
        for v in [p.odometer_km, p.fuel_l].into_iter().flatten() {
            out.extend_from_slice(&v.to_le_bytes());
        }
        for v in p.pos.iter().flatten() {
            out.extend_from_slice(&v.to_le_bytes());
        }
        if let Some(t) = p.game_time_min {
            out.extend_from_slice(&t.to_le_bytes());
        }
        out.extend_from_slice(&p.local_scale.to_le_bytes());
        out.extend_from_slice(&p.truck.to_le_bytes());
        out.extend_from_slice(&p.mp_time_offset.to_le_bytes());
        if let Some(d) = p.cargo_damage {
            out.extend_from_slice(&d.to_le_bytes());
        }
        if let Some(k) = &p.mp_mod {
            // Config validation keeps kinds to 32 ASCII bytes.
            let b = &k.as_bytes()[..k.len().min(255)];
            out.push(b.len() as u8);
            out.extend_from_slice(b);
        }
    }
    out
}

const CODEC_VERSION: u8 = 1;

pub fn decode_points(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<Point>, String> {
    struct R<'a>(&'a [u8]);
    impl<'a> R<'a> {
        fn bytes(&mut self, n: usize) -> Result<&'a [u8], String> {
            if self.0.len() < n {
                return Err("truncated point data".into());
            }
            let (a, b) = self.0.split_at(n);
            self.0 = b;
            Ok(a)
        }
        fn take<const N: usize>(&mut self) -> Result<[u8; N], String> {
            self.bytes(N).map(|a| a.try_into().expect("length checked"))
        }
        fn u16(&mut self) -> Result<u16, String> {
            self.take().map(u16::from_le_bytes)
        }
        fn u32(&mut self) -> Result<u32, String> {
            self.take().map(u32::from_le_bytes)
        }
        fn u64(&mut self) -> Result<u64, String> {
            self.take().map(u64::from_le_bytes)
        }
        fn i64(&mut self) -> Result<i64, String> {
            self.take().map(i64::from_le_bytes)
        }
        fn f64(&mut self) -> Result<f64, String> {
            self.take().map(f64::from_le_bytes)
        }
    }
    let mut r = R(bytes);
    let [version] = r.take()?;
    if version != CODEC_VERSION {
        return Err(format!("point data version {version}"));
    }
    let n = r.u32()? as usize;
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(n.min(1 << 20));
    for _ in 0..n {
        let flags = r.u16()?;
        let bit = |k: u16| flags & (1 << k) != 0;
        let sess = r.u32()?;
        let seq = r.u64()?;
        let wall_ms = r.i64()?;
        let sim_us = r.u64()?;
        let run = r.u32()?;
        let speed_mps = r.f64()?;
        let odometer_km = if bit(0) { Some(r.f64()?) } else { None };
        let fuel_l = if bit(1) { Some(r.f64()?) } else { None };
        let pos = if bit(2) { Some([r.f64()?, r.f64()?, r.f64()?]) } else { None };
        let game_time_min = if bit(3) { Some(r.u32()?) } else { None };
        let local_scale = r.f64()?;
        let truck = r.u32()?;
        let mp_time_offset = r.i64()?;
        let cargo_damage = if bit(8) { Some(r.f64()?) } else { None };
        let mp_mod = if bit(9) {
            let [n] = r.take()?;
            let kind = r.bytes(n as usize)?.to_vec();
            Some(String::from_utf8(kind).map_err(|_| "mod kind is not UTF-8".to_string())?)
        } else {
            None
        };
        out.push(Point {
            sess,
            seq,
            wall_ms,
            sim_us,
            run,
            speed_mps,
            odometer_km,
            fuel_l,
            pos,
            game_time_min,
            local_scale,
            cargo_loaded: bit(4),
            trailer_connected: bit(5),
            truck,
            mp_time_offset,
            truckersmp: bit(6),
            mp_mod,
            after_teleport: bit(7),
            cargo_damage,
        });
    }
    if !r.0.is_empty() {
        return Err("trailing bytes after point data".into());
    }
    Ok(out)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn point_codec_round_trips_every_field() {
        let mut a = pt(7);
        a.sess = 3;
        a.wall_ms = -12;
        a.odometer_km = Some(1234.5678);
        a.fuel_l = Some(f64::MIN_POSITIVE);
        a.game_time_min = Some(u32::MAX);
        a.cargo_loaded = true;
        a.truckersmp = true;
        a.after_teleport = true;
        a.cargo_damage = Some(0.125);
        a.mp_mod = Some("haulmp".into());
        a.speed_mps = -0.0;
        a.mp_time_offset = i64::MIN;
        let mut b = pt(8);
        b.pos = None;
        b.trailer_connected = false;
        let pts = vec![a, b];
        let back = decode_points(&encode_points(&pts)).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(back, pts);
        assert_eq!(back[0].speed_mps.to_bits(), (-0.0f64).to_bits());
        assert!(decode_points(&encode_points(&pts)[..20]).is_err());
    }

    fn pt(seq: u64) -> Point {
        Point {
            sess: 0,
            seq,
            wall_ms: seq as i64,
            sim_us: seq,
            run: 0,
            speed_mps: 0.0,
            odometer_km: None,
            fuel_l: None,
            pos: Some([seq as f64, 0.0, 0.0]),
            game_time_min: None,
            local_scale: 1.0,
            cargo_loaded: false,
            trailer_connected: true,
            truck: 0,
            mp_time_offset: 0,
            truckersmp: false,
            mp_mod: None,
            after_teleport: false,
            cargo_damage: None,
        }
    }

    fn seqs(s: &VecStore, t: TrackId) -> Vec<u64> {
        PointStore::iter(s, t).map(|p| p.seq).collect()
    }

    #[test]
    fn split_and_append_move_points() {
        let mut s = VecStore::new();
        let a = s.create();
        for i in 0..5 {
            s.push(a, pt(i));
        }
        let b = s.split_off(a, 3);
        assert_eq!((seqs(&s, a), seqs(&s, b)), (vec![0, 1, 2], vec![3, 4]));
        let empty = s.split_off(a, 3);
        assert!(s.is_empty(empty));
        s.append(a, b);
        assert_eq!(seqs(&s, a), vec![0, 1, 2, 3, 4]);
        assert_eq!(s.len(b), 0, "appended track is gone");
        assert_eq!(s.last(a).map(|p| p.seq), Some(4));
        assert_eq!(s.position(a, &|p| p.seq == 2), Some(2));
        assert_eq!(s.near(a, [0.0; 3], 1.0).map(|(i, _)| i).collect::<Vec<_>>(), vec![0, 1, 2, 3, 4]);
    }
}
```
