`crates/pt-server/src/sheet.rs`:

```rs
//! A job's stats sheet (ADMIN_API §14): the fields a player submits for a
//! manual job and a moderator may edit on any job, in canonical units
//! (km, litres, Unix ms). Also the manual distance rule: game distance ÷ map
//! scale, with the UK stretch and up to five adjusted sections at their own
//! scales (project owner, 2026-10-15).

use pt_core::config::ScaleClass;
use pt_core::{Config, Game};
use serde_json::{json, Map, Value};

use crate::http::{ApiError, ApiResult};
use crate::util::{self, round2, round3};

/// ETS2's UK roads (the game's own `local.scale` there).
pub const UK_SCALE: f64 = 15.0;

pub const KM_PER_MI: f64 = 1.609344;
const L_PER_US_GAL: f64 = 3.785411784;
const L_PER_UK_GAL: f64 = 4.54609;

/// Text fields: canonical key ← request key.
const TEXT: [(&str, &str); 8] = [
    ("source_city", "start_city"),
    ("source_company", "start_company"),
    ("destination_city", "end_city"),
    ("destination_company", "end_company"),
    ("cargo_name", "cargo_name"),
    ("truck", "truck"),
    ("truck_model", "truck_model"),
    ("bonus_id", "bonus_id"),
];

/// Every request key a sheet accepts (PATCH, approval corrections).
pub const EDIT_KEYS: [&str; 19] = [
    "start_city", "start_company", "end_city", "end_company", "cargo_name", "truck", "truck_model", "bonus_id",
    "distance", "fuel_used", "damage", "profit", "started_at", "ended_at", "mod_names", "map_scale", "uk", "adjusted_scales",
    "speed_penalty",
];

pub const MAX_TEXT: usize = 100;
pub const MAX_MODS: usize = 100;
pub const MAX_DISTANCE_KM: f64 = 50_000.0;
/// Adjusted-scale sections per job (owner, 2026-10-15).
pub const MAX_SECTIONS: usize = 5;
/// A city-scale section counts only from 1 mi of real distance, i.e. 3 mi in
/// game at scale 3 (owner, 2026-10-15).
pub const CITY_SECTION_MIN_WORLD_KM: f64 = KM_PER_MI;

#[derive(Default)]
struct Errs(Map<String, Value>);

impl Errs {
    fn add(&mut self, k: &str, m: &str) {
        self.0.entry(k.to_string()).or_insert_with(|| m.into());
    }
}

fn text(v: &Value, key: &str, errs: &mut Errs) -> Option<String> {
    match v.as_str().map(str::trim) {
        Some(s) if (1..=MAX_TEXT).contains(&s.chars().count()) => Some(s.to_string()),
        _ => {
            errs.add(key, &format!("1-{MAX_TEXT} characters"));
            None
        }
    }
}

fn number(v: &Value, key: &str, lo: f64, hi: f64, errs: &mut Errs) -> Option<f64> {
    match v.as_f64() {
        Some(x) if x.is_finite() && x >= lo && x <= hi => Some(x),
        _ => {
            errs.add(key, &format!("a number from {lo} to {hi}"));
            None
        }
    }
}

fn positive(v: &Value, key: &str, hi: f64, errs: &mut Errs) -> Option<f64> {
    match v.as_f64() {
        Some(x) if x.is_finite() && x > 0.0 && x <= hi => Some(x),
        _ => {
            errs.add(key, &format!("a number above 0, at most {hi}"));
            None
        }
    }
}

fn instant(v: &Value, key: &str, errs: &mut Errs) -> Option<i64> {
    match v.as_str().and_then(util::parse_rfc3339) {
        Some(t) => Some(t),
        None => {
            errs.add(key, "an RFC 3339 instant");
            None
        }
    }
}

/// Request distance → km in the given unit.
fn km(x: f64, unit: Option<&str>) -> f64 {
    if unit == Some("mi") {
        x * KM_PER_MI
    } else {
        x
    }
}

/// Parses the sheet fields of a request body into canonical form. `full`: a
/// submission (every required field); otherwise a partial edit, where `null`
/// clears a field. `base` is the effective sheet the edit applies to (for
/// a partial `uk` and edits of `adjusted_scales` by section number).
pub fn parse(body: &Value, game: Game, full: bool, base: &Map<String, Value>) -> ApiResult<Map<String, Value>> {
    let mut e = Errs::default();
    let mut out = Map::new();
    let unit = body.get("unit").and_then(Value::as_str);
    let fuel_unit = body.get("fuel_unit").and_then(Value::as_str);
    if let Some(u) = body.get("unit").filter(|v| !v.is_null()) {
        if !matches!(u.as_str(), Some("mi" | "km")) {
            e.add("unit", "mi or km");
        }
    }
    if let Some(u) = body.get("fuel_unit").filter(|v| !v.is_null()) {
        if !matches!(u.as_str(), Some("l" | "us_gal" | "uk_gal")) {
            e.add("fuel_unit", "l, us_gal or uk_gal");
        }
    }
    let has = |k: &str| body.get(k).is_some();
    // A distance anywhere in the UK section or the adjusted sections (a list,
    // or an object by section number) needs the unit.
    let has_distance = |v: &Value| v.get("distance").is_some();
    let in_sections = match body.get("adjusted_scales") {
        Some(Value::Array(a)) => a.iter().any(has_distance),
        Some(Value::Object(o)) => o.values().any(has_distance),
        _ => false,
    };
    let needs_unit = has("distance") || body.get("uk").is_some_and(has_distance) || in_sections;
    if (full || needs_unit) && unit.is_none() {
        e.add("unit", "required with distances");
    }
    if (full || has("fuel_used")) && fuel_unit.is_none() && !body.get("fuel_used").is_some_and(Value::is_null) {
        e.add("fuel_unit", "required with fuel_used");
    }
    let required = |k: &str, e: &mut Errs| {
        if full && !has(k) {
            e.add(k, "required");
        }
    };

    for (canon, key) in TEXT {
        match body.get(key) {
            None => {
                if full && !matches!(key, "bonus_id" | "truck_model") {
                    required(key, &mut e);
                }
            }
            Some(Value::Null) if matches!(key, "bonus_id" | "truck_model") || (!full && key == "truck") => {
                out.insert(canon.into(), Value::Null);
            }
            Some(v) => {
                if let Some(s) = text(v, key, &mut e) {
                    out.insert(canon.into(), s.into());
                }
            }
        }
    }
    if full {
        // A player never picks a bonus: moderators do (owner, 2026-10-15).
        if has("bonus_id") {
            e.add("bonus_id", "set by moderators only");
        }
        out.remove("bonus_id");
        if has("speed_penalty") {
            e.add("speed_penalty", "set by moderators only");
        }
    } else {
        // Moderators add or remove the speed penalty; null: back to the rules
        // (owner, 2026-10-16).
        match body.get("speed_penalty") {
            None => {}
            Some(v @ (Value::Bool(_) | Value::Null)) => {
                out.insert("speed_penalty".into(), v.clone());
            }
            Some(_) => e.add("speed_penalty", "true, false or null"),
        }
    }

    let nullable = |k: &str| !full && body.get(k).is_some_and(Value::is_null);
    if nullable("distance") {
        e.add("distance", "cannot be cleared");
    } else if let Some(v) = body.get("distance") {
        if let Some(x) = positive(v, "distance", MAX_DISTANCE_KM, &mut e) {
            out.insert("distance_km".into(), json!(km(x, unit)));
        }
    } else {
        required("distance", &mut e);
    }
    if nullable("fuel_used") {
        out.insert("fuel_used_l".into(), Value::Null);
    } else if let Some(v) = body.get("fuel_used") {
        if let Some(x) = number(v, "fuel_used", 0.0, 1_000_000.0, &mut e) {
            let l = match fuel_unit {
                Some("us_gal") => x * L_PER_US_GAL,
                Some("uk_gal") => x * L_PER_UK_GAL,
                _ => x,
            };
            out.insert("fuel_used_l".into(), json!(l));
        }
    } else {
        required("fuel_used", &mut e);
    }
    if nullable("damage") {
        out.insert("damage_pct".into(), Value::Null);
    } else if let Some(v) = body.get("damage") {
        if let Some(x) = number(v, "damage", 0.0, 100.0, &mut e) {
            out.insert("damage_pct".into(), json!(x));
        }
    } else {
        required("damage", &mut e);
    }
    if nullable("profit") {
        out.insert("profit".into(), Value::Null);
    } else if let Some(v) = body.get("profit") {
        if let Some(x) = number(v, "profit", -100_000_000.0, 100_000_000.0, &mut e) {
            out.insert("profit".into(), json!(x));
        }
    } else {
        required("profit", &mut e);
    }
    for (canon, key) in [("started_at_ms", "started_at"), ("ended_at_ms", "ended_at")] {
        if nullable(key) {
            e.add(key, "cannot be cleared");
        } else if let Some(v) = body.get(key) {
            if let Some(t) = instant(v, key, &mut e) {
                out.insert(canon.into(), json!(t));
            }
        } else {
            required(key, &mut e);
        }
    }
    if nullable("mod_names") {
        out.insert("mods".into(), json!([]));
    } else if let Some(v) = body.get("mod_names") {
        match v.as_array() {
            Some(a) if a.len() <= MAX_MODS => {
                let mods: Vec<Value> = a.iter().filter_map(|m| text(m, "mod_names", &mut e)).map(Value::from).collect();
                out.insert("mods".into(), Value::Array(mods));
            }
            _ => e.add("mod_names", &format!("a list of at most {MAX_MODS} names")),
        }
    } else if full {
        out.insert("mods".into(), json!([]));
    }
    if nullable("map_scale") {
        out.insert("map_scale".into(), Value::Null);
    } else if let Some(v) = body.get("map_scale") {
        if let Some(x) = positive(v, "map_scale", 1000.0, &mut e) {
            out.insert("map_scale".into(), json!(x));
        }
    }

    // The UK stretch (ETS2): a whole object on a submission, field by field
    // on an edit.
    if let Some(v) = body.get("uk") {
        if v.is_null() {
            out.insert("uk".into(), Value::Null);
        } else if game != Game::Ets2 {
            e.add("uk", "ETS2 only");
        } else if let Some(o) = v.as_object() {
            let start = match (full, base.get("uk")) {
                (false, Some(Value::Object(b))) => b.clone(),
                _ => Map::new(),
            };
            let sec = section(o, "uk", start, full, unit, &mut e);
            out.insert("uk".into(), Value::Object(sec));
        } else {
            e.add("uk", "an object");
        }
    }

    // Adjusted-scale sections, at most five (owner, 2026-10-15).
    if body.get("adjusted_scale").is_some() {
        e.add("adjusted_scale", "replaced by adjusted_scales, a list");
    }
    if let Some(v) = body.get("adjusted_scales") {
        let current: Vec<Map<String, Value>> = sections(base).into_iter().cloned().collect();
        let list = match v {
            Value::Null => Some(Vec::new()),
            Value::Array(items) => {
                // A whole list: on a submission, or replacing every section.
                let mut list = Vec::new();
                for (i, item) in items.iter().enumerate() {
                    let path = format!("adjusted_scales[{i}]");
                    match item.as_object() {
                        Some(o) => list.push(section(o, &path, Map::new(), full, unit, &mut e)),
                        None => e.add(&path, "an object"),
                    }
                }
                Some(list)
            }
            Value::Object(by_index) if !full => {
                // An edit by index: change fields of one section, remove it
                // (null), or add one at the end (index = current count).
                let mut list: Vec<Option<Map<String, Value>>> = current.into_iter().map(Some).collect();
                let mut keys: Vec<(usize, &Value)> = Vec::new();
                for (k, x) in by_index {
                    match k.parse::<usize>() {
                        Ok(i) => keys.push((i, x)),
                        Err(_) => e.add(&format!("adjusted_scales.{k}"), "a section number from 0"),
                    }
                }
                keys.sort_by_key(|(i, _)| *i);
                for (i, x) in keys {
                    let path = format!("adjusted_scales[{i}]");
                    match (x, i.cmp(&list.len())) {
                        (Value::Null, std::cmp::Ordering::Less) => list[i] = None,
                        (Value::Object(o), std::cmp::Ordering::Less) => {
                            let start = list[i].clone().unwrap_or_default();
                            list[i] = Some(section(o, &path, start, false, unit, &mut e));
                        }
                        (Value::Object(o), std::cmp::Ordering::Equal) => list.push(Some(section(o, &path, Map::new(), false, unit, &mut e))),
                        _ => e.add(&path, "no such section"),
                    }
                }
                Some(list.into_iter().flatten().collect())
            }
            _ => {
                e.add("adjusted_scales", if full { "a list" } else { "a list, an object by section number, or null" });
                None
            }
        };
        if let Some(list) = list {
            if list.len() > MAX_SECTIONS {
                e.add("adjusted_scales", &format!("at most {MAX_SECTIONS} sections"));
            }
            out.insert("adjusted_scales".into(), Value::Array(list.into_iter().map(Value::Object).collect()));
        }
    }
    if !e.0.is_empty() {
        return Err(ApiError::validation(Value::Object(e.0)));
    }
    Ok(out)
}

/// One section (`uk` or an adjusted-scale section) from request fields laid
/// over `start`. `path` names its fields in errors (`uk`, `adjusted_scales[2]`).
/// Images only come with a submission (`full`), where they are required.
fn section(o: &Map<String, Value>, path: &str, mut sec: Map<String, Value>, full: bool, unit: Option<&str>, e: &mut Errs) -> Map<String, Value> {
    let uk = path == "uk";
    let (texts, image): (&[&str], &str) = if uk { (&["entry_city", "end_city"], "route_evidence") } else { (&["entry_city", "exit_city"], "evidence") };
    for (k, x) in o {
        let p = format!("{path}.{k}");
        match k.as_str() {
            "distance" => {
                if let Some(d) = positive(x, &p, MAX_DISTANCE_KM, e) {
                    sec.insert("distance_km".into(), json!(km(d, unit)));
                }
            }
            "scale" if !uk => {
                if let Some(s) = positive(x, &p, 1000.0, e) {
                    sec.insert("scale".into(), json!(s));
                }
            }
            k if k == image => {
                if !full {
                    e.add(&p, "evidence cannot be edited");
                } else if let Some(s) = x.as_str() {
                    sec.insert("evidence_id".into(), s.into());
                } else {
                    e.add(&p, "an evidence id");
                }
            }
            k if texts.contains(&k) => {
                if let Some(s) = text(x, &p, e) {
                    sec.insert(k.to_string(), s.into());
                }
            }
            _ => e.add(&p, "unknown field"),
        }
    }
    let mut want: Vec<(&str, &str)> = texts.iter().map(|t| (*t, *t)).collect();
    want.push(("distance_km", "distance"));
    if !uk {
        want.push(("scale", "scale"));
    }
    if full {
        want.push(("evidence_id", image));
    }
    for (key, name) in want {
        if !sec.contains_key(key) {
            e.add(&format!("{path}.{name}"), "required");
        }
    }
    sec
}

/// A sheet's adjusted-scale sections (also an older single `adjusted_scale`).
pub fn sections(sheet: &Map<String, Value>) -> Vec<&Map<String, Value>> {
    match (sheet.get("adjusted_scales"), sheet.get("adjusted_scale")) {
        (Some(Value::Array(a)), _) => a.iter().filter_map(Value::as_object).collect(),
        (_, Some(Value::Object(o))) => vec![o],
        _ => Vec::new(),
    }
}

/// Rejects body keys a PATCH does not know (besides its control fields).
pub fn check_keys(body: &Value, control: &[&str]) -> ApiResult<()> {
    let mut e = Errs::default();
    for k in body.as_object().into_iter().flatten().map(|(k, _)| k) {
        if !EDIT_KEYS.contains(&k.as_str()) && !control.contains(&k.as_str()) && !matches!(k.as_str(), "unit" | "fuel_unit") {
            e.add(k, "unknown field");
        }
    }
    if e.0.is_empty() {
        Ok(())
    } else {
        Err(ApiError::validation(Value::Object(e.0)))
    }
}

/// `base` with `overrides` laid over it, key by key.
pub fn merged(base: &Map<String, Value>, overrides: &Map<String, Value>) -> Map<String, Value> {
    let mut m = base.clone();
    for (k, v) in overrides {
        m.insert(k.clone(), v.clone());
    }
    m
}

/// Cross-field checks on an effective sheet: the sections fit in the
/// distance, and a city-scale section is at least 1 mi of real distance
/// (rejected, not flagged: owner, 2026-10-15).
pub fn check(sheet: &Map<String, Value>, game: Game, cfg: &Config) -> ApiResult<()> {
    let mut e = Errs::default();
    let f = |v: Option<&Value>| v.and_then(Value::as_f64).unwrap_or(0.0);
    let total = f(sheet.get("distance_km"));
    let uk = f(sheet.get("uk").and_then(|u| u.get("distance_km")));
    let secs = sections(sheet);
    let adj: f64 = secs.iter().map(|s| f(s.get("distance_km"))).sum();
    if uk + adj > total + 1e-9 {
        e.add(if adj > 0.0 { "adjusted_scales" } else { "uk.distance" }, "the UK and adjusted sections are part of distance, so cannot exceed it");
    }
    let city = cfg.map.scale.vanilla(game).city_local_scale;
    for (i, s) in secs.iter().enumerate() {
        let scale = f(s.get("scale"));
        if scale == city && f(s.get("distance_km")) / scale + 1e-9 < CITY_SECTION_MIN_WORLD_KM {
            e.add(&format!("adjusted_scales[{i}].distance"), "a city-scale section counts only from 3 mi in game (1 mi real)");
        }
    }
    if let (Some(a), Some(b)) = (sheet.get("started_at_ms").and_then(Value::as_i64), sheet.get("ended_at_ms").and_then(Value::as_i64)) {
        if b <= a {
            e.add("ended_at", "must be after started_at");
        }
    }
    if e.0.is_empty() {
        Ok(())
    } else {
        Err(ApiError::validation(Value::Object(e.0)))
    }
}

/// World (1:1) distance of a sheet: (distance − UK − adjusted) ÷ map scale,
/// UK ÷ 15, adjusted ÷ its scale. Returns (world km, per scale class: game km,
/// world km).
pub fn world_km(sheet: &Map<String, Value>, game: Game, cfg: &Config) -> (f64, Vec<(ScaleClass, f64, f64)>) {
    let vanilla = cfg.map.scale.vanilla(game);
    let f = |v: Option<&Value>| v.and_then(Value::as_f64);
    let total = f(sheet.get("distance_km")).unwrap_or(0.0);
    let scale = f(sheet.get("map_scale")).unwrap_or_else(|| vanilla.main_road_local_scale());
    let mut parts = Vec::new();
    let mut rest = total;
    if let Some(d) = f(sheet.get("uk").and_then(|u| u.get("distance_km"))) {
        parts.push((d, UK_SCALE));
        rest -= d;
    }
    for a in sections(sheet) {
        if let (Some(d), Some(s)) = (f(a.get("distance_km")), f(a.get("scale"))) {
            parts.push((d, s));
            rest -= d;
        }
    }
    parts.insert(0, (rest.max(0.0), scale));
    let mut classes: Vec<(ScaleClass, f64, f64)> = Vec::new();
    let mut world = 0.0;
    for (d, s) in parts {
        let w = d / s;
        world += w;
        let c = vanilla.classify(Some(s));
        match classes.iter_mut().find(|x| x.0 == c) {
            Some(x) => {
                x.1 += d;
                x.2 += w;
            }
            None => classes.push((c, d, w)),
        }
    }
    (world, classes)
}

fn mi(km: f64) -> f64 {
    round2(km / KM_PER_MI)
}

fn section_json(o: &Map<String, Value>) -> Value {
    let mut sec = Map::new();
    for (sk, sv) in o {
        if sk == "distance_km" {
            let x = sv.as_f64().unwrap_or(0.0);
            sec.insert("distance_km".into(), json!(round3(x)));
            sec.insert("distance_mi".into(), json!(mi(x)));
        } else {
            sec.insert(sk.clone(), sv.clone());
        }
    }
    Value::Object(sec)
}

/// The sheet as the API shows it: distances in km and mi, times as RFC 3339.
pub fn to_json(sheet: &Map<String, Value>) -> Value {
    let mut out = Map::new();
    for (k, v) in sheet {
        match (k.as_str(), v) {
            ("distance_km", Value::Number(n)) => {
                let x = n.as_f64().unwrap_or(0.0);
                out.insert("distance_km".into(), json!(round3(x)));
                out.insert("distance_mi".into(), json!(mi(x)));
            }
            ("started_at_ms" | "ended_at_ms", Value::Number(n)) => {
                let key = k.trim_end_matches("_ms").to_string();
                out.insert(key, util::rfc3339(n.as_i64().unwrap_or(0)).into());
            }
            ("started_at_ms" | "ended_at_ms", _) => {
                out.insert(k.trim_end_matches("_ms").to_string(), Value::Null);
            }
            ("fuel_used_l", Value::Number(n)) => {
                out.insert(k.clone(), json!(round2(n.as_f64().unwrap_or(0.0))));
            }
            ("uk", Value::Object(o)) => {
                out.insert(k.clone(), section_json(o));
            }
            ("adjusted_scales", Value::Array(a)) => {
                out.insert(k.clone(), a.iter().filter_map(Value::as_object).map(section_json).collect());
            }
            ("adjusted_scale", Value::Object(o)) => {
                // Stored before the list existed.
                out.insert("adjusted_scales".into(), json!([section_json(o)]));
            }
            _ => {
                out.insert(k.clone(), v.clone());
            }
        }
    }
    Value::Object(out)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn cfg() -> Config {
        crate::config::sample()
    }

    fn submission() -> Value {
        json!({"game": "ets2", "unit": "mi", "fuel_unit": "us_gal", "start_city": "Calais", "start_company": "Tradeaux",
               "end_city": "London", "end_company": "Posped", "cargo_name": "Apples", "distance": 300, "fuel_used": 40,
               "damage": 3.5, "profit": 12000, "started_at": "2026-10-14T08:00:00Z", "ended_at": "2026-10-14T09:10:00Z",
               "truck": "Scania", "truck_model": "S", "mod_names": ["Realistic Physics"],
               "uk": {"distance": 100, "entry_city": "Folkestone", "end_city": "London", "route_evidence": "evd_x"}})
    }

    #[test]
    fn submissions_convert_units_and_split_the_uk() {
        let s = parse(&submission(), Game::Ets2, true, &Map::new()).unwrap();
        assert!((s["distance_km"].as_f64().unwrap() - 300.0 * KM_PER_MI).abs() < 1e-9);
        assert!((s["fuel_used_l"].as_f64().unwrap() - 40.0 * L_PER_US_GAL).abs() < 1e-9);
        assert_eq!(s["source_city"], "Calais");
        check(&s, Game::Ets2, &cfg()).unwrap();
        let (w, classes) = world_km(&s, Game::Ets2, &cfg());
        let expect = (200.0 * KM_PER_MI) / 19.0 + (100.0 * KM_PER_MI) / 15.0;
        assert!((w - expect).abs() < 1e-9, "{w} vs {expect}");
        // 19 and 15 are both ETS2 road scales.
        assert_eq!(classes.len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(classes[0].0, ScaleClass::Road);
    }

    #[test]
    fn defaults_and_adjusted_sections() {
        let mut b = submission();
        b["game"] = "ats".into();
        b.as_object_mut().unwrap().remove("uk");
        b["unit"] = "km".into();
        b["adjusted_scales"] = json!([
            {"entry_city": "A", "exit_city": "B", "distance": 50, "scale": 1, "evidence": "evd_y"},
            {"entry_city": "C", "exit_city": "D", "distance": 30, "scale": 3, "evidence": "evd_z"},
        ]);
        let s = parse(&b, Game::Ats, true, &Map::new()).unwrap();
        check(&s, Game::Ats, &cfg()).unwrap();
        let (w, classes) = world_km(&s, Game::Ats, &cfg());
        assert!((w - (220.0 / 20.0 + 50.0 + 10.0)).abs() < 1e-9, "{w}");
        assert!(classes.iter().any(|c| c.0 == ScaleClass::OneToOne && c.2 == 50.0));
        assert!(classes.iter().any(|c| c.0 == ScaleClass::City && c.1 == 30.0));
        // The older single section still reads as one.
        let mut old = s.clone();
        let one = old.remove("adjusted_scales").unwrap()[0].clone();
        old.insert("adjusted_scale".into(), one);
        assert_eq!(sections(&old).len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(to_json(&old)["adjusted_scales"][0]["scale"], 1.0);
    }

    fn adjusted(scale: f64, distance: f64) -> Value {
        json!({"entry_city": "A", "exit_city": "B", "distance": distance, "scale": scale, "evidence": "evd"})
    }

    #[test]
    fn at_most_five_sections_and_city_ones_from_three_game_miles() {
        let mut b = submission();
        b["adjusted_scales"] = json!((0..6).map(|_| adjusted(1.0, 1.0)).collect::<Vec<_>>());
        assert_eq!(parse(&b, Game::Ets2, true, &Map::new()).unwrap_err().details["fields"]["adjusted_scales"], "at most 5 sections");
        // City scale: 3 mi in game (1 mi real) counts, just under does not.
        b["adjusted_scales"] = json!([adjusted(3.0, 3.0), adjusted(3.0, 2.99), adjusted(19.0, 0.5)]);
        let s = parse(&b, Game::Ets2, true, &Map::new()).unwrap();
        let f = check(&s, Game::Ets2, &cfg()).unwrap_err().details["fields"].clone();
        assert!(f.get("adjusted_scales[0].distance").is_none());
        assert!(f.get("adjusted_scales[1].distance").is_some(), "{f}");
        assert!(f.get("adjusted_scales[2].distance").is_none(), "only city scale has a minimum");
        // In km: 4.828032 km is exactly 3 mi.
        b["unit"] = "km".into();
        b["adjusted_scales"] = json!([adjusted(3.0, 4.828032)]);
        check(&parse(&b, Game::Ets2, true, &Map::new()).unwrap(), Game::Ets2, &cfg()).unwrap();
        // Sections and the UK together cannot exceed the distance.
        b["unit"] = "mi".into();
        b["adjusted_scales"] = json!([adjusted(1.0, 150.0), adjusted(1.0, 60.0)]);
        let s = parse(&b, Game::Ets2, true, &Map::new()).unwrap();
        assert!(check(&s, Game::Ets2, &cfg()).unwrap_err().details["fields"].get("adjusted_scales").is_some());
        // Per-item errors are named by index; the old key is refused.
        b["adjusted_scales"] = json!([adjusted(1.0, 1.0), {"entry_city": "A", "distance": 2}]);
        b["adjusted_scale"] = adjusted(1.0, 1.0);
        let f = parse(&b, Game::Ets2, true, &Map::new()).unwrap_err().details["fields"].clone();
        assert!(f.get("adjusted_scales[1].exit_city").is_some() && f.get("adjusted_scales[1].scale").is_some(), "{f}");
        assert!(f.get("adjusted_scales[1].evidence").is_some() && f.get("adjusted_scale").is_some(), "{f}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn sections_are_edited_by_number() {
        let mut b = submission();
        b["adjusted_scales"] = json!([adjusted(1.0, 10.0), adjusted(3.0, 5.0), adjusted(20.0, 7.0)]);
        let base = parse(&b, Game::Ets2, true, &Map::new()).unwrap();
        // Change section 0, remove section 1, add a fourth (index = count).
        let edit = json!({"unit": "mi", "adjusted_scales": {
            "0": {"distance": 12}, "1": null, "3": {"entry_city": "E", "exit_city": "F", "distance": 4, "scale": 1}}});
        let e = parse(&edit, Game::Ets2, false, &base).unwrap();
        let list = e["adjusted_scales"].as_array().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(list.len(), 3);
        assert!((list[0]["distance_km"].as_f64().unwrap() - 12.0 * KM_PER_MI).abs() < 1e-9);
        assert_eq!(list[0]["evidence_id"], "evd", "an edit keeps the image of the section");
        assert_eq!(list[1]["scale"], 20.0);
        assert_eq!(list[2]["entry_city"], "E");
        // No such section; images cannot be edited; null clears them all.
        let f = parse(&json!({"adjusted_scales": {"7": {"scale": 2}}}), Game::Ets2, false, &base).unwrap_err().details["fields"].clone();
        assert_eq!(f["adjusted_scales[7]"], "no such section");
        let f = parse(&json!({"adjusted_scales": {"0": {"evidence": "evd_new"}}}), Game::Ets2, false, &base).unwrap_err().details["fields"].clone();
        assert!(f.get("adjusted_scales[0].evidence").is_some());
        assert_eq!(parse(&json!({"adjusted_scales": null}), Game::Ets2, false, &base).unwrap()["adjusted_scales"], json!([]));
    }

    #[test]
    fn validation_names_every_bad_field() {
        let mut b = submission();
        b["damage"] = 120.into();
        b["uk"]["distance"] = 400.into();
        b["bonus_id"] = "bon_x".into();
        b.as_object_mut().unwrap().remove("cargo_name");
        let e = parse(&b, Game::Ets2, true, &Map::new()).unwrap_err();
        let f = &e.details["fields"];
        assert!(f.get("damage").is_some() && f.get("bonus_id").is_some() && f.get("cargo_name").is_some(), "{f}");
        let mut ok = submission();
        ok["uk"]["distance"] = 400.into();
        let s = parse(&ok, Game::Ets2, true, &Map::new()).unwrap();
        assert!(check(&s, Game::Ets2, &cfg()).unwrap_err().details["fields"].get("uk.distance").is_some());
        assert!(parse(&submission(), Game::Ats, true, &Map::new()).unwrap_err().details["fields"].get("uk").is_some());
    }

    #[test]
    fn edits_are_partial_and_merge_sections() {
        let base = parse(&submission(), Game::Ets2, true, &Map::new()).unwrap();
        let edit = parse(&json!({"unit": "km", "uk": {"distance": 120}, "damage": null}), Game::Ets2, false, &base).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(edit["uk"]["entry_city"], "Folkestone");
        assert_eq!(edit["uk"]["distance_km"], 120.0);
        assert_eq!(edit["damage_pct"], Value::Null);
        assert!(edit.get("distance_km").is_none());
        let e = parse(&json!({"uk": {"route_evidence": "evd_z"}}), Game::Ets2, false, &base).unwrap_err();
        assert!(e.details["fields"].get("uk.route_evidence").is_some());
        assert!(check_keys(&json!({"reason": "x", "speed": 1}), &["reason"]).is_err());
    }
}
```

`crates/pt-server/src/store.rs`:

```rs
//! Shared storage helpers: ids, users, tokens, the audit log and idempotency
//! (API_CONVENTIONS §3).

use serde_json::{json, Value};

use crate::env::{Host, Row, RowExt, P};
use crate::http::{ApiError, ApiResult, Request, Response};
use crate::params;
use crate::util;

/// `prefix_` + 10 Crockford characters (50 random bits), lower-case.
pub fn new_id<H: Host>(h: &H, prefix: &str) -> String {
    let mut b = [0u8; 7];
    h.random(&mut b);
    format!("{prefix}_{}", util::crockford(&b, 10).to_ascii_lowercase())
}

/// An 8-character job id (40 random bits).
pub fn new_job_id<H: Host>(h: &H) -> String {
    let mut b = [0u8; 5];
    h.random(&mut b);
    util::crockford(&b, 8)
}

/// A player token: `pt_live_` + 43 base64url characters (256 bits).
pub fn new_token<H: Host>(h: &H) -> String {
    let mut b = [0u8; 32];
    h.random(&mut b);
    format!("pt_live_{}", util::b64url(&b))
}

pub async fn one<H: Host>(h: &H, sql: &str, p: Vec<P>) -> ApiResult<Option<Row>> {
    Ok(h.all(sql, p).await?.into_iter().next())
}

pub async fn count<H: Host>(h: &H, sql: &str, p: Vec<P>) -> ApiResult<usize> {
    Ok(one(h, sql, p).await?.map(|r| r.values().next().and_then(Value::as_f64).unwrap_or(0.0) as usize).unwrap_or(0))
}

// ---- users -----------------------------------------------------------------------

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub struct User {
    pub user_id: String,
    pub discord_user_id: String,
    pub display_name: String,
    pub role: String,
    pub singleplayer_division: bool,
    pub division_changed_at: i64,
    pub disabled: bool,
    pub created_at: i64,
}

impl User {
    fn from_row(r: &Row) -> User {
        User {
            user_id: r.s("user_id"),
            discord_user_id: r.s("discord_user_id"),
            display_name: r.s("display_name"),
            role: r.s("role"),
            singleplayer_division: r.b("singleplayer_division"),
            division_changed_at: r.i("division_changed_at"),
            disabled: r.b("disabled"),
            created_at: r.i("created_at"),
        }
    }

    /// `{"user_id", "discord_user_id", "display_name"}`.
    pub fn brief(&self) -> Value {
        json!({"user_id": self.user_id, "discord_user_id": self.discord_user_id, "display_name": self.display_name})
    }
}

pub async fn user_by_discord<H: Host>(h: &H, discord_id: &str) -> ApiResult<Option<User>> {
    Ok(one(h, "SELECT * FROM users WHERE discord_user_id = ?1", params![discord_id]).await?.map(|r| User::from_row(&r)))
}

pub async fn user_by_id<H: Host>(h: &H, user_id: &str) -> ApiResult<Option<User>> {
    Ok(one(h, "SELECT * FROM users WHERE user_id = ?1", params![user_id]).await?.map(|r| User::from_row(&r)))
}

/// Discord IDs are decimal snowflakes.
pub fn check_discord_id(id: &str) -> ApiResult<()> {
    if (1..=20).contains(&id.len()) && id.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_digit()) {
        Ok(())
    } else {
        Err(ApiError::bad_request("Discord IDs are decimal strings.").details(json!({"discord_id": id})))
    }
}

pub fn check_display_name(name: &str) -> ApiResult<String> {
    let name = name.trim();
    let n = name.chars().count();
    if !(2..=32).contains(&n) {
        return Err(ApiError::field("display_name", "must be 2-32 characters"));
    }
    Ok(name.to_string())
}

/// The user of a Discord ID, created when missing. Returns (user, created).
pub async fn ensure_user<H: Host>(h: &H, discord_id: &str, display_name: Option<&str>) -> ApiResult<(User, bool)> {
    if let Some(u) = user_by_discord(h, discord_id).await? {
        return Ok((u, false));
    }
    let name = match display_name {
        Some(n) => check_display_name(n)?,
        None => format!("Player {}", &discord_id[discord_id.len().saturating_sub(4)..]),
    };
    let id = new_id(h, "usr");
    h.run(
        "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO users (user_id, discord_user_id, display_name, created_at) VALUES (?1, ?2, ?3, ?4)",
        params![&id, discord_id, &name, h.now_ms()],
    )
    .await?;
    let u = user_by_discord(h, discord_id).await?.ok_or_else(|| ApiError::internal("user vanished"))?;
    let created = u.user_id == id;
    Ok((u, created))
}

// ---- tokens ----------------------------------------------------------------------

/// The active token's metadata, if any.
pub async fn active_token<H: Host>(h: &H, user_id: &str) -> ApiResult<Option<Value>> {
    Ok(one(
        h,
        "SELECT token_id, created_at, last_used_at FROM tokens WHERE user_id = ?1 AND revoked_at IS NULL ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1",
        params![user_id],
    )
    .await?
    .map(|r| {
        json!({"token_id": r.s("token_id"), "created_at": util::rfc3339(r.i("created_at")),
               "last_used_at": util::opt_rfc3339(r.opt_i("last_used_at"))})
    }))
}

pub const TOKENS_PER_DAY: usize = 5;

/// Issues a token, revoking the previous one. Returns the response object
/// with the plaintext (PUBLIC_API §1) and the audit "after".
pub async fn issue_token<H: Host>(h: &H, user: &User) -> ApiResult<(Value, Option<String>)> {
    let now = h.now_ms();
    let today = count(h, "SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM tokens WHERE user_id = ?1 AND created_at > ?2", params![&user.user_id, now - 86_400_000])
        .await?;
    if today >= TOKENS_PER_DAY {
        return Err(ApiError::rate_limited(3600));
    }
    let previous = one(h, "SELECT token_id FROM tokens WHERE user_id = ?1 AND revoked_at IS NULL", params![&user.user_id])
        .await?
        .map(|r| r.s("token_id"));
    let token = new_token(h);
    let token_id = new_id(h, "tok");
    h.batch(vec![
        ("UPDATE tokens SET revoked_at = ?2 WHERE user_id = ?1 AND revoked_at IS NULL".into(), params![&user.user_id, now]),
        (
            "INSERT INTO tokens (token_id, user_id, token_sha256, created_at) VALUES (?1, ?2, ?3, ?4)".into(),
            params![&token_id, &user.user_id, util::sha256_hex(token.as_bytes()), now],
        ),
    ])
    .await?;
    Ok((
        json!({"token_id": token_id, "token": token, "created_at": util::rfc3339(now), "revoked_token_id": previous}),
        previous,
    ))
}

pub async fn revoke_token<H: Host>(h: &H, user: &User) -> ApiResult<String> {
    let Some(r) = one(h, "SELECT token_id FROM tokens WHERE user_id = ?1 AND revoked_at IS NULL", params![&user.user_id]).await? else {
        return Err(ApiError::not_found("token"));
    };
    h.run("UPDATE tokens SET revoked_at = ?2 WHERE token_id = ?1", params![r.s("token_id"), h.now_ms()]).await?;
    Ok(r.s("token_id"))
}

// ---- audit -----------------------------------------------------------------------

pub struct Audit<'a> {
    pub actor: &'a str,
    pub action: &'a str,
    pub target_kind: &'a str,
    pub target_id: &'a str,
    pub target_user: Option<&'a str>,
    pub reason: Option<&'a str>,
    pub before: Value,
    pub after: Value,
}

pub fn audit_stmt<H: Host>(h: &H, a: Audit<'_>) -> (String, Vec<P>) {
    (
        "INSERT INTO audit_log (at, actor, action, target_kind, target_id, target_user, reason, before, after)
         VALUES (?1, ?2, ?3, ?4, ?5, ?6, ?7, ?8, ?9)"
            .into(),
        params![
            h.now_ms(),
            a.actor,
            a.action,
            a.target_kind,
            a.target_id,
            a.target_user,
            a.reason,
            a.before.to_string(),
            a.after.to_string()
        ],
    )
}

pub async fn audit<H: Host>(h: &H, a: Audit<'_>) -> ApiResult<()> {
    let (sql, p) = audit_stmt(h, a);
    h.run(&sql, p).await?;
    Ok(())
}

// ---- idempotency -----------------------------------------------------------------

pub const IDEMPOTENCY_TTL_MS: i64 = 24 * 3_600_000;

pub struct Idem {
    scope: String,
    key: String,
    body_sha256: String,
}

/// Checks `Idempotency-Key` on a write. `Ok(Err(response))` is a replay to
/// return as is; `Ok(Ok(idem))` means go ahead and [`idem_store`] the result.
pub async fn idem_begin<H: Host>(h: &H, req: &Request, scope: &str) -> ApiResult<Result<Idem, Response>> {
    let key = req.header("idempotency-key").unwrap_or_default();
    if key.is_empty() || key.len() > 128 || !key.bytes().all(|b| (0x20..0x7f).contains(&b)) {
        return Err(ApiError::new(400, "validation_failed", "Writes need an Idempotency-Key header (1-128 printable ASCII).")
            .details(json!({"fields": {"idempotency_key": "required"}})));
    }
    let body_sha256 = util::sha256_hex(&req.body);
    let found = one(
        h,
        "SELECT body_sha256, status, response, created_at FROM idempotency WHERE scope = ?1 AND key = ?2",
        params![scope, key],
    )
    .await?;
    if let Some(r) = found {
        if h.now_ms() - r.i("created_at") <= IDEMPOTENCY_TTL_MS {
            if r.s("body_sha256") != body_sha256 {
                return Err(ApiError::new(409, "idempotency_mismatch", "This Idempotency-Key was used with a different body."));
            }
            return Ok(Err(Response::json(r.i("status") as u16, &r.json("response"))));
        }
    }
    Ok(Ok(Idem { scope: scope.into(), key: key.into(), body_sha256 }))
}

/// Remembers the response a replay should get (it may differ from the one
/// sent now: a token's plaintext is never replayed).
pub async fn idem_store<H: Host>(h: &H, idem: Idem, status: u16, replay_body: &Value) -> ApiResult<()> {
    h.run(
        "INSERT OR REPLACE INTO idempotency (scope, key, body_sha256, status, response, created_at) VALUES (?1, ?2, ?3, ?4, ?5, ?6)",
        params![idem.scope, idem.key, idem.body_sha256, status as i64, replay_body.to_string(), h.now_ms()],
    )
    .await?;
    Ok(())
}

/// The `reason` of an admin write: 3-1000 characters after trimming.
pub fn reason(body: &Value) -> ApiResult<String> {
    let r = body.get("reason").and_then(Value::as_str).map(str::trim).unwrap_or_default();
    let n = r.chars().count();
    if n == 0 {
        return Err(ApiError::field("reason", "required"));
    }
    if !(3..=1000).contains(&n) {
        return Err(ApiError::field("reason", "must be 3-1000 characters"));
    }
    Ok(r.to_string())
}
```

`crates/pt-server/src/updates.rs`:

```rs
//! Client updates and downloads (docs/UPDATES.md). A release published with a
//! signed update manifest is offered to clients; its files, the setup program
//! and the uninstaller are in the release bucket. Only the uninstaller is
//! public: updates need a player token, the setup a personal link the bot asks
//! for (owner, 2026-10-15: only some Discord roles may download the tracker). The server checks the signature when the
//! release is published but cannot sign anything itself: the key stays with the
//! maintainer, and clients verify again before installing.

use pt_core::update::{self, UpdateManifest};
use serde_json::{json, Value};

use crate::env::{Host, Row, RowExt};
use crate::http::{ApiError, ApiResult, Request, Response};
use crate::store;
use crate::util::{self, rfc3339};
use crate::{auth, params};

pub const MAX_NOTES_CHARS: usize = 2000;

/// What a release adds for updates, checked and ready to store.
pub struct UpdateCols {
    pub manifest: Option<String>,
    pub signature: Option<String>,
    pub installer: Option<String>,
    pub notes: Option<String>,
    pub offered: bool,
}

fn file_name_ok(s: &str) -> bool {
    !s.is_empty() && s.len() <= 100 && !s.starts_with('.') && s.bytes().all(|c| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || b"._-".contains(&c))
}

/// Checks the update part of `POST /admin/releases`: the signature, that the
/// manifest is for this version and platform and ships exactly the release's
/// plugin and client binaries, and that every file is in the release bucket.
pub async fn check<H: Host>(h: &H, body: &Value, version: &str, platform: &str, files: &[Value]) -> ApiResult<UpdateCols> {
    let text = |k: &str| body.get(k).and_then(Value::as_str).map(str::to_string);
    let invalid = |field: &str, msg: String| ApiError::field(field, &msg);
    let notes = text("notes").map(|n| n.trim().to_string()).filter(|n| !n.is_empty());
    if notes.as_ref().is_some_and(|n| n.chars().count() > MAX_NOTES_CHARS) {
        return Err(invalid("notes", format!("at most {MAX_NOTES_CHARS} characters")));
    }
    let installer = text("installer");
    if let Some(name) = &installer {
        if !file_name_ok(name) || !name.to_ascii_lowercase().ends_with(".exe") && platform == "windows" {
            return Err(invalid("installer", "a file name such as PlasmaTrack-Setup-0.2.0.exe".into()));
        }
        let key = format!("{platform}/{version}/{name}");
        if h.release_size(&key).await?.is_none() {
            return Err(invalid("installer", format!("{key} is not in the release bucket")));
        }
    }
    let (manifest, signature) = match body.get("update") {
        None | Some(Value::Null) => (None, None),
        Some(u) => {
            let m = u["manifest"].as_str().unwrap_or_default();
            let s = u["signature"].as_str().unwrap_or_default();
            let keys = match h.settings().update_keys.as_slice() {
                [] => update::UPDATE_KEYS,
                k => k,
            };
            let parsed = update::verify_with(m, s, keys).map_err(|e| invalid("update", e.to_string()))?;
            check_manifest(h, &parsed, version, platform, files).await?;
            (Some(m.to_string()), Some(s.trim().to_ascii_lowercase()))
        }
    };
    let offered = body.get("offer").and_then(Value::as_bool).unwrap_or(manifest.is_some());
    if offered && manifest.is_none() {
        return Err(invalid("offer", "only a release with an update can be offered".into()));
    }
    Ok(UpdateCols { manifest, signature, installer, notes, offered })
}

async fn check_manifest<H: Host>(h: &H, m: &UpdateManifest, version: &str, platform: &str, files: &[Value]) -> ApiResult<()> {
    let bad = |msg: String| ApiError::field("update", &msg);
    if m.version != version || m.platform != platform {
        return Err(bad(format!("the manifest is for {} {}", m.platform, m.version)));
    }
    let hashes: Vec<&str> = files.iter().filter_map(|f| f["sha256"].as_str()).collect();
    for f in files {
        let sha = f["sha256"].as_str().unwrap_or_default();
        if f["role"] != "config_file" && !m.files.iter().any(|u| u.sha256 == sha) {
            return Err(bad(format!("no file in the update has the {} hash {sha}", f["role"].as_str().unwrap_or_default())));
        }
    }
    for f in &m.files {
        let program = [".exe", ".dll", ".so"].iter().any(|x| f.path.to_ascii_lowercase().ends_with(x)) || !f.path.contains('.');
        if program && !hashes.contains(&f.sha256.as_str()) {
            return Err(bad(format!("{} is not one of the release's files", f.path)));
        }
        let key = m.key(f);
        match h.release_size(&key).await? {
            Some(n) if n == f.gz_size => {}
            Some(n) => return Err(bad(format!("{key} has {n} bytes, the manifest says {}", f.gz_size))),
            None => return Err(bad(format!("{key} is not in the release bucket"))),
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// The update fields of a release in admin responses.
pub fn release_extras(r: &Row) -> Value {
    let manifest = r.opt_s("update_manifest").and_then(|m| update::parse(&m).ok());
    json!({
        "update": manifest.map(|m| json!({"files": m.files.len(), "bytes": m.files.iter().map(|f| f.gz_size).sum::<u64>()})),
        "installer": r.opt_s("installer"),
        "notes": r.opt_s("notes"),
        "offered": r.b("offered"),
    })
}

/// Offered releases for a platform that nothing revokes (a scheduled
/// revocation counts: a release on its way out is not handed out), newest first.
async fn offered<H: Host>(h: &H, platform: &str) -> ApiResult<Vec<Row>> {
    let mut rows = h
        .all(
            "SELECT * FROM releases WHERE platform = ?1 AND offered = 1 AND update_manifest IS NOT NULL
             AND release_id NOT IN (SELECT target_id FROM revocations WHERE target_kind = 'release' AND cancelled_at IS NULL)",
            params![platform],
        )
        .await?;
    rows.sort_by_key(|r| std::cmp::Reverse(update::parse_version(&r.s("release_version"))));
    Ok(rows)
}

async fn newest<H: Host>(h: &H, platform: &str) -> ApiResult<Option<Row>> {
    Ok(offered(h, platform).await?.into_iter().next())
}

fn platform_of(req: &Request) -> ApiResult<String> {
    let p = req.q("platform").unwrap_or("windows").to_string();
    if !matches!(p.as_str(), "windows" | "linux") {
        return Err(ApiError::bad_request("platform is windows or linux").details(json!({"platform": p})));
    }
    Ok(p)
}

/// `GET /api/v1/client/update?platform=windows&version=0.2.1`, asked by
/// clients with their player token: the newest offered release when it is
/// newer than `version`.
pub async fn client_update<H: Host>(h: &H, req: &Request) -> ApiResult<Response> {
    auth::player(h, req).await?;
    let platform = platform_of(req)?;
    let current = req.q("version").and_then(update::parse_version).ok_or_else(|| ApiError::bad_request("version is like 0.2.1"))?;
    let offer = newest(h, &platform).await?.filter(|r| update::parse_version(&r.s("release_version")) > Some(current));
    let body = match offer {
        Some(r) => json!({"update": {
            "release_id": r.s("release_id"),
            "version": r.s("release_version"),
            "manifest": r.s("update_manifest"),
            "signature": r.s("update_signature"),
            "notes": r.opt_s("notes"),
            "published_at": rfc3339(r.i("created_at")),
        }}),
        None => json!({"update": null}),
    };
    Ok(Response::ok(body).with_header("cache-control", "no-store"))
}

/// The uninstaller's name in every release folder. Anyone may download it.
pub const UNINSTALLER: &str = "PlasmaTrack-Uninstall.exe";
/// How long a personal setup link works.
pub const SETUP_LINK_TTL_MS: i64 = 3_600_000;
/// On a response from [`file`]: the release-bucket key whose bytes are the
/// body. The Worker streams the object and drops the header.
pub const STREAM_HEADER: &str = "x-plasmatrack-release-key";

fn origin<H: Host>(h: &H) -> String {
    h.settings().public_url.trim_end_matches('/').to_string()
}

fn release_sig<H: Host>(h: &H, key: &str, exp_s: i64) -> String {
    util::hex(&util::hmac_sha256(h.settings().download_secret.as_bytes(), format!("release.{key}.{exp_s}").as_bytes()))
}

/// The newest offered release whose folder holds the file `name` picks, with
/// that file's name and size.
async fn newest_with<H: Host>(h: &H, platform: &str, name: impl Fn(&Row) -> Option<String>) -> ApiResult<Option<(Row, String, u64)>> {
    for r in offered(h, platform).await? {
        if let Some(n) = name(&r) {
            if let Some(size) = h.release_size(&format!("{platform}/{}/{n}", r.s("release_version"))).await? {
                return Ok(Some((r, n, size)));
            }
        }
    }
    Ok(None)
}

/// `GET /api/v1/public/client?platform=windows`: the newest release, its
/// setup program (downloaded through a personal link, [`client_download`])
/// and the uninstaller (a public link).
pub async fn latest<H: Host>(h: &H, req: &Request) -> ApiResult<Response> {
    auth::service(h, req)?;
    let platform = platform_of(req)?;
    let r = newest(h, &platform).await?.ok_or_else(|| ApiError::not_found("release"))?;
    let installer = match r.opt_s("installer") {
        Some(name) => {
            let size = h.release_size(&format!("{platform}/{}/{name}", r.s("release_version"))).await?;
            json!({"file_name": name, "bytes": size})
        }
        None => Value::Null,
    };
    let uninstaller = newest_with(h, &platform, |_| Some(UNINSTALLER.to_string())).await?.map_or(Value::Null, |(_, name, size)| {
        json!({"file_name": name, "bytes": size, "url": format!("{}/dl/uninstall/{platform}", origin(h))})
    });
    Ok(Response::ok(json!({
        "platform": platform,
        "release_id": r.s("release_id"),
        "version": r.s("release_version"),
        "published_at": rfc3339(r.i("created_at")),
        "notes": r.opt_s("notes"),
        "installer": installer,
        "uninstaller": uninstaller,
    })))
}

/// `GET /api/v1/players/{discord_id}/client-download?platform=windows` (bot
/// token): a personal link to the newest setup program, valid for an hour.
/// The bot decides who may have one (Discord roles); a disabled player gets 403.
pub async fn client_download<H: Host>(h: &H, req: &Request, discord_id: &str) -> ApiResult<Response> {
    auth::bot(h, req)?;
    store::check_discord_id(discord_id)?;
    if store::user_by_discord(h, discord_id).await?.is_some_and(|u| u.disabled) {
        return Err(ApiError::forbidden("This player is disabled."));
    }
    let platform = platform_of(req)?;
    let (r, name, size) = newest_with(h, &platform, |r| r.opt_s("installer")).await?.ok_or_else(|| ApiError::not_found("release"))?;
    let key = format!("{platform}/{}/{name}", r.s("release_version"));
    let exp_s = (h.now_ms() + SETUP_LINK_TTL_MS) / 1000;
    let url = format!("{}/dl/releases/{key}?exp={exp_s}&sig={}", origin(h), release_sig(h, &key, exp_s));
    Ok(Response::ok(json!({
        "platform": platform,
        "release_id": r.s("release_id"),
        "version": r.s("release_version"),
        "notes": r.opt_s("notes"),
        "file_name": name,
        "bytes": size,
        "url": url,
        "expires_at": rfc3339(exp_s * 1000),
    }))
    .with_header("cache-control", "no-store"))
}

/// `GET /dl/uninstall/{platform}`: a redirect to the newest uninstaller, for
/// anyone, so one link stays right across releases.
pub async fn uninstall<H: Host>(h: &H, platform: &str) -> ApiResult<Response> {
    let (r, name, _) = newest_with(h, platform, |_| Some(UNINSTALLER.to_string())).await?.ok_or_else(|| ApiError::not_found("file"))?;
    let to = format!("{}/dl/releases/{platform}/{}/{name}", origin(h), r.s("release_version"));
    Ok(Response::bytes(302, "text/plain", Vec::new()).with_header("location", &to).with_header("cache-control", "no-store"))
}

/// The R2 key of a `/dl/releases/…` path, when it is one.
pub fn release_key(parts: &[&str]) -> Option<String> {
    let ok = parts.len() >= 3
        && matches!(parts[0], "windows" | "linux")
        && update::parse_version(parts[1]).is_some()
        && parts[2..].iter().all(|p| file_name_ok(p) || (!p.is_empty() && p.bytes().all(|c| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || b"_-".contains(&c))));
    ok.then(|| parts.join("/"))
}

pub fn content_type(key: &str) -> &'static str {
    match key.rsplit('.').next().unwrap_or_default() {
        "gz" => "application/gzip",
        "exe" => "application/vnd.microsoft.portable-executable",
        _ => "application/octet-stream",
    }
}

/// `GET /dl/releases/{platform}/{version}/{path}`. Who may download what:
/// - update files (`.gz`): a client with a player token;
/// - the uninstaller: anyone;
/// - anything else (the setup program): a personal link from
///   [`client_download`].
///
/// The answer names the object in [`STREAM_HEADER`] with an empty body: the
/// Worker streams it (setup programs are large), and the native tests read
/// the header.
pub async fn file<H: Host>(h: &H, req: &Request, parts: &[&str]) -> ApiResult<Response> {
    let key = release_key(parts).ok_or_else(|| ApiError::not_found("file"))?;
    let name = key.rsplit('/').next().unwrap_or_default().to_string();
    let cache = if key.ends_with(".gz") {
        auth::player(h, req).await?;
        "private, max-age=86400"
    } else if name == UNINSTALLER {
        "public, max-age=31536000, immutable"
    } else {
        let bad = || ApiError::forbidden("This link is not valid. Ask the Discord bot for a new one.");
        let (Some(exp), Some(sig)) = (req.q("exp"), req.q("sig")) else { return Err(bad()) };
        let exp_s: i64 = exp.parse().map_err(|_| bad())?;
        if !util::constant_eq(sig.as_bytes(), release_sig(h, &key, exp_s).as_bytes()) {
            return Err(bad());
        }
        if h.now_ms() / 1000 > exp_s {
            return Err(ApiError::forbidden("This link has expired. Ask the Discord bot for a new one."));
        }
        "private, no-store"
    };
    h.release_size(&key).await?.ok_or_else(|| ApiError::not_found("file"))?;
    let mut r = Response::bytes(200, content_type(&key), Vec::new()).with_header("cache-control", cache).with_header(STREAM_HEADER, &key);
    if !key.ends_with(".gz") {
        r = r.with_header("content-disposition", &format!("attachment; filename=\"{name}\""));
    }
    Ok(r)
}
```

```rs
//! Small self-contained helpers: UTC dates, IDs, base64url, HMAC-SHA256, gzip.

use std::io::{Read, Write};

use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};

// ---- dates (UTC, proleptic Gregorian) ----------------------------------------

/// Days since 1970-01-01 of a civil date (Howard Hinnant's algorithm).
pub fn days_from_civil(y: i64, m: u32, d: u32) -> i64 {
    let y = if m <= 2 { y - 1 } else { y };
    let era = y.div_euclid(400);
    let yoe = y - era * 400;
    let m = m as i64;
    let doy = (153 * (if m > 2 { m - 3 } else { m + 9 }) + 2) / 5 + d as i64 - 1;
    let doe = yoe * 365 + yoe / 4 - yoe / 100 + doy;
    era * 146_097 + doe - 719_468
}

pub fn civil_from_days(z: i64) -> (i64, u32, u32) {
    let z = z + 719_468;
    let era = z.div_euclid(146_097);
    let doe = z - era * 146_097;
    let yoe = (doe - doe / 1460 + doe / 36_524 - doe / 146_096) / 365;
    let y = yoe + era * 400;
    let doy = doe - (365 * yoe + yoe / 4 - yoe / 100);
    let mp = (5 * doy + 2) / 153;
    let d = (doy - (153 * mp + 2) / 5 + 1) as u32;
    let m = if mp < 10 { mp + 3 } else { mp - 9 } as u32;
    (if m <= 2 { y + 1 } else { y }, m, d)
}

const DAY_MS: i64 = 86_400_000;

/// `2026-10-13T21:25:00.070Z` (API_CONVENTIONS §6).
pub fn rfc3339(ms: i64) -> String {
    let (days, rem) = (ms.div_euclid(DAY_MS), ms.rem_euclid(DAY_MS));
    let (y, m, d) = civil_from_days(days);
    let (h, mi, s, milli) = (rem / 3_600_000, rem / 60_000 % 60, rem / 1000 % 60, rem % 1000);
    format!("{y:04}-{m:02}-{d:02}T{h:02}:{mi:02}:{s:02}.{milli:03}Z")
}

pub fn opt_rfc3339(ms: Option<i64>) -> serde_json::Value {
    ms.map_or(serde_json::Value::Null, |m| rfc3339(m).into())
}

/// Parses RFC 3339 with a `Z` or numeric offset and optional fraction.
pub fn parse_rfc3339(s: &str) -> Option<i64> {
    let b = s.as_bytes();
    if b.len() < 20 || b[4] != b'-' || b[7] != b'-' || !matches!(b[10], b'T' | b't' | b' ') || b[13] != b':' || b[16] != b':' {
        return None;
    }
    let num = |r: std::ops::Range<usize>| s.get(r)?.parse::<i64>().ok();
    let (y, mo, d, h, mi, sec) = (num(0..4)?, num(5..7)?, num(8..10)?, num(11..13)?, num(14..16)?, num(17..19)?);
    if !(1..=12).contains(&mo) || !(1..=31).contains(&d) || h > 23 || mi > 59 || sec > 60 {
        return None;
    }
    let mut i = 19;
    let mut milli = 0i64;
    if b.get(i) == Some(&b'.') {
        i += 1;
        let start = i;
        while i < b.len() && b[i].is_ascii_digit() {
            i += 1;
        }
        let frac = &s[start..i];
        if frac.is_empty() {
            return None;
        }
        milli = format!("{:0<3}", &frac[..frac.len().min(3)]).parse().ok()?;
    }
    let offset_min = match b.get(i) {
        Some(b'Z' | b'z') if i + 1 == b.len() => 0,
        Some(&c @ (b'+' | b'-')) if i + 6 == b.len() && b[i + 3] == b':' => {
            let v = num(i + 1..i + 3)? * 60 + num(i + 4..i + 6)?;
            if c == b'+' {
                v
            } else {
                -v
            }
        }
        _ => return None,
    };
    let days = days_from_civil(y, mo as u32, d as u32);
    Some(days * DAY_MS + h * 3_600_000 + mi * 60_000 + sec * 1000 + milli - offset_min * 60_000)
}

/// Monday 00:00 UTC of ISO week `week` of ISO year `year`.
pub fn iso_week_start(year: i64, week: u32) -> i64 {
    // The week with January 4th is week 1.
    let jan4 = days_from_civil(year, 1, 4);
    let weekday = (jan4 + 3).rem_euclid(7); // 0 = Monday
    (jan4 - weekday + (week as i64 - 1) * 7) * DAY_MS
}

/// ISO year and week of an instant.
pub fn iso_week_of(ms: i64) -> (i64, u32) {
    let days = ms.div_euclid(DAY_MS);
    let weekday = (days + 3).rem_euclid(7);
    let thursday = days - weekday + 3;
    let (y, _, _) = civil_from_days(thursday);
    let week = ((thursday - days_from_civil(y, 1, 1)) / 7 + 1) as u32;
    (y, week)
}

pub fn iso_weeks_in_year(year: i64) -> u32 {
    iso_week_of(days_from_civil(year, 12, 28) * DAY_MS).1
}

pub fn month_start(year: i64, month: u32) -> i64 {
    days_from_civil(year, month, 1) * DAY_MS
}

pub fn year_month_of(ms: i64) -> (i64, u32) {
    let (y, m, _) = civil_from_days(ms.div_euclid(DAY_MS));
    (y, m)
}

// ---- encodings -------------------------------------------------------------------

pub fn hex(bytes: &[u8]) -> String {
    bytes.iter().map(|b| format!("{b:02x}")).collect()
}

pub fn sha256_hex(data: &[u8]) -> String {
    hex(&Sha256::digest(data))
}

const B64URL: &[u8; 64] = b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789-_";

/// base64url without padding.
pub fn b64url(data: &[u8]) -> String {
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(data.len().div_ceil(3) * 4);
    for c in data.chunks(3) {
        let n = (c[0] as u32) << 16 | (*c.get(1).unwrap_or(&0) as u32) << 8 | *c.get(2).unwrap_or(&0) as u32;
        for i in 0..=c.len() {
            out.push(B64URL[(n >> (18 - 6 * i) & 63) as usize] as char);
        }
    }
    out
}

pub fn b64url_decode(s: &str) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(s.len() * 3 / 4);
    let (mut acc, mut bits) = (0u32, 0u32);
    for c in s.bytes() {
        let v = B64URL.iter().position(|&x| x == c)? as u32;
        acc = acc << 6 | v;
        bits += 6;
        if bits >= 8 {
            bits -= 8;
            out.push((acc >> bits) as u8);
            acc &= (1 << bits) - 1;
        }
    }
    Some(out)
}

/// Crockford base32 (no I, L, O, U).
const CROCKFORD: &[u8; 32] = b"0123456789ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTVWXYZ";

/// `n` Crockford characters from random bytes (5 bits each).
pub fn crockford(random: &[u8], n: usize) -> String {
    let mut bits = random.iter().flat_map(|b| (0..8).rev().map(move |i| (b >> i) & 1));
    (0..n)
        .map(|_| {
            let v = (0..5).fold(0usize, |acc, _| acc << 1 | bits.next().unwrap_or(0) as usize);
            CROCKFORD[v] as char
        })
        .collect()
}

/// A job id as typed by a person: case-insensitive, optional hyphen, I/L → 1
/// and O → 0 (API_CONVENTIONS §6). `None` unless 8 valid characters remain.
pub fn normalize_job_id(s: &str) -> Option<String> {
    let id: String = s
        .chars()
        .filter(|c| *c != '-')
        .map(|c| match c.to_ascii_uppercase() {
            'I' | 'L' => '1',
            'O' => '0',
            c => c,
        })
        .collect();
    (id.len() == 8 && id.bytes().all(|b| CROCKFORD.contains(&b))).then_some(id)
}

/// HMAC-SHA256 (RFC 2104).
pub fn hmac_sha256(key: &[u8], msg: &[u8]) -> [u8; 32] {
    let mut k = [0u8; 64];
    if key.len() > 64 {
        k[..32].copy_from_slice(&Sha256::digest(key));
    } else {
        k[..key.len()].copy_from_slice(key);
    }
    let pad = |x: u8| k.iter().map(|b| b ^ x).collect::<Vec<u8>>();
    let inner = Sha256::new().chain_update(pad(0x36)).chain_update(msg).finalize();
    Sha256::new().chain_update(pad(0x5c)).chain_update(inner).finalize().into()
}

/// Compares in time independent of where the inputs differ.
pub fn constant_eq(a: &[u8], b: &[u8]) -> bool {
    a.len() == b.len() && a.iter().zip(b).fold(0u8, |acc, (x, y)| acc | (x ^ y)) == 0
}

pub fn gunzip(data: &[u8], limit: usize) -> std::io::Result<Vec<u8>> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    flate2::read::GzDecoder::new(data).take((limit as u64).saturating_add(1)).read_to_end(&mut out)?;
    if out.len() > limit {
        return Err(std::io::Error::other("too large"));
    }
    Ok(out)
}

/// JSON straight into the compressor, without the text or a JSON tree in
/// memory.
pub fn gzip_json<T: serde::Serialize>(v: &T) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
    let mut enc = flate2::write::GzEncoder::new(Vec::new(), flate2::Compression::default());
    {
        let mut w = std::io::BufWriter::with_capacity(64 << 10, &mut enc);
        serde_json::to_writer(&mut w, v).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        w.flush().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    }
    enc.finish().map_err(|e| e.to_string())
}

/// The reverse of [`gzip_json`], reading as it decompresses.
pub fn gunzip_json<T: serde::de::DeserializeOwned>(z: &[u8]) -> Result<T, String> {
    serde_json::from_reader(std::io::BufReader::with_capacity(64 << 10, flate2::read::GzDecoder::new(z))).map_err(|e| e.to_string())
}

pub fn gzip(data: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut enc = flate2::write::GzEncoder::new(Vec::new(), flate2::Compression::default());
    enc.write_all(data).expect("in-memory write");
    enc.finish().expect("in-memory finish")
}

/// `*` matches any run of characters (slashes included), `?` one character;
/// ASCII case is ignored and `\` counts as `/` (Windows paths).
pub fn glob(pattern: &str, s: &str) -> bool {
    fn norm(x: &str) -> Vec<char> {
        x.chars().map(|c| if c == '\\' { '/' } else { c.to_ascii_lowercase() }).collect()
    }
    let (p, s) = (norm(pattern), norm(s));
    // Iterative wildcard matching with backtracking to the last `*`.
    let (mut pi, mut si, mut star, mut mark) = (0, 0, None, 0);
    while si < s.len() {
        if pi < p.len() && (p[pi] == '?' || p[pi] == s[si]) {
            pi += 1;
            si += 1;
        } else if pi < p.len() && p[pi] == '*' {
            star = Some(pi);
            mark = si;
            pi += 1;
        } else if let Some(st) = star {
            pi = st + 1;
            mark += 1;
            si = mark;
        } else {
            return false;
        }
    }
    p[pi..].iter().all(|c| *c == '*')
}

/// km → miles, the contract's two-decimal rounding for shown distances.
pub fn mi(km: f64) -> f64 {
    round2(km / 1.609_344)
}

pub fn round2(v: f64) -> f64 {
    (v * 100.0).round() / 100.0
}

pub fn round3(v: f64) -> f64 {
    (v * 1000.0).round() / 1000.0
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn dates_round_trip() {
        let ms = parse_rfc3339("2026-10-13T21:25:00.070Z").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(rfc3339(ms), "2026-10-13T21:25:00.070Z");
        assert_eq!(parse_rfc3339("2026-10-13T23:25:00+02:00"), parse_rfc3339("2026-10-13T21:25:00Z"));
        assert_eq!(parse_rfc3339("1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"), Some(0));
        assert_eq!(rfc3339(-1), "1969-12-31T23:59:59.999Z");
        assert!(parse_rfc3339("2026-13-01T00:00:00Z").is_none());
        assert!(parse_rfc3339("2026-10-13").is_none());
    }

    #[test]
    fn iso_weeks() {
        // 2026-10-14 is a Wednesday of ISO week 42; the week starts Monday 12th.
        let ms = parse_rfc3339("2026-10-14T09:00:00Z").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(iso_week_of(ms), (2026, 42));
        assert_eq!(rfc3339(iso_week_start(2026, 42)), "2026-10-12T00:00:00.000Z");
        // 2027-01-01 (Friday) is still in 2026-W53.
        assert_eq!(iso_week_of(parse_rfc3339("2027-01-01T12:00:00Z").unwrap()), (2026, 53));
        assert_eq!(iso_weeks_in_year(2026), 53);
        assert_eq!(iso_weeks_in_year(2025), 52);
        assert_eq!(rfc3339(iso_week_start(2026, 1)), "2025-12-29T00:00:00.000Z");
    }

    #[test]
    fn encodings() {
        assert_eq!(b64url(b"hello?"), "aGVsbG8_");
        assert_eq!(b64url(b"ab"), "YWI");
        assert_eq!(b64url_decode("YWI").unwrap(), b"ab");
        assert_eq!(crockford(&[0xff; 5], 8), "ZZZZZZZZ");
        assert_eq!(crockford(&[0; 5], 8), "00000000");
        assert_eq!(normalize_job_id("7k2m-9qxa").as_deref(), Some("7K2M9QXA"));
        assert_eq!(normalize_job_id("OIL00000").as_deref(), Some("01100000"));
        assert_eq!(normalize_job_id("7K2M9QX"), None);
        assert_eq!(normalize_job_id("7K2M9QXU"), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn globs() {
        assert!(glob("*/bin/win_x64/plugins/plasmatrack.dll", r"C:\Steam\steamapps\common\ETS2\bin\win_x64\plugins\PlasmaTrack.dll"));
        assert!(glob("a?c", "abc"));
        assert!(!glob("a?c", "ac"));
        assert!(glob("*", ""));
        assert!(!glob("*.dll", "x.exe"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn hmac_matches_rfc4231_case_2() {
        let mac = hmac_sha256(b"Jefe", b"what do ya want for nothing?");
        assert_eq!(hex(&mac), "5bdcc146bf60754e6a042426089575c75a003f089d2739839dec58b964ec3843");
    }

    #[test]
    fn gzip_round_trip_and_limit() {
        let z = gzip(b"abcabcabc");
        assert_eq!(gunzip(&z, 100).unwrap(), b"abcabcabc");
        assert!(gunzip(&z, 5).is_err());
    }
}
```

```rs
//! Signed webhooks to the bot (docs/WEBHOOKS.md). Events go to an outbox in
//! D1; the queue delivers them with the retry schedule of §3 and drops them
//! after 72 h.

use serde_json::{json, Value};

use crate::env::{Host, RowExt};
use crate::http::ApiResult;
use crate::params;
use crate::store;
use crate::util;

/// Seconds to wait after attempt n fails (§3), then every 8 h.
const RETRY_S: [u32; 7] = [30, 120, 600, 1800, 3600, 7200, 14_400];
const RETRY_LATER_S: u32 = 28_800;
pub const MAX_AGE_MS: i64 = 72 * 3_600_000;
pub const MAX_BODY_BYTES: usize = 256 << 10;
pub const TIMESTAMP_TOLERANCE_S: i64 = 300;

/// Records an event and queues its delivery after `delay_s` seconds.
pub async fn emit<H: Host>(h: &H, kind: &str, data: Value, delay_s: u32) -> ApiResult<String> {
    let event_id = store::new_id(h, "evt");
    let now = h.now_ms();
    let body = json!({
        "event_id": event_id,
        "type": kind,
        "occurred_at": util::rfc3339(now),
        "payload_version": 1,
        "data": data,
    });
    h.run(
        "INSERT INTO webhook_outbox (event_id, type, body, created_at) VALUES (?1, ?2, ?3, ?4)",
        params![&event_id, kind, body.to_string(), now],
    )
    .await?;
    h.queue_webhook(&event_id, delay_s).await?;
    Ok(event_id)
}

/// `t=<unix s>,v1=<hex>[,v1=<hex>…]`: one `v1` per configured secret.
pub fn signature(secrets: &[String], t: i64, body: &[u8]) -> String {
    let mut msg = format!("{t}.").into_bytes();
    msg.extend_from_slice(body);
    let mut s = format!("t={t}");
    for secret in secrets {
        s.push_str(&format!(",v1={}", util::hex(&util::hmac_sha256(secret.as_bytes(), &msg))));
    }
    s
}

/// Checks a signature header the way the bot does (§2); used by the tests.
pub fn verify(secret: &str, header: &str, body: &[u8], now_s: i64) -> bool {
    let mut t = None;
    let mut sigs = Vec::new();
    for part in header.split(',') {
        match part.split_once('=') {
            Some(("t", v)) => t = v.parse::<i64>().ok(),
            Some(("v1", v)) => sigs.push(v.to_string()),
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    let Some(t) = t else { return false };
    if (now_s - t).abs() > TIMESTAMP_TOLERANCE_S {
        return false;
    }
    let expected = signature(&[secret.to_string()], t, body);
    let want = expected.rsplit_once("v1=").map(|(_, v)| v).unwrap_or_default();
    sigs.iter().any(|s| util::constant_eq(s.as_bytes(), want.as_bytes()))
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Delivery {
    Done,
    /// Try again after this many seconds.
    RetryIn(u32),
    Dropped,
}

/// One delivery attempt of an outbox event.
pub async fn deliver<H: Host>(h: &H, event_id: &str) -> ApiResult<Delivery> {
    let Some(row) = store::one(h, "SELECT * FROM webhook_outbox WHERE event_id = ?1", params![event_id]).await? else {
        return Ok(Delivery::Dropped);
    };
    if row.opt_i("delivered_at").is_some() {
        return Ok(Delivery::Done);
    }
    if row.opt_i("dropped_at").is_some() {
        return Ok(Delivery::Dropped);
    }
    let now = h.now_ms();
    if now - row.i("created_at") > MAX_AGE_MS {
        h.run("UPDATE webhook_outbox SET dropped_at = ?2 WHERE event_id = ?1", params![event_id, now]).await?;
        return Ok(Delivery::Dropped);
    }
    let attempts = row.i("attempts");
    let retry = RETRY_S.get(attempts as usize).copied().unwrap_or(RETRY_LATER_S);
    let settings = h.settings();
    let (Some(url), false) = (settings.webhook_url.clone(), settings.webhook_secrets.is_empty()) else {
        h.run(
            "UPDATE webhook_outbox SET attempts = attempts + 1, last_error = 'no webhook URL or secret configured' WHERE event_id = ?1",
            params![event_id],
        )
        .await?;
        return Ok(Delivery::RetryIn(retry));
    };
    let body = row.s("body").into_bytes();
    let headers = vec![
        ("content-type".to_string(), "application/json".to_string()),
        ("x-plasmatrack-event".to_string(), row.s("type")),
        ("x-plasmatrack-event-id".to_string(), event_id.to_string()),
        ("x-plasmatrack-signature".to_string(), signature(&settings.webhook_secrets, now / 1000, &body)),
    ];
    let outcome = h.http_post(&url, headers, body).await;
    match outcome {
        Ok(status) if (200..300).contains(&status) => {
            h.run("UPDATE webhook_outbox SET attempts = attempts + 1, delivered_at = ?2 WHERE event_id = ?1", params![event_id, now])
                .await?;
            Ok(Delivery::Done)
        }
        other => {
            let error = match other {
                Ok(status) => format!("HTTP {status}"),
                Err(e) => e.0,
            };
            h.run(
                "UPDATE webhook_outbox SET attempts = attempts + 1, last_error = ?2 WHERE event_id = ?1",
                params![event_id, error],
            )
            .await?;
            Ok(Delivery::RetryIn(retry))
        }
    }
}
```

```rs
mod common;

#[test]
fn upload_score_and_read_a_real_delivery() {

    assert_eq!(t.call(t.bot("GET", "/api/v1/public/ats/leaderboard?division=singleplayer")).body_json()["total"], 0);

    // A valid result emits job.scored; delivering it signs it for the bot.
    let ev = t.q("SELECT event_id, type FROM webhook_outbox");

    assert_eq!(ev[0]["type"], "job.scored");
    let id = ev[0]["event_id"].as_str().unwrap();

    let posts = t.posts.borrow();

    assert_eq!(url, "https://bot.example/webhooks/plasmatrack");
    let sig = &headers.iter().find(|(k, _)| k == "x-plasmatrack-signature").unwrap().1;
    assert!(webhooks::verify(WEBHOOK_SECRET, sig, body, t.now.get() / 1000));
    assert!(!webhooks::verify("other", sig, body, t.now.get() / 1000));
    let b: Value = serde_json::from_slice(body).unwrap();
    assert_eq!((b["type"].as_str(), b["data"]["job_id"].as_str(), b["data"]["by"]["kind"].as_str()), (Some("job.scored"), Some(job_id.as_str()), Some("rules")));
}

/// A HaulMP job uploaded the way the client does (module lists redacted to
/// `mod_matches`): labelled `haulmp`, and discarded once the player is in the
/// Singleplayer Division, because the sample config says so for HaulMP.
#[test]
fn haulmp_jobs_are_labelled_and_left_out_of_the_singleplayer_division() {
    let t = TestHost::new();
    publish(&t);
    let token = link(&t);
    upload(&t, &token, &fixture("ets2-haulmp-ferry-three-sessions.jsonl.gz"), 400);
    assert_eq!(score(&t, Game::Ets2).jobs_stored, 1);
    let job_id = t.q("SELECT job_id FROM jobs")[0]["job_id"].as_str().unwrap().to_string();

    let j = t.call(t.bot("GET", &path)).body_json();

    // The same job by a player in the division since before it: discarded.
    let other = "223456789012345678";
    let token = link_other(&t, other, "Division Driver");
    let r = t.call(t.admin("PATCH", &format!("/api/v1/admin/players/{other}")).with_json(&json!({"singleplayer_division": true, "reason": "Joins the division"})));
    assert_eq!(r.status, 200, "{}", r.body_json());
    t.q(&format!("UPDATE users SET division_changed_at = 0 WHERE discord_user_id = '{other}'"));
    upload(&t, &token, &fixture("ets2-haulmp-ferry-three-sessions.jsonl.gz"), 400);
    let uid = t.q(&format!("SELECT user_id FROM users WHERE discord_user_id = '{other}'"))[0]["user_id"].as_str().unwrap().to_string();
    assert_eq!(block_on(t.scorer(&uid, Game::Ets2).process(&t)).unwrap().jobs_stored, 1);
    let job_id = t.q(&format!("SELECT job_id FROM jobs WHERE user_id = '{uid}'"))[0]["job_id"].as_str().unwrap().to_string();
    let j = t.call(t.bot("GET", &format!("/api/v1/public/jobs/{}", job_id.to_lowercase()))).body_json();
    assert_eq!((j["outcome"].as_str(), j["points"].as_f64()), (Some("discarded"), Some(0.0)), "{j}");
    assert_eq!(
        j["public_notes"],
        json!([{"code": "discarded_singleplayer_division", "text": "Discarded: a HaulMP job by a Singleplayer Division player."}])
    );
    let a = t.call(t.admin("GET", &format!("/api/v1/admin/jobs/{job_id}"))).body_json();
    let reason = a["reasons"].as_array().unwrap().iter().find(|r| r["code"] == "singleplayer_division_multiplayer_mod").cloned();
    assert_eq!(reason.map(|r| r["details"].clone()), Some(json!({"kind": "haulmp", "name": "HaulMP"})), "{a}");
}

#[test]
fn moderators_decide_with_etags_and_idempotency() {
    let t = TestHost::new();
    let job_id = chicago(&t);
    let path = format!("/api/v1/admin/jobs/{job_id}");
    let d = t.call(t.admin("GET", &path)).body_json();
    let etag = d["etag"].as_str().unwrap().to_string();
    assert_eq!(d["start_kind"], "tracked");
    assert_eq!(d["integrity"]["manifest_result"], "ok", "{}", d["integrity"]);
    assert!(d["timeline"].as_array().unwrap().iter().any(|e| e["event"] == "delivered"));

    // Reject, with the etag; the same key again replays; a new body conflicts.
    let reject = |key: &str, body: Value| t.call(t.bot("POST", &format!("{path}/reject")).with_header("x-plasmatrack-actor", ADMIN).with_header("idempotency-key", key).with_json(&body));
    let r = reject("dec-1", json!({"reason": "Testing a rejection", "expected_etag": etag}));
    assert_eq!(r.status, 200, "{}", r.body_json());
    assert_eq!(r.body_json()["outcome"], "rejected");
    assert_eq!(r.body_json()["points"], 0.0);
    assert_eq!(reject("dec-1", json!({"reason": "Testing a rejection", "expected_etag": etag})).body_json(), r.body_json());
    assert_eq!(reject("dec-1", json!({"reason": "Something else"})).body_json()["error"]["code"], "idempotency_mismatch");
    // The old etag is stale now.
    let r = t.call(t.admin("POST", &format!("{path}/approve")).with_json(&json!({"reason": "Fine after all", "expected_etag": etag})));
    assert_eq!((r.status, r.body_json()["error"]["code"].as_str()), (409, Some("conflict")));
    let r = t.call(t.admin("POST", &format!("{path}/approve")).with_json(&json!({"reason": "Fine after all"})));
    assert_eq!(r.body_json()["outcome"], "approved");
    assert_eq!(r.body_json()["points"], 3.6);
    let r = t.call(t.admin("POST", &format!("{path}/restore")).with_json(&json!({"reason": "Not voided"})));
    assert_eq!((r.status, r.body_json()["error"]["code"].as_str()), (409, Some("invalid_transition")));
    t.advance(1);
    let r = t.call(t.admin("POST", &format!("{path}/void")).with_json(&json!({"reason": "Void it"})));
    assert_eq!(r.body_json()["outcome"], "voided");
    t.advance(1);
    let r = t.call(t.admin("POST", &format!("{path}/restore")).with_json(&json!({"reason": "Bring it back"})));
    assert_eq!(r.body_json()["outcome"], "approved", "restore returns the outcome before the void");

    // Decisions stick through a recalculation.
    t.advance(1);
    let r = t.call(t.admin("POST", &format!("{path}/recalculate")).with_json(&json!({"reason": "Check stickiness"})));
    assert_eq!(r.body_json()["after"]["outcome"], "approved", "{}", r.body_json());

    // Missing reason and missing idempotency key.
    let r = t.call(t.admin("POST", &format!("{path}/void")).with_json(&json!({})));
    assert_eq!(r.body_json()["error"]["details"]["fields"]["reason"], "required");
    let r = t.call(t.bot("POST", &format!("{path}/void")).with_header("x-plasmatrack-actor", ADMIN).with_json(&json!({"reason": "abc"})));
    assert_eq!(r.status, 400);

    // The audit log has every decision, newest first.
    let a = t.call(t.admin("GET", &format!("/api/v1/admin/audit?job_id={job_id}"))).body_json();
    let actions: Vec<&str> = a["items"].as_array().unwrap().iter().map(|i| i["action"].as_str().unwrap()).collect();
    assert_eq!(actions, ["job.recalculate", "job.restore", "job.void", "job.approve", "job.reject"]);
    assert_eq!(a["items"][0]["actor"]["discord_user_id"], ADMIN);
}

#[test]
fn auth_is_enforced() {
    let t = TestHost::new();
    let r = t.call(Request::new("GET", "/api/v1/admin/review-queue"));
    assert_eq!(r.status, 401);
    let read = |m: &str, p: &str| Request::new(m, p).with_header("authorization", &format!("Bearer {READ_TOKEN}"));
    assert_eq!(t.call(read("GET", "/api/v1/admin/review-queue").with_header("x-plasmatrack-actor", ADMIN)).status, 403);
    assert_eq!(t.call(read("POST", &format!("/api/v1/players/{PLAYER}/token")).with_header("idempotency-key", "x")).status, 403);
    let r = t.call(t.bot("GET", "/api/v1/admin/review-queue").with_header("x-plasmatrack-actor", "555"));
    assert_eq!(r.status, 403, "not an admin");
    assert_eq!(t.call(t.admin("GET", "/api/v1/admin/review-queue")).status, 200, "a bootstrap admin");
    // A player token never reads the bot API, and the bot token never uploads.
    let token = link(&t);
    let r = t.call(Request::new("GET", "/api/v1/admin/review-queue").with_header("authorization", &format!("Bearer {token}")));
    assert_eq!(r.status, 401);
    let r = t.call(Request::new("POST", "/api/v1/chunks").with_header("authorization", &format!("Bearer {BOT_TOKEN}")));
    assert_eq!(r.status, 401);
    // A revoked token stops uploads.
    let r = t.call(t.bot("DELETE", &format!("/api/v1/players/{PLAYER}/token")).with_header("idempotency-key", "rv"));
    assert_eq!(r.status, 200);
    let r = t.call(Request::new("POST", "/api/v1/chunks").with_header("authorization", &format!("Bearer {token}")));
    assert_eq!(r.status, 401);
}
```
